home_pitcher_note: Blanton, the subject of trade rumors for much of the winter, will be making the first Opening Day start of his career. He struggled against the Red Sox in 2007, going 0-1 with a 4.66 ERA (10 earned runs over 19 1/3 inning) in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: What better way for Dice-K to kick off his second season with the Sox than pitching Opening Day at Tokyo Dome? Dice-K is nothing short of a legend in Japan, and the baseball-crazed nation is enthused to see him pitch.

home_pitcher_note: A tantalizing talent that most baseball insiders think would contend for a Cy Young Award if he could avoid the injury bug that's limited him to 32 starts over the past three seasons, Harden has enjoyed a healthy spring this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is looking to make the leap from promising young pitcher to dependable starter. Whereas last year when he was trying to come back from cancer, he has been able to focus exclusively on pitching this spring.

home_pitcher_note: In Oakland's season opener against the Red Sox in Japan, Blanton cruised through the first five innings before Boston broke through with three runs, two coming on a two-out double by Manny Ramirez.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching in his native country, Matsuzaka labored in his Opening Day start against the A's at the Tokyo Dome, walking five and throwing 95 pitches over five innings. He minimized the damage, giving up just two hits and two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Harden, who was limited to seven appearances (four starts) by a variety of arm injuries in 2007, powered his way through the vaunted Red Sox lineup in Tokyo on the way to six innings of three-hit work with nine strikeouts and three walks.
away_pitcher_note: Lester didn't get off to the start he was looking for, being touched up for five hits and four runs on March 26 in Tokyo against the Oakland Athletics. The left-hander has a chance for immediate redemption, as he again faces the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer, who made three starts for the A's late in the 2003 season but was used exclusively in relief during the following four seasons, has transitioned back to the starting role he prefers this spring after recovering from hip surgery that ended his 2007 season in May. Prior to his big league debut in 2003, Duchscherer made 23 starts at Triple-A Sacramento and went 14-2 with a 3.25 ERA to claim Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Year honors. An All-Star setup man for the A's in 2005, Duchscherer threw mostly cutters out of the bullpen, but he'll be using his full arsenal (two-seamer, four-seamer, curveball, changeup) as a starter.
away_pitcher_note: Unfortunately, Byrd's 2007 season will best be remembered for his admitted use of human growth hormone, which he said he used under doctor's supervision to treat a medical condition. MLB hasn't said whether Byrd will face a suspension for that HGH use, so he'll take the ball for the opener of a three-game set at McAfee Coliseum, where he is 1-2 with a 5.26 ERA in five career starts. The veteran Byrd was a 15-game winner in '07, but he'd still like to improve his performance against left-handed hitters. He certainly doesn't have to improve his control after leading the AL with 1.31 walks issued per nine innings pitched last year.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland, 24, was part of the six-player package that Oakland received from the Diamondbacks in the deal that sent ace Dan Haren to Arizona. He entered Spring Training with only 41 games of experience at the big league level.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians will keep Sabathia pitching on his fifth day after his uneven outing on Opening Day start against the White Sox, pushing fifth starter Cliff Lee back a day. Sabathia, though, will get an extra day of rest twice in the month of April because of the off-days built into the Tribe�s schedule. That should ease the burden on his arm after he logged 256 1/3 innings last year. Sabathia always seems to struggle in hometown Oakland. He is 1-3 with a 7.17 ERA in seven starts in McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton faced the Red Sox in his first two starts of the season and pitched well enough to win in both of them. After tossing five shutout innings in Oakland's opener, he got a couple of tough breaks before being chased with two out during Boston's three-run sixth and didn't factor in the decision. A week later, he held the Red Sox to two runs on seven hits over six innings but got only one run of support on the way to the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Look who?s back. Lee has reclaimed his old spot in the rotation after a truly disastrous 2007 in which he strained his abdominal muscle, struggled upon his return and was demoted to Triple-A Buffalo at the end of July. He came into spring camp in good shape and hungry to win his job back, and he did just that.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett was sharp in his 2008 debut, fashioning six strong innings in a win over the Yankees on Wednesday. The hard-throwing right-hander allowed two runs on five hits with three strikeouts and one walk in the 93-pitch outing. Burnett mixed a handful of changeups -- a pitch he worked extensively on this spring. In his career against the A's, Burnett is 1-1 with a 2.18 ERA in three starts. Burnett is 12-5 with a 3.26 ERA in 22 career outings at Rogers Centre.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin gets the start here as Rich Harden, originally scheduled to make this start, gets pushed back a day. This will Gaudin's first start of 2008. The right-hander went 11-13 with a 4.42 ERA in 34 starts for the A's in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Battling the remnants of the flu, McGowan turned in a strong performance against the formidable Yankee offense on Thursday. The right-hander allowed two runs on four hits over six innings for a no-decision. He struck out four and walked three in the 99-pitch outing. In his career against Oakland, McGowan is 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA and 17 strikeouts over 18 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Oakland purchased Greg Smith's contract from Triple-A Sacramento on Tuesday and will make a corresponding roster move Wednesday afternoon to add him to the roster. The 24-year-old was scheduled to arrive in Toronto late on Tuesday night and is expected to be named the starter for Wednesday night's affair against the Jays. Smith, one of the players acquired in the Dan Haren trade during the offseason, allowed two runs on six hits in his first Minor League start of '08. This will be his Major League debut.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum is coming off a strong performance in Friday's home opener against the Red Sox. The 26-year-old right-hander tossed seven solid innings allowing three runs on three hits. He also struck eight while walking one. In 33 career games at Rogers Centre, Marcum is 9-4 with a 4.47 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland was brilliant in his first outing of the season Saturday against the Indians at McAfee Coliseum. He silenced the Tribe's bats, allowing just one run on six hits in seven innings. In addition, the lefty struck out a career-high tying seven batters while issuing one walk. Eveland had pinpoint control and mixed in a solid slider and breaking pitch to keep the Indians hitters off-balance. Eveland has never faced the Blue Jays in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia's struggles in his hometown of Oakland continued Saturday. He lasted just 5 1/3 innings against the A's, surrendering four runs on six hits with four walks and two strikeouts. It was an uphill battle for Sabathia all afternoon, as he struggled to get ahead in the count. He hopes to have better luck in his other "home" at Progressive Field, as the reigning Cy Young Award winner has been slow to get into the flow of the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton dominated for six innings against the Indians on Sunday at McAfee Coliseum, but once again, he came away with a loss. Blanton, who went 6 2/3 innings, allowing just two runs on seven hits while striking out two, issued four walks in the game, including one with the bases loaded in the seventh. The righty used a heavy fastball and solid breaking pitch to keep the Indians' hitters at bay. In seven career starts against the Jays, Blanton is 4-2 with a 3.12 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona had some rare control problems in his start in Anaheim on Monday, yet he still came out virtually unscathed. In six innings of work, all he allowed was an unearned run on four hits. But he also walked five batters, including three with two outs in the fifth. Carmona is 2-1 with a 5.73 ERA in five career appearances against the A?s, including a 2-1 record and 7.71 ERA in three starts against them last season.
away_pitcher_note: This start originally belonged to right-hander Rich Harden, but he was scratched after being placed on the 15-day disabled list with a mild subscapularis strain in his right shoulder. The leading candidate to take Harden`s place is long reliever Lenny Dinardo. The 28-year-old left-hander made 20 starts for the A`s last season, going 7-8 with a 4.93 ERA. Dinardo has surrendered two runs on four hits while walking one in one third of an inning so far this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his return to the Tribe rotation on April 6 in Oakland, Lee looked much more like the 18-game winner he was in '05 than the demoted disaster he was in '07. Lee was solid for 6 2/3 innings, allowing just an unearned run on four hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He got ahead with his fastball and began working his changeup into the mix more often as the game wore on. If Lee can keep up that type of performance this season, the Indians' rotation looks even more potent and dangerous than previously thought.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin made his season debut in his last outing against the Blue Jays. The 25-year-old righty started the season in the Minor Leagues rehabbing from offseason hip surgery. The results were mixed in his start against Toronto. Gaudin allowed six runs -- five earned -- on eight hits while striking out three over four innings of work. Not the best of pitching lines but all of the earned-run damage came on home runs to Toronto center fielder Vernon Wells and second baseman Aaron Hill. Without those two mistake pitches that were left up in the zone, Gaudin's night would have gone a lot smoother. Gaudin is 2-1 with a 5.47 ERA in nine career outings against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle gained a form of redemption Sunday night, after getting pummeled for seven runs on seven hits over 1 2/3 innings during his Opening Day start in Cleveland on Monday. Against the Tigers, Buehrle yielded two runs on seven hits over seven innings, walking two and striking out one. Buehrle induced double-play grounders in the fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh innings in order to stem the Tigers� damage. Due to Tuesday�s off-day and Thursday�s rainout, Buehrle will have seven days in between starts. He was pushed back to face Oakland because of their left-handed laden lineup. Buehrle has a 3-9 record with a 3.86 ERA lifetime against the A�s, but most of that trouble has come in Oakland, where he is 0-6.
away_pitcher_note: Smith made his much-anticipated Major League debut in his last outing against the Blue Jays. The 24-year-old lefty, who was acquired as part of an offseason trade that sent No.1 starter Dan Haren to the Diamondbacks, survived a rough first inning en route to allowing three runs on two hits while striking out five. Smith did struggle with his control, though, surrendering five walks over six innings of work. A spot in Oakland's starting rotation was created for Smith when right-hander Justin Duchscherer was placed on the 15-day disabled list with a strained right biceps.

home_pitcher_note: The strong showing made by the southpaw during his first start of the year in Cleveland was balanced out by the shellacking administered by the Twins during Wednesday?s loss at U.S. Cellular Field. Danks allowed seven runs on seven hits over 2 1/3 innings, struggling with his control from the outset. He walked three and struck out two, exiting after walking Craig Monroe with the bases loaded in the third. Danks won his only previous career start against Oakland, allowing one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland continued to impress the Oakland brain trust with an impressive outing in his last start against the Blue Jays. Making just his second start with the Athletics, Eveland tossed 6 1/3 shutout innings. The 24-year-old surrendered just three hits while striking out six batters and threw 53 of his 95 pitches for strikes. Eveland credited the majority of his success against Toronto to establishing his fastball and curveball combination early in the game before mixing in a slider and changeup to keep the Jays hitters off-balance.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton picked up his first win of the season against the Indians, allowing five runs and eight hits in 7 2/3 innings. The right-hander cruised through the first seven innings, giving up only Jhonny Peralta's home run in the second. Staked to an early 9-1 lead, Blanton still went after the Indians' hitters and let his defense do the work.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander surrendered his first earned runs of the season in his last start, which ended a 17-inning streak, but he battled his tail off against the Angels, throwing 117 pitches over 6 2/3 innings. The two-seam fastball has been Felix's best pitch, locating it down and in to right-handed hitters. He also is pitching inside more this season, and it is keeping hitters honest.

home_pitcher_note: DiNardo picked up his first win of the season Saturday against the Indians. Starting in place of the injured Rich Harden, the left-hander allowed two runs and six hits in five innings. He struck out three and didn't walk a batter. DiNardo was removed after allowing two singles to start the sixth. He threw 73 pitches and was around the strike zone in his first start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is a contact pitcher, and in his last start Saturday against the Angels he was contacted. The Angels knocked out 11 hits in Silva's eight innings to score three runs. But a stout defense behind him -- turning three double plays -- prevented any more Angels rallies. Silva went eight innings, throwing 98 pitches, to save the bullpen and pick up his second victory for his new team. He is 3-2 with a 3.12 ERA in nine career starts against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start of the season against the Indians on Sunday, Gaudin allowed three runs and four hits over six innings in a losing effort. He walked four and struck out four. Gaudin started the season on the disabled list after offseason hip surgery. Gaudin is building up his pitch count. He threw 77 pitches in his first start against the Blue Jays and 108 against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister is coming off a complete-game 5-1 victory over the Twins. He allowed one unearned run and three singles, while walking one, striking out three and hitting a batter. He thew 112 pitches, 73 for strikes. In three starts, Bannister has yielded just 10 hits and two earned runs in 21 innings, while striking out 13 and walking five. He also owns victories this season over the Tigers and Yankees. Bannister was 1-0 with a 2.40 ERA in two starts last season against the Athletics, including a complete-game on Aug. 17 in which he allowed two runs on four hits at Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Smith, a 24-year-old acquired in the eight-player deal that sent ace Dan Haren to the Diamondbacks in December, was brilliant in his second start with Oakland and picked up his first Major League win. After a strong debut and a no-decision against the Blue Jays, Smith silenced the powerful White Sox five days later by scattering six hits over seven innings of one-run work. In addition to keeping Chicago off-balance with a excellent changeup, Smith, who walked one, got himself two outs on the bases with a deft pickoff move.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke has gone seven, eight and nine innings in running his record to 3-0 in three starts. He went the distance last Monday night at Seattle, giving up one run and his ERA actually went up from 0.60. He needed just 107 pitches to bamboozle the Mariners, getting 16 outs via ground balls. Greinke can ratchet up mid-90s fastballs with regularity and has been using his slider and offspeed pitches with precision. Since last Aug. 7, he?s given up just nine earned runs in 65 innings for a 1.25 ERA, best among all Major League pitchers with at least 50 innings in that period.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland, who was acquired from the Diamondbacks in December and sailed through Spring Training and his first two starts of the regular season, finally had his first rough outing in an Oakland uniform on Tuesday, allowing four runs (three earned) over 4 2/3 innings against the White Sox in Chicago. Command was the biggest problem for Eveland, who consistently fell behind batters and allowed five hits while walking three and hitting two. He also threw a wild pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar is being recalled from Triple-A Omaha to make his first start this season, taking the spot vacated when John Bale (left shoulder fatigue) went on the disabled list. Hochevar was 1-1 with a 2.60 ERA in three starts for Omaha. He made a strong bid for a rotation spot during Spring Training when he notched a 2.25 ERA in three Cactus League games, but he lost out to Bale and Brett Tomko.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has pitched quite a bit better than his numbers suggest, and his most recent outing was a good example of such. Although he gave up three runs in the first inning and was peppered for a career-high-tying 12 hits, he only gave up one run after the first, didn't issue any walks and managed to get through eight innings on 101 pitches. In his first season as Oakland's No. 1 starter, Blanton hasn't received much in the way of offensive support with the exception of a nine-run largesse on April 11. In Blanton's other four starts, he's been backed by a total of six runs.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first three starts, Hernandez was the recipient of a no-decision against the Rays in his most recent outing. The pitcher gave up five runs (three earned) with four of them courtesy of three home runs. One thing that Hernandez did improve on was getting the ball to catcher Joe Mauer faster in pitch-out situations. Mauer was able to catch two Rays on attempted steals and shut down Tampa Bay�s running game. During Spring Training, Hernandez had problems doing that. He's 2-2 with a 4.76 ERA in four career starts against the A's in his career, with all of the previous meetings occurring in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Brought off the disabled list about a week earlier than expected in the wake of injuries to A's starters Rich Harden and Justin Duchscherer, Gaudin, who had offseason surgery on his left hip and right foot -- on the same December day -- and made only one Spring Training appearance, was outstanding in his most recent outing. He stifled Kansas City with seven innings of four-hit work, allowing one earned run while striking out eight and walking one on 96 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Heading into the 2008 season, the Twins were looking to Bonser to help lead the starting staff as one of their more experienced starters. But Bonser hasn't exactly lived up to the billing. In his fourth start of the season, Bonser had problems commanding the strike zone. Just 46 of Bonser's 72 pitches were for strikes and the pitcher admittedly didn't have his best stuff.

home_pitcher_note: After two nice starts, Smith stumbled a little bit, allowing four runs (three earned) against the Kansas City Royals on Saturday. He gave up a three-run homer in the first inning and a solo shot in the second. Over his final 13 batters, though, he struck out four, and gave up two singles. He?ll be making his third road start of the season against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Liriano had problems commanding the strike zone. After struggling to locate his fastball against the Royals last Sunday, Liriano had similar issues when he faced the Indians on Friday night. The left-hander walked a total of five batters in his outing while allowing three runs on four hits. Despite the problems with his fastball, Liriano's dominant slider has appeared to be getting back into form.

home_pitcher_note: The 37-year-old right-hander pitched one of his best games with Seattle in his last outing, holding the Angels scoreless over 7 2/3 innings in a game the Mariners had to win to avoid being swept. Batista had great command of his fastball, moving it in and out, up and down and recording eight strikeouts. He also walked only one. Six of the eight hits he allowed came with two outs.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland rebounded from a loss with another fine outing against the Royals in which he allowed one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings. He walked four and struck out three. Eveland, one of the key players involved in the trade that sent Dan Haren to the D-backs, never faced more than four batters in an inning, with the only run (as a result of a walk) scoring on a double play. He retired 10 of 11 before running into some trouble in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Bedard's first start in 18 days, a delay caused by time spent on the disabled list with a sore left hip. He had his second start pushed back, finally working six innings in a 6-5 win over Tampa Bay on April 8. His third start was again pushed back until the club finally decided to place him on the DL. He threw a couple bullpens this week without discomfort. He is 1-3 with a 4.12 ERA in seven appearances against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer had thrown five shutout innings against the Indians on April 4 when he was lifted from his first start of the season because of a strain in his right biceps. Duchscherer ended up getting the win for his four-hit work, but he also ended up on the disabled list. He was cleared to resume throwing withing a few days, and he threw 48 pitches in a rehab start at Triple-A Sacramento on Monday. A converted reliever, Duchscherer likely will be working with a pitch limit of between 70-85 if he's activated to face the M's.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez, coming off his complete-game victory April 16 against Oakland, was tough again Tuesday against the Orioles. He allowed just two runs in his seven innings but left with the score tied at 2-2. Now he faces the A's again, carrying in a five-game win streak and an overall 6-2 record against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is a workhorse, having pitched into the sixth inning in each of his six starts and past the sixth four times, but he's allowed at least seven hits each time out, and he's gotten more than two runs of support only twice. In his start at home against the Twins Tuesday, Blanton stuck around for 7 2/3 innings, but he gave up a game-tying homer to Craig Monroe in the seventh, and a bloop single off reliever Alan Embree allowed Minnesota to score the go-ahead run in the eighth and pin Blanton with the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Searching for a consistent groove, Garland was rolling along in good fashion before leaving a pitch inside to David Ortiz for a two-run homer in Fenway Park. He departed with a 5-4 lead, having yielded four earned runs on eight hits in six innings, and gained credit for the win. Garland has struggled against the A's in his career, going 3-8 with a 4.58 ERA in 13 outings. He's 1-1 with a 7.15 ERA in two home starts for the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin, who had surgery on his left hip and right foot on the same day in December and missed most of Spring Training, ripped through the Minnesota lineup in short order on Wednesday in his fourth start of the season. He allowed four singles without a walk and struck out four, throwing 83 pitches before leaving after the seventh. Gaudin recently stopped bringing his hands over his head to start his windup in an effort to maintain eye contact with his target, and since making the change, he's allowed one earned run on eight hits while striking out 12 and walking one over 14 innings to pick up his first two wins.

home_pitcher_note: He wasn't on top of his game, but Saunders did a terrific job of minimizing damage in holding the Red Sox to three earned runs across six innings on seven hits and three walks. With his four-seam fastball in the 92-94 mph range and his sinker effective in big situations, he struck out three hitters and got 11 outs on the ground. Saunders is 2-1 with a 5.54 ERA in five career outings against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: One of the youngsters acquired in the offseason trade that sent Dan Haren to the Diamondbacks, Smith has made four starts since being called up from Triple-A Sacramento earlier this month, and he's yet to allow more than three earned runs in an assignment. In his most recent outing, Thursday against the visiting Twins, he allowed a leadoff home run but held Minnesota to two runs on seven hits over seven innings, walking one and striking out three. It marked the third time that Smith has issued less than two walks, and he's worked at least six innings in all but one start.

home_pitcher_note: Showing again that he's intent on conquering his old road demons, Santana delivered his first effective outing at Comerica Park on Friday night. He held the torrid Tigers to three earned runs on six hits and two walks in 6 1/3 innings. Using his mid-90s fastball and sharp-breaking slider, he struck out four hitters. He's 3-0 with a 3.72 road ERA after going 1-10 with an 8.38 ERA on the road last season. Santana has dominated the A's, going 7-1 with a 1.38 ERA in 10 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: More of the same for Eveland through his first five innings Friday against Seattle, allowing one run and four hits. It appeared to be like his previous outing against Kansas City, when he allowed one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings for a 7-1 victory. But the lefty got nicked in the sixth, allowing a pair of singles and issuing a walk before leaving the bases loaded. He threw 98 pitches. This will be his first career shot at the rival Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Highly-touted right-handed pitching prospect Nick Adenhart will make his Major League debut Thursday night against the Oakland A's. Adenhart was dominating at Triple-A Salt Lake. The 21-year old is 4-0 with a 0.87 ERA in five starts spanning 31 innings. He has struck out 19 and walked 15 in 31 innings. He will be pitching on three days' rest with a light bullpen session in between and manager Mike Scioscia said he will probably keep Adenhart on a conservative leash.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer looked remarkably sharp Saturday in his five-inning outing against Seattle. It was his first start in 20 days after coming off the disabled list with a strained right biceps. He went five innings, allowing six hits and two fairly cheap runs. He threw an efficient 73 pitches. This will be his first start against the Angels -- after 22 relief appearances. Curiously, he has never lost the the Angels, going 5-0 with a 1.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has been a tough-luck pitcher all year, and it looked like that way in his last start Sunday against Seattle. He was behind 2-0 and Felix Hernandez was pitching a gem. But Hernandez lost it in the eighth, giving up four runs. Blanton kept his team in the game and was rewarded with the victory, just his second in six decisions. He leads off the Texas series at home. He was 2-0 with a 4.12 in two starts against the Rangers last season.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is making his first start in Oakland since Sept. 16, when he faced just two batters and was ejected after hitting outfielder Nick Swisher with a pitch. He is 3-1 with a 4.66 ERA in nine career games against the Athletics, including a 1-1 record with a 7.11 ERA in six appearances in Oakland. Padilla is 2-1 with a 4.70 ERA in four starts on the road this year and 11-13 with a 5.55 ERA in 33 road starts since the beginning of the 2006 season.

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin, who was rushed off the disabled list in the wake of injuries to fellow starters Rich Harden and Justin Duchscherer, struggled in his first two starts of the season but has been lights-out as of late. In his most recent outing, Monday at Anaheim, he won his third consecutive start by holding the Halos to give hits and two walks while striking out four over six innings. Gaudin, whose velocity was down in his first two outings, is back to working in the 90-93 mph range, and his sinker is every bit as good as it was during the first half of 2007, when he went 8-3 with a 2.88 ERA before the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Murray was pulled after just one inning of his Wednesday start for Triple-A Oklahoma when it became apparent he would be summoned for this start. Murray was 2-0 with a 4.00 ERA and one complete game through his first five starts for the RedHawks this year. The left-hander made 14 appearances in the big leagues last year (including two starts), spanning 28 innings. He was 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA and held opposing hitters to a .238 average. He has pitched three times in relief against Oakland, going 1-1 with a 7.11 ERA. The Athletics put up five runs on eight hits (three home runs) in 6 1/3 innings against Murray.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday in Anaheim, Smith gave up two runs on three hits and three walks while striking out four over seven innings for his fourth quality start in five assignments this year. The A's offense was stifled by the Halos, pinning Smith with his first big league loss in his first complete game, but the rookie was again impressive, keeping the hosts off-balance with his high-80s fastball and an array of offspeed pitches. Smith has never faced the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman threw 69 pitches over four innings Tuesday against Kansas City in relief of the injured Jason Jennings. He will take over Jennings' spot in the rotation beginning with this game, which will mark his second Major League start. Feldman has made five career relief appearances against Oakland, posting a 0-0 record and 1.50 ERA. He has allowed the Athletics one run on two hits and nine walks over six career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Looking to win third consecutive start in Anaheim on Wednesday, Eveland has his roughest outing of the year. An aggressive pitcher who attacks hitters, Eveland cruised through the first inning before giving up two runs in the second and one in the third. Three consecutive hits with one out in the sixth chased him, and he was charged with six earned runs on seven hits and two walks while striking out five. Eveland, who has never faced Baltimore, has pitched into the sixth inning in five of his six starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Olson fared well in his season debut, pitching into the seventh inning and allowing just two earned runs -- one of which scored after he left the game. Olson, who joined the rotation in place of injured starter Adam Loewen, should have a slot as long as he continues to thrive. Last year, Olson finished third in the Triple-A International League in ERA (3.16) but struggled in his big league audition.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start off the disabled list, Duchscherer gave up one earned run on six hits and a walk while striking out six over five innings to beat the Angels in Anaheim. He left with a pitch count of 81, and were it not for a two-out dropped fly ball by left fielder Jack Cust that led to five unearned runs and 30 extra pitches for Duchscherer, Oakland's reliever-turned-starter probably would have gone much deeper into the game. Duchscherer is 1-0 with a 2.87 ERA in eight career appearances against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Burres pitched into the seventh inning of his most recent outing and has been Baltimore's most consistent starter this season. The southpaw is third on the team in strikeouts and has held opposing hitters to a .237 batting average. Burres, who served as swingman last season, finally appears to have nailed down a rotation slot.

home_pitcher_note: Luck has not been on Blanton's side this year, as was evident on Tuesday against the Rangers. He tossed seven strong innings, the fifth time he's gone at least seven this season, scattering seven hits and one walk. Oakland's four errors proved costly, however, as Blanton left the game behind 4-3 with all runs (two earned) attached to his name. Scheduled to make his Major League-leading ninth start of the season, Blanton was 0-2 with a 3.91 ERA against the Orioles last season, and he's 2-3 with a 3.98 ERA in five career starts against Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie snapped a 15-start winless drought in his last start, when he worked seven strong innings against the Angels. Guthrie had allowed three earned runs or less in 11 of his 15 starts during the skid. So far this season, the right-hander's shortest outing is five innings.

home_pitcher_note: This is probably Feldman's start but it could go to A.J. Murray. Both pitched well against the Athletics in Oakland. Feldman lost 3-1 on Sunday despite taking a shutout into the seventh inning. The Athletics scored three runs off him, and Feldman is now 0-1 with a 4.38 ERA in two starts this season. Murray, making his first start for the Rangers, beat the Athletics, 6-3, on Saturday, allowing three runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander struck out a career-high 10 in his last start, while allowing only one run in a three-hit, six-inning effort against Texas. Since making his Major League debut on April 9, Smith has not allowed more than three runs in any of his six starts and has gone at least five innings in each.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is 2-0 despite a 5.55 ERA in four starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington this season and is now 17-11 with a 5.10 ERA in 37 career starts. He is 3-3 with a 4.34 ERA in 10 career starts against Oakland. Frank Thomas has been particularly rough on him with 12 hits in 20 at-bats against him, including two home runs. That's a .600 average that is Thomas' highest against any pitcher with at least 20 at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: Following a rough outing in Anaheim, Eveland scattered three hits and four walks while pitching into the eighth without allowing a run in a 10-inning, 2-1 Oakland win over Baltimore in his seventh start of the year. The lefty threw 90 pitches while improving his home ERA to 0.92. He will look to conquer his struggles on the road, where he has a 4.98 ERA, against the Rangers. Eveland has never faced Texas in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson has won his last two starts for the Rangers, allowing just two runs on 13 hits in 15 innings. This will be his fourth start for the Rangers. He was signed midway through Spring Training and opened the season in Triple-A Oklahoma where he was 1-2 with a 3.47 ERA in five games. He is 3-3 with a 6.58 ERA in 13 games, including 10 starts, against the Athletics in his career.
away_pitcher_note: This will mark Harden's return to the Oakland rotation after spending the past month on the disabled list with a strain under his right shoulder blade. One of the game's most dominant pitchers when he's healthy, Harden, who throws a high-90s fastball and has a split-fingered pitch that occasionally knuckles, has been on the DL six times since the start of the 2005 season. In his final Minor League rehab start Tuesday, Harden struck out nine without a walk -- he hit three batters -- over six shutout innings of three-hit work for Class A Stockton against visiting Visalia. Harden is 5-2 with a 3.73 ERA in 11 career appearances against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd has had an up and down season, because he can't seem to consistently keep the ball in the park. He has been hammered for 10 home runs in the early going, including the three he served up in a loss to the Yankees in his last start on May 8. In that game, he had trouble getting the ball down and away, and he was burned for five runs on eight hits with no walks or strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer tossed a career-high-tying seven innings against the Orioles in his fourth start of the season and ninth of his career. The former setup man proved he belongs in the starting rotation, throwing seven effective innings while using only 85 pitches (56 for strikes) to limit Baltimore to two runs on four hits and two walks while striking out four. Duchscherer faced Cleveland just once last year, pitching a scoreless inning in a relief appearance. In his career, he is 0-2 with a 6.48 ERA against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: In a duel of Cy Young winners on Friday, Sabathia looked the part of a past winner. He displayed dominating stuff, dazzling Toronto with power and finesse. Sabathia was as sharp in his outing at Progressive Field as he's been at any other time this season. He fanned nine in beating Blue Jays ace Roy Halladay. In his next start, Sabathia will be taking on an Oakland team that has proved troublesome. During his Major League career, he's posted un-Cy Young-like numbers against the A's. He's 2-6 with an ERA over 6.00.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League-leading ninth start of the season, Blanton threw for 5 2/3 innings, scattering eight hits and three walks while allowing two runs and striking out three in a no-decision en route to the A's 10th-inning 6-5 win over the Orioles. It marked the fourth time of the year the pitcher allowed two runs or fewer. The right-hander compiled a 1-1 record with a 4.26 ERA against Cleveland last year, allowing nine runs on 21 hits -- three of them home runs -- while striking out 12 through 19 innings in three games vs. the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: If Laffey is trying to prove he belongs in the bigs for the long haul, he just needs to keep pitching as he has. Since returning to the Major Leagues to fill Jake Westbrook's spot, Laffey has been downright impressive. His latest outing might rank as his best ever. He threw strikes, pitched ahead in the count, went seven innings and gave up six hits in shutting out the Blue Jays. His performance, if it continues, will present a pleasant problem for manager Eric Wedge once Westbrook is ready to come off the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Smith, a rookie left-hander, lost his last start to Texas, but the A's are still 5-2 in his starts. He has gone at least six innings in six of his seven starts. The 24-year-old Smith can't get frustrated by a lack of run support; the A's have not scored a run for him in his last three starts. Smith's other concern is the first inning. He has allowed eight runs in the opening frame.

home_pitcher_note: The Braves have decided to bring Jurrjens back on short rest for the first time in his career. The 22-year-old rookie right-hander threw 69 pitches while allowing three runs in five innings against the Pirates on Monday afternoon. The only damage he incurred came courtesy of a fifth-inning, two-out, three-run double. He had won each of his previous three decisions and pitched into the sixth inning in each of his previous seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland had another solid start in Saturday's loss to the Rangers, allowing three earned runs in six innings. Eveland has pitched into the sixth inning in seven of his eight starts. He gave up a two-run home run to Milton Bradley on Saturday, but that matched his home runs allowed for the season. Eveland has allowed just two home runs in 47 2/3 innings this season, and seven homers in 111 2/3 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson had arguably his best outing of the season Monday, scattering two hits over seven innings to get the win against the Pirates, which snapped the Braves' seven-game road losing streak. Hudson didn't allow a run for the second time in three starts; he pitched a three-hit shutout on May 2 against the Reds. He has allowed just two extra-base hits in the past 23 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harden struggled in his first start since April 2, allowing five runs in 3 2/3 innings in the A's 12-6 victory over the Rangers. Harden, who had been on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder, was held to a 90-pitch count. He struggled with his control, allowing four walks and hitting a batter. Three of those runners scored. Harden's main goal is staying off the DL. His recent trip there was his sixth in the last four seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes believed he made the finest start of his young career on Tuesday night, when he allowed 11 hits and five earned runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Phillies. He wasn't alone in his assessment as Braves manager Bobby Cox and Chipper Jones indicated they'd never seen him any better. Their praise was result of the fact that he didn't issue a walk and threw first-pitch strikes to 27 of the 32 batters that he faced. Control has been the one issue that has troubled him early in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Indians in Cleveland his last time out, Duchscherer gave up a run on a two-out single in the first inning, but he retired the next 13 batters he faced on the way to 6 2/3 innings of four-hit work with two walks (one intentional) and six strikeouts while throwing a season-high 108 pitches. He took the loss, though, because the A's were blanked by Paul Byrd over 7 1/3 innings. Duchscherer, who spent two weeks on the disabled list with biceps tendinitis after leaving his first start of the season after five innings, has allowed a total of six earned runs in five starts since being activated. Both of Duchscherer's career outings against Atlanta have come in relief; he's pitched three innings, allowing three earned runs on five hits, including two homers.

home_pitcher_note: In his 10th start of the season, Blanton landed on the losing end of a pitching duel against Cleveland starter C.C. Sabathia. The A's pitcher threw seven innings, scattering two runs -- both solo home runs -- on four hits while striking out four and walking two in the 2-0 loss. It marked the fifth time this year the right-hander allowed two runs or fewer. Blanton was 1-1 with a 4.38 ERA against Tampa Bay last year, allowing six runs on 18 hits while striking out 11 in two starts versus the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a solid performance, the right-hander remains winless vs. the Yankees, yielding two runs over 7 1/3 innings and scattering six hits. Shields is now 3-1 with a 1.41 ERA at home, compared to his 1-2, 6.10 ERA on the road, and will look to better those numbers in Monday's start vs. the Athletics. The hurler will face Oakland for the first time this year -- he is 2-1 in three career starts vs. the A's, posting a 4.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Smith failed to complete the sixth inning for just the second time this year in his last start against Cleveland, giving up three runs on seven hits while walking three and striking out seven in 5 2/3 innings. The southpaw's early-inning troubles continued, as he allowed his ninth first-inning run. Lack of run support, however, also haunts Smith. The A's have only scored one run for him in his last four starts. The rookie has never faced the Rays in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The Rays ace lowered his ERA in a superb outing vs. the Yankees on May 15. The southpaw tossed six scoreless innings -- allowing just three hits -- and sealing the club's sixth series victory. Kazmir is at his best when he is locating his fastball, which makes his slider even more devastating for the opposition. In his past two starts, the reigning American League strikeout king has looked every bit the ace that the Rays recently signed to a three-year extension. He will try to replicate that success on Tuesday vs. Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland allowed just two hits in the first five innings on Friday against the Braves before running into trouble in the sixth. He was forced out with two out in the sixth after surrendering two runs. Eveland allowed six hits, walked three and struck out four in a no-decision. In the three starts prior to Friday, Eveland was 0-2 with a 4.42 ERA. He has walked a team-high 23 batters this season. Eveland has not won since April 25.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine pitched well against the Cardinals in his last outing, holding the birds to one run on eight hits while walking none and striking out four in a 3-1 Rays win. The right-hander is a master of deception employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Since making that adjustment he has been a lot more successful. Sonnanstine is 1-0 with a 3.60 ERA in one career start against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Harden baffled Atlanta on Saturday night, Braves manager Bobby Cox said Harden was "as good as advertised." Tim Hudson, who was teammates with Harden in Oakland, said his team saw firsthand how devastating Harden's stuff can be. Harden allowed one run on four hits in seven strong innings for the A's, who snapped a season-high four-game losing streak. Making just his second start since returning from the disabled list, Harden struck out eight and walked one. He is showing no ill effects from the strained right shoulder that landed him on the DL.
away_pitcher_note: After getting shelled at Minnesota, Wakefield made a nice recovery in his last start, surrendering six hits and three runs over 5 1/3 innings. Wakefield left in position to get the win, but the bullpen couldn't hang on, so he was left with a no-decision. In four May starts, Wakefield is 1-2 with a 4.70 ERA. Lifetime against Oakland, he is 9-5 with a 4.03 ERA. At McAfee Colisuem, Wakefield is 5-3 with a 5.47 ERA in 15 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer pitched five innings in his last start, allowing three runs on seven hits against Atlanta. The loss was his second straight and just the second time this year that he allowed more than two earned runs in a game.  Duchscherer walked two and struck out two. He is 2-0 with a 0.75 ERA in 18 relief appearances against Tampa Bay, striking out 20 in 24 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The ace is still trying to get into a sustained groove. Despite getting a win in his last start, Beckett didn't pitch all that well, giving up four home runs to the Brewers. In that outing, Beckett gave up six hits and six runs over seven innings. In four May starts, Beckett is 3-1 with a 5.20 ERA. Lifetime against Oakland, Beckett is 2-2 with a 5.55 ERA in four starts. At McAfee Colisuem, he is 1-1 with a 3.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his Major League-leading 11th start of the season, Blanton got the run support he's been looking for all year, thanks to a pair of homers by Frank Thomas and another by Emil Brown, but it wasn't enough for a win, as Blanton left the game with a no-decision in an eventual 5-4 Tampa Bay victory. Blanton threw six innings, surrendering four runs on six hits with five strikeouts. He posted an 0-1 record with a 4.66 ERA in three starts against Boston last year, allowing 10 runs on 21 hits with 10 strikeouts through 19 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: All the lefty did in his last start was throw a no-hitter, the 18th in Red Sox history. The gem came against the Royals, as Lester walked two and struck out nine while throwing 130 pitches. Lester has been solid in May, going 2-0 with a 2.04 ERA in four starts. Opponents are hitting .229 against Lester this season. This is his third start of 2008 against the Athletics, going 1-1 with a 3.38 ERA in the first two.

home_pitcher_note: Smith bounced back from his worst start of the season with one of his best against Tampa Bay. He avoided his previous first-inning struggles and pitched seven innings without allowing a run before being tagged with two runs in the eighth on a double that was initially ruled an error. Once 2-0 with a 2.88 ERA over his first four starts, Smith is now 2-4 with a 3.18 ERA and is still lacking offensive support. In his first five starts, he has been backed by a total of two runs. As a result, he hasn't won since April 24 and will look to change that in his first career start against Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: With a win over the Angels on Thursday, Burnett improved to 3-2 with a 3.48 ERA in five May starts. The right-hander carried a one-hit shutout into the fifth inning before running into some trouble. Burnett finished with three runs allowed on six hits with six strikouts and a pair of walks in six innings. Burnett has 31 strikeouts and nine walks over his past four starts. He is 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA in four career games against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Harden looked sharp in his third start since being activated from the DL on May 11, scattering just two runs on four hits with eight strikeouts through six innings in his third starting assignment against Boston this year. Harden, limited to seven games last year because of a strained right shoulder, did not face Toronto in the 2007 campaign. However, he will look to move past his previous woes against the Blue Jays -- a lifetime record of 0-3 with a 5.59 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Halladay turned in his Major League-leading fifth complete game of the season, spinning nine stellar innings in a win over the Royals. Halladay allowed one run on four hits with five strikeouts and no walks in the 104-pitch effort. For May, Halladay is 3-1 with a 2.87 ERA, 31 strikeouts and just three walks over 31 1/3 innings. He's now gone 22 straight innings without a non-intentional walk. In his career against the A's, Halladay is 4-4 with a 5.35 ERA in 11 games.

home_pitcher_note: Before Eveland took the mound in his last start against Tampa Bay, the A's had mustered just two or fewer runs six times in his nine previous starting assignments. Oakland forgot about those numbers, though, and gave Eveland a nine-run lead in the midst of a remarkable one-run, three-hit complete game performance. The win, his third at home, marked the first time Eveland went the distance. It's hard to top a performance like that, but Eveland will look to do just that in his second career start against the Blue Jays. On April 10, he didn't allow a run through 6 1/3 innings at Toronto, scattering three hits and three walks with six strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch dominated the Royals on Saturday, logging the first complete-game shutout of his young career. Litsch scattered seven hits and finished with three strikeouts and one walk over nine innings against Kansas City, which grounded into 14 outs against the right-hander. Litsch walked a batter in the ninth inning, ending a run of 38 straight innings without a walk, which established a new franchise record. In his career against the A's, Litsch is 0-1 with a 1.38 ERA in two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood was cleared to return off the disabled list after throwing 65 pitches in a simulated game at Progressive Field on Saturday. Millwood has been sidelined for two weeks with a strained right groin muscle. He is 1-1 with a 7.67 ERA in his last six starts. His last start was against the Athletics but had to come out in the first inning after injuring himself. He is 3-3 with a 4.29 ERA in 11 career starts against the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer tossed the best game of his career in his last start against the Red Sox, carrying a no-hitter into the seventh inning before David Ortiz broke it up with a one-out single. That was the only hit allowed by Duchscherer, though, and the second of only two baserunners on the night in a 3-0 combined one-hit shutout with closer Huston Street. After throwing 101 pitches, Duchscherer left the game after a career-high eight innings. This will be his first career start against Texas, a team against which he has a career 3-1 record as a relief pitcher. Duchscherer was 0-1 versus the Rangers last year, allowing three runs on two hits through just 2/3 of an inning.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson got his first loss of the year after allowing a season-high 12 hits in a mere five innings in Tampa Bay on Monday night. The right-hander walked three batters after allowing only one walk in his previous two outings, and will look to bounce back at home on Saturday. The veteran hurler faced Oakland once already this season, surrendering four first-inning runs before settling down to leave the game with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: In his Major League-tying 12th start of the season, Blanton picked up his first home victory in a 6-3 win over Boston while putting a stop to the longest home losing streak of his career at five. He walked a season-high-tying four batters but also struck out a season-high-tying seven in his three-run, six-hit, six-inning effort. This is the second time Blanton will face Texas this year. In his May 2 start at home against the Rangers, he allowed just two runs on seven hits through seven innings, but he took the tough-luck loss in a 4-3 game. Blanton is 6-2 with a 4.75 ERA in his career against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has pitched at least six innings in all six starts, but the Rangers are just 1-5 in those games. Feldman couldn't overcome one big hit, a three-run home run in his latest outing, a 5-2 loss to the Indians by Saturday. Prior to that start, the hurler also gave up five runs in six innings to the Twins, again with allowing a three-run homer. If Feldman can avoid the long ball vs. Oakland, the right-hander could finally pick up his second win of the season on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Smith snapped a four-game losing streak while pitching into the seventh inning and not allowing a run to the visiting Blue Jays in his last start. He gave up just six hits and one walk with three strikeouts as his teammates gave him three runs of support in a 3-1 A's win -- a far cry from the 0.57 runs of support per nine innings he had been averaging over his previous five starts. Smith has already faced Texas twice this season, going 0-1 with a 2.77 ERA. He went six innings both times, surrendering a combined five earned runs and nine hits with 14 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: In his sixth start of the season, his fourth since being reinstated from the disabled list May 11, Harden completed seven innings for just the second time this year, scattering five hits with no walks and five strikeouts while allowing just one run. He was part of a pitching dual against Toronto's Roy Halladay, though, and watched the A's suffer a 2-1 loss. It was his third career start in which he did not surrender a walk. Harden did not face Detroit last year, but is 3-1 with a 3.70 ERA in his career against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers pushed Rogers back a day so that he could pitch at McAfee Coliseum, where he's 25-4 over a 20-year career that included two years with the A's. He's coming off of his best performance of the season, even though it earned him no decision in the Tigers' 1-0, 12-inning loss to the Angels last Monday. Beyond his seven scoreless innings, he racked up 13 groundouts and showed he can still command a game when he commands the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: After pitching the best game of his career with a one-run complete game in his previous start, Eveland tossed his worst against the Blue Jays in allowing seven runs on 11 hits with two walks and three strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings -- his shortest outing of the season. With the loss, his ERA went from 2.90 to 3.66. Eveland will look to get back to form against a Detroit team he's never faced in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After struggling to find innings for Willis pitching out of the bullpen, manager Jim Leyland decided to slot six starters into a five-man rotation by working Willis in a piggy-back role with Armando Galarraga, the guy who replaced him. Willis will get the start, his first since he hyperextended his right knee on April 11. Galarraga, whose 8 1/3 innings his last time out marked the longest start by a Tiger this season, will then follow Willis in relief. It's an unusual move usually seen only in the Minor Leagues, but it's the one way Leyland could work Willis back into rotation without removing another deserving candidate.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer continues to thrive as a starter. He allowed just two runs in six innings against the Rangers in a 3-1 loss on Friday. It was fourth time in nine starts that Duchscherer has gone at least six innings. Even more impressive, the former reliever has allowed two earned runs or fewer in seven of his nine starts. He has not allowed more than three earned runs in a start. He has never walked more than two batters in 205 career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson battled through flu-like symptoms in his last outing Friday at Seattle to last 5 2/3 innings, long enough to earn a win after the Tigers gave him a seven-run lead before he took the mound for his first pitch. He has alternated quality and non-quality starts over his last five starts, and after allowing four Mariners runs -- two of them on Adrian Beltre home runs -- he's due for a more effective outing. Problem is, he's 0-3 with a 6.12 in four regular-season starts at Oakland, though he was successful there in the 2006 ALCS.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton failed in his third bid to win consecutive decisions last Saturday in an 8-4 loss at Texas. Blanton allowed six runs in six innings and didn't have a strikeout. Blanton will try to win for just the second time in 10 home starts. He has a decent enough home ERA of 3.99 at pitcher-friendly McAfee Coliseum, but he has only a 1-5 record to show for it. Blanton does continue to eat up innings with 86 1/3 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has continued to pitch like an ace in his four starts since being recalled from the disabled list on May 14. Lackey threw eight strong innings against the Blue Jays on Saturday, giving up two runs (one earned) on six hits while striking out seven and walking one. He didn't factor into the decision but once again showed his right shoulder has recovered from its early season triceps strain. Lackey is 12-3 with a 2.84 ERA against the A's in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Smith finally had a bad outing in the A's 13-8 victory over Texas last Sunday. The Rookie of the Year candidate allowed seven runs in five innings. The left-hander was more unlucky than anything, giving up several ground-ball hits in a five-run sixth that cost him a chance at a victory. Smith had a strong May with a 2.97 ERA for five starts. He led all American League rookies with 49 strikeouts before punching out four against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a superb May (2-0, 1.78 ERA in five starts), Garland struggled to get through five innings while yielding three runs against the Jays on Sunday. A 44-pitch first inning left him in a hole, but he kept the team in a game it eventually won. Garland is 3-1 with a 3.00 ERA in five road starts. The A's knocked him around (seven earned runs, 10 hits in six innings) in an April 28 loss at home. Garland is 3-9 in 14 career starts against the A's but pitched better (3.86 ERA) than his 2-5 record suggests at McAfee Coliseum during his White Sox days.

home_pitcher_note: Harden got his second-straight no-decision in his last start against Detroit, pitching into the seventh inning before leaving with the A's behind 2-1. He allowed just two runs on five hits with three walks and eight strikeouts, marking the sixth time this season he�s allowed two runs or fewer. Harden, who did not face Los Angeles last year, has a 5-3 career record with a 3.95 ERA in 12 starts against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Back in 2006 form with another solid effort, Santana went 7 2/3 innings to beat the Mariners in Seattle on Monday night, holding them to two earned runs on six hits. He already has exceeded his win total from 2007, when he was a disappointing 7-14. Santana walked only one man and struck out three. He beat the A's, 6-1, at home on April 30, giving up one unearned run in 6 2/3 innings. He's 8-1 in 11 career outings against the A's with a 1.25 ERA, and he's 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA at McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland is coming off two consecutive starts in which he lasted just 4 1/3 innings. In his previous start against Detroit, he allowed three runs on three hits and a career-high seven walks while throwing 85 pitches in a no-decision. Before allowing 10 runs in his past two starts, Eveland had surrendered just six runs total over his first four starts in May.
away_pitcher_note: Wang has been struggling lately, going winless in his last six starts with a 6.45 ERA.  Wang is 1-0 with a 1.42 ERA in two starts against Oakland, and the Yankees are hoping for similar results in the series opener, as pitching coach Dave Eiland continues to work with Wang on his recent mechanical problems.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer survived a scary hit to his left wrist and bounced back to toss another solid pitching performance in his last start against Detroit. He allowed just two runs on three hits despite a career-high five walks. It was the fifth time this season he tossed at least six innings and the seventh time he allowed two runs or fewer. Duchscherer faced the Yankees for just one inning last year, giving up two hits and no runs. He is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA lifetime against New York, all in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Rasner suffered a tough-luck 2-1 loss against the Royals Friday. It marked his third straight loss, despite giving up just two runs in eight innings. The righty threw a career-high 118 pitches, scattering nine hits and striking out four. Rasner said he won't change how he's pitching and against Oakland, he'll look for some run support from the Yankees offense, which has scored just three combined runs in Rasner's last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton pitched seven strong innings in his last start against the Angels, but John Lackey threw seven stronger innings as the A's fell, 3-1, and Blanton got stuck with his second straight loss. He surrendered three runs (two earned) on seven hits with three strikeouts and one walk while the A's bats failed to give him much support at the plate. Blanton has never fared well against the Yankees. He got a no-decision in his only start against them last year, giving up three runs on five hits through 6 2/3 innings. Lifetime, he is 0-2 with a 9.39 ERA against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Though Pettitte strung together his worst line in 12 years, allowing 10 runs on 10 hits to the Royals on Saturday, he earned a no-decision after the Yankees capped a furious comeback with a walk-off single in the ninth. Pettitte was hurt mostly by a lack of location, leaving pitches in the middle of the plate -- including one that Jose Guillen hit for a grand slam to knock Pettitte out of the game. His next start will come against the Athletics, a team that tagged him for an 8.31 ERA in two starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Zito picked up his second win of the season against the Nationals, allowing three runs spread out over five innings of work, and leaving the bases loaded in the fifth to protect his win. He showed flashes of the strong command the Giants would like to see regularly, but had to labor to get out of jams in some innings. He said afterward that he was struggling to cope with the intense Washington heat during the afternoon game. His 83-pitch outing is something the team would like to see him build on against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Smith threw what he called an inconsistent game in his last start against the Angels, allowing five runs (four earned) on seven hits and three walks with three strikeouts in 6 1/3 innings. Coming off his worst start of the season, a seven-run no-decision against Texas, his performance against the Angels represented just the third time in his career he allowed at least four earned runs. This will be Smith's first start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: After struggling to find his command, Cain spent the week consulting with the team's other pitchers and coaches. His practice paid off on Monday as he displayed strong command in a 3-2 victory against Washington. He walked one and struck out six while lasting 6 1/3 innings. After the game, he said he felt confident during the outing, and will look to keep his aggressive mentality against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Harden got his third consecutive no-decision in his last start against the Angels, pitching six effective innings while surrendering three runs on six hits and three walks with a season-high-tying nine strikeouts. The highlight of his 99-pitch outing were the first nine pitches he threw in the game that struck out the side.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Correia's first start since April 26, when he was removed after facing three Cincinnati hitters with a strained muscle in his left side. Correia looked sharp in his Minor League injury rehabilitation outings -- particularly last Monday, when he allowed one run and five hits in seven innings against Triple-A Colorado Springs. Except for that truncated effort against the Reds, Correia lasted at least six innings in each of his four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Entering his last start, against the Yankees, Eveland had not been the same pitcher since throwing a one-run complete game on May 21. He had lasted just 4 1/3 innings in two consecutive starts, giving up a combined 10 runs. Against New York he fared better, giving up two runs on just four hits while walking six and striking out three, but it wasn't enough for a win. It marked the seventh time in 13 starts he allowed two runs or fewer. This will be Eveland's first career start versus the Giants. In 2007, he pitched a perfect 1/3 of an inning in relief against them as a Diamondback.

home_pitcher_note: Webb did not have his best stuff in his last outing against the Mets. He was removed after allowing three runs over five innings. Webb was struck on the right hip by a line drive off the bat of Carlos Delgado in the fourth inning, but manager Bob Melvin said the reason Webb was taken out after throwing just 58 pitches was because he wanted to give him a break after all the innings he has thrown this year. It was the first time that Webb did not get a decision this year. It snapped a two-start winning streak which saw him compile a 0.56 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the eighth time in 10 starting assignments, Duchscherer allowed two runs or fewer in his last start. He pitched seven strong innings against a fierce Yankees lineup, surrendering just one run on five hits while walking one and striking out four -- his lone mistake being a home run off the bat of Jason Giambi. It was the sixth time he pitched at least six innings and the ninth time he walked two batters or fewer. Duchscherer has only faced Arizona once in his career, and it came as a relief pitcher. In one inning, he allowed a run on two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Haren did not get a decision in his last start, against the Mets, but he certainly pitched well enough to win. The right-hander allowed just two runs on five hits over six innings. Unfortunately for him, he was up against Johan Santana, who tossed seven scoreless innings. The D-backs rallied for two runs in the eighth and two in the ninth before eventually winning the game in the 10th. Haren was acquired in an eight-player deal with the A's last December.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton had a strong 6 2/3-inning outing in his last start, against the Yankees, but one pitch was enough to hand him his third straight loss. After getting through the first five innings unscathed, he loaded the bases in the sixth and gave up a grand slam to Hideki Matsui. As usual, Blanton didn't get much run support in the 4-1 loss. This will be his first career start against Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Davis pitched seven shutout innings in his last start against the Royals, but he gave up four walks and six hits in his no-decision. Davis has been struggling with command, allowing 23 walks and 43 hits in 38 1/3 innings in 2008. The left-hander hasn't won since May 23, his first start since he had a cancerous thyroid removed.
away_pitcher_note: Other than giving up a season-high six walks, Smith threw a solid five-inning outing against the Giants in his last start. He gave up one run on just three hits while striking out four in five innings. After the game, Smith noted he wants to work on his control and, thus, last longer in games, but "a win's a win." He has never faced Arizona, the team that selected him in the sixth round of the 2005 Draft.

home_pitcher_note: Harden tossed a one-hit gem in his last start against the Giants, but a pitch count of 95 forced him out after the sixth inning. He didn't allow a run while walking two and striking out five for his first win since May 23. Before Sunday's game, he had been dealt three consecutive no-decisions. Harden has never faced the Diamondbacks in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw is coming off a four-hit performance vs. Tampa Bay, during which his six strikeouts were overshadowed by a trio of crippling walks. Hendrickson is always as good as his command, and the veteran pitcher fell behind in the count often in Saturday night's loss. Of the  103 pitches he threw to the Rays, only 57 were strikes. Hendrickson will look to bounce back in Oakland, where he is 2-3 in six games, with a 7.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland got the start he had been looking for since his one-run complete game May 21 in his last outing against the Giants. He pitched a solid 6 2/3 innings, allowing just one run on six hits while walking three and striking out five, marking the eighth time in 14 starts he allowed two runs or fewer. The win came after two consecutive starts in which he had walked six or more. Eveland will be facing Florida for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-high 12 strikeouts in a win over the Rays, Nolasco is emerging into a dependable starter. As a rookie in 2006, he won 11 games, and he is moving closer to that number. He threw a career-most 132 pitches in his 8 2/3 innings at Tampa Bay. In June, he is 2-1 with a 3.98 ERA in three starts. In May, he was 4-1 with a 3.97 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer cruised his way through his last outing, a 15-1 A's rout over Brandon Webb and the Arizona Diamondbacks. The right-hander picked up his seventh win of the season, going eight innings, allowing only one run and five hits. Duchscherer has won four of his last five outings and has lowered his season ERA to 2.08. He will be making his first career start against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Positive results are starting to emerge for Miller, who stepped up with his second straight strong seven-inning start. In a win over the Mariners, the 23-year-old gave up one run on six hits. He showed he could cruise along without relying on the strikeout, as he fanned two, but also walked two. In a start before that, he struck out seven in seven innings, while giving up one run in a no-decision against the Phillies. Beating Seattle marked his first win since May 22, when he claimed the decision against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton had his worst outing of the year the last time out, as he surrendered eight earned runs and seven hits in just three innings of work against the D-backs at Chase Field. After being the victim of a lack of run support in recent games, Blanton lacked command right out of the chute, allowing five runs in the first and three more on a Dan Haren bases-loaded double in the third. The A's are 4-12 (.250) in his starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer struggled with his control Tuesday against the Red Sox, walking five in five innings of work. The free bases cost the veteran lefty, as Boston built an early lead that the Phillies' offense could not surmount. The loss to Boston was Moyer's first since losing in San Francisco on May 10. In 43 lifetime starts against the Athletics, Moyer is 17-15 -- including two shutouts -- with a 4.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Smith will be making his 15th start of the year after getting a no-decision in his last start against Arizona. He gave up one run on just three hits in five innings against the Diamondbacks, marking the second consecutive game he posted those exact numbers. Smith has never faced the Phillies in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick hit an early wall against the Red Sox on Wednesday. He allowed back-to-back home runs in the first inning and ultimately left the game after allowing six runs in three innings. The rough outing against the defending World Series champs may prove to be just one blemish on Kendrick's season. The Phillies have, after all, won 10 of his last 12 starts. Kendrick has not yet faced Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Harden got his sixth no-decision of the season in his last start against Florida. In 5 2/3 innings, he gave up just one run on five hits while walking two and striking out five in a back-and-forth game that eventually ended in a 7-6 A's win. It was the eighth time this season he had allowed two runs or fewer and the fourth time he walked two batters or fewer. Harden has never faced Philadelphia but is 2-0 with a 0.69 ERA in Interleague Play this season.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander regressed after a string of five straight quality starts when he allowed 12 hits in five innings on Friday to the Angels. Eaton was in trouble all evening, starting with a first-inning, two-run home run allowed to Vladimir Guerrero. Still, with nine quality starts this season, Eaton has kept his team in the game. He is 1-1 with a 4.91 ERA in his career vs. the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland threw for 6 1/3 innings and gave up two runs on eight hits while walking two, hitting two and striking out four in his last start against the Marlins, which he described as a "battle." It was the ninth time in 18 starts, however, that he limited the opposing team to two runs or fewer. Eveland is 1-0 against the Giants -- the win coming just two weeks ago when he limited San Francisco to one run on six hits through 6 2/3 innings at AT&T Park.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts off the disabled list, Correia has shown flashes of good pitching but hasn't put it all together. In his most recent start, against the Royals, he lasted a season-low five innings and gave up three runs. A two-out, two-run single in the fourth sank him in that outing. In his two starts since getting off the DL, Correia has pitched 10 1/3 innings and given up eight runs.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer made yet another case for a second All-Star game appearance in his last start against Florida. He limited the Marlins to just one run on six hits while walking two and striking out five en route to becoming the Major League's ERA leader. Duchscherer is riding on a career-high four-game winning streak, and he will start against the Giants for the first time in his career. In five relief appearances, he is 1-0 with a 2.16 ERA versus San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum had the shortest start of his season on Sunday against the Royals. He lasted just five innings and gave up five runs. Lincecum said he just wasn't focused. A third-inning collision may have also affected his concentration. The subpar outing raised his ERA from 2.21 to 2.54. Lincecum has now been unable to notch a quality start in two straight outings after opening the season with 13 straight quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton finally looked like his staff ace self in his last start against the Phillies while snapping a four-game losing streak. He limited Philadelphia to just one run on four hits while walking four and striking out five -- his only mistake coming on a solo home run. Blanton did not face San Francisco when the A's made a visit to AT&T Park earlier this month, but in his career he has a 1-1 record with a 3.97 ERA in four games against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez excelled in his last start, limiting Cleveland to one run and five hits in 7 2/3 innings for his fifth victory in six games. He has slowly emerged as the staff's co-ace with Tim Lincecum, as reflected by San Francisco's 12-4 record when he starts (the Giants are 11-5 when Lincecum pitches, including his April 2 relief effort). Plagued by erratic control early in the season, Sanchez has walked no more than three batters in eight consecutive starts. He also has allowed only one home run in his last seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: Garland got plenty of early run support in his last start against Washington -- the Angels scored a season-high six runs before Garland even toed the rubber. The seasoned right-hander did his part, pitching seven innings and giving up just three runs while striking out 11. Garland also took full advantage of his Interleague opportunity to hit, picking up an RBI on a groundout in that six-run first.
away_pitcher_note: Smith had to battle yet again in his last start against the Marlins, but he got zero run support in the four-run outing, allowing seven hits while walking two and striking out three in the 4-0 loss. He lasted 5 2/3 innings in his 98-pitch performance. Smith took a tough 2-0 loss in his first career start against Los Angeles on April 29, scattering just two runs on three hits while walking five through eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Santana struggled with his control in a 5-4 loss to the Nationals last Wednesday, walking five. One walk was intentional, but another came unintended and with the bases loaded. In total, Santana gave up four runs over six innings, but picked up no-decision when the Nationals won on a walk-off single in the ninth.
away_pitcher_note: Harden tossed one of his best outings of the season in his last start against Philadelphia, throwing four innings of no-hit ball before giving up one of just two hits without allowing a run in eight innings. He walked only one while striking out a career-high 11. In his first start against the Angels this year on June 8, Harden gave up three runs on six hits through six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders wasn't razor-sharp, needing 70 pitches to get 12 outs on his way to allowing three runs (two earned) in five innings against the Dodgers Friday night at Dodger Stadium. But he pitched well enough to keep his team in the game and did nothing to damage his case for an All-Star Game berth. Saunders wasn't hurt by his four walks while striking out four, but they elevated his pitch count. Back on more familiar AL West turf, Saunders beat the A's 2-0 on April 29 at home, holding them to four hits across eight innings. He's 3-1 with a 4.24 ERA in six career outings against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland appeared to have the command he said he's been missing during his last few appearances in his most recent start against the Giants. He limited San Francisco to just one run on five hits while walking two and striking out three in 7 1/3 innings. It was the fourth time in 16 starts he lasted at least seven innings and the seventh time he walked two batters or fewer. In his first career start against the Angels on April 30, Eveland was tagged with the loss after giving up six earned runs on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez simply hasn't pitched well for the White Sox recently, and manager Ozzie Guillen said after his latest start that the staff ace needs to start challenging hitters more. Vazquez lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Cubs on Saturday, his shortest outing of the season. He allowed five runs for a fourth consecutive start, despite striking out seven batters. He owns a 7.48 ERA in his last five outings. Vazquez hasn't faced the Athletics this season, but has seen them five times in his career with little success. He's 1-2 with a 6.60 ERA lifetime against them.
