away_pitcher_note: Despite getting the loss in a close 1-0 game in his last start against the Giants, Duchscherer made yet another case for his second career All-Star appearance. He didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning, when he gave up two before going the next four innings without surrendering another one. In his eight innings of work, he walked just one and struck out four while throwing 97 pitches. In 13 relief appearances against Chicago, Duchscherer is 3-1 with a 2.76 ERA. He has given up five runs on 13 hits in 16 1/3 innings versus the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle is looking more and more like the White Sox ace of old with each passing start. To illustrate that point, the seven innings he pitched Sunday were the fewest in his last five starts. He surrendered just one unearned run to the Cubs and picked up his third-straight victory. Buehrle is 4-0 in his last five starts with an accompanying 1.15 ERA.  He's faced Oakland once this year and pitched far too well to have earned the loss. He allowed two earned runs in seven innings and exited the game trailing 2-1.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing three innings of no-hit ball in his last start, Blanton gave up a string of five consecutive hits in the fourth against the Giants en route to surrendering seven runs on eight hits while pitching into the fifth inning -- the second time in his last three starts he's given up seven runs or more. Blanton will look to get back on track against the White Sox, against whom he owns a 2-1 record with a 3.12 ERA in three career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd looked much better Monday against the Indians than he had in either of his previous two starts. He allowed four runs -- three earned -- and struck out a career-high 10 batters. The only player that got the better of him was Jhonny Peralta, who smacked three of the seven hits he allowed. Two of the hits were doubles and the other was a home run. Floyd attributed the quality start to the return of his offspeed command. He hadn't been able to throw his changeup for strikes in his previous starts. Floyd has never faced the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Oakland's lone rookie in the starting rotation, Smith was outstanding his last time out, beating the Angels by holding them to one run -- a solo home run -- on four hits while walking two and striking out three in the first complete game of his career Monday in Anaheim. Owner of one of the best pickoff moves in the game, Smith has nailed an MLB-high eight runners and now controls the opponents' running game on reputation alone. He's pitched more than seven innings only once, on April 29, in part because the A's are being cautious as he closes in on his 2007 Minor League innings total of 122. Smith, who picked up his first big league win by holding the White Sox to six hits over seven innings on April 14, has made 16 starts and has thrown 99 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Danks threw one of his best outings of the season and one of the best of his career Tuesday night against the Indians. His eight innings and eight strikeouts tied career highs, and he allowed just one earned run on four hits and a walk. He didn't factor in the decision, though. Danks has allowed only eight earned runs in his last six starts and has just one win to show for it. He's faced Oakland once this season and surrendered no runs over 7 2/3 innings. It was arguably his best start of the season before the gem he threw Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Harden, who had dominated the Phillies with eight innings of two-hit work his previous time out, wasn't nearly as strong Tuesday in Anaheim, where he threw 91 pitches while allowing two runs on five hits and a walk while striking out five over five innings before leaving with the game tied. Harden, who didn't throw any breaking balls against the Phillies, relied heavily on his changeup against the Angels but occasionally popped 94 mph on the stadium radar gun. Since the start of the 2005 season, Harden is 1-1 with a 3.71 ERA in three starts against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland gave up three runs on four hits and three walks while striking out four over 5 2/3 innings in his previous outing, Wednesday at Anaheim, on the way to losing for the first time in four starts. Eveland hasn't allowed a home run in his past seven starts, and his outing against the Angels snapped his streak of four starts of working at least six innings. He walked 13 batters in his first two starts of June, but he hasn't walked more than three in a start since then.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn is on a roll right now with five consecutive strong starts. His fastball has been effective, and he unleashed some successful split-finger fastballs during his last outing against the Blue Jays on Wednesday. He made just one mistake in that game with a two-run homer to Adam Lind, but finished up strong. He's now riding a two-game winning streak and has lowered his ERA by nearly two runs in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer made the All-Star team in 2005 as a reliever and, manager Bob Geren said, "deserves a bid" as a starter this season. He continued pitching like an All-Star, shutting down the White Sox after a rough first inning in his previous start. Duchscherer allowed two runs and five hits, walking two and striking out five over seven innings to get the decision in the A's 3-2 victory on July 3. He has six victories in his past eight starts with a 1.54 ERA. He has allowed 33 hits over 58 1/3 innings, and opponents are slugging .260 against him in that span. Duchscherer is 0-5 in his career, mostly in relief, against the Mariners. They beat him 5-3 on April 26 when Duchscherer had not pitched in three weeks because of a strained right biceps.
away_pitcher_note: Silva welcomes a start against just about anybody except the Tigers. After finally ending a nine-game losing streak, including two to Detroit, the veteran right-hander met the Bengals one last time in his latest start. He was more effective, surrendering five runs in five innings, but absorbed his 10th loss of the season. The Tigers know Silva throws a lot of strikes and came out swinging, accumulating nine hits. A sinker-ball specialist, the first six outs he recorded were on fly balls. Silva is 1-0 against the Athletics this season, beating them on April 17. He allowed four hits and one run over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton had a poor start against the Giants on June 29, but rebounded against the White Sox by dominating the inside part of the plate. Blanton allowed a run and six hits over seven innings -- establishing four types of pitches -- in the A's 7-1 victory. His performance contrasted his previous six starts, in which he had a 7.49 ERA and opponents slugged .511 against him. Usually it was one poor inning, Blanton said, that would bite him in his rough stretch. Ideally, he would like to find consistency.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander, who led the team in wins last season with 16 as a starting pitcher, returns to the rotation in place of ailing (shoulder) Erik Bedard. Batista worked two solid innings of relief against the Tigers on Saturday night and his fastball was clocked at 98 mph, prompting interim manager Jim Riggleman to say it's the best he has seen Batista throw all season. When he has good command of his fastball and is able to locate it, the 37-year-old can be extremely effective.

home_pitcher_note: Smith tossed a complete game against the Angels on June 30, but was unable to pitch six innings -- for the fifth time in seven starts -- against the White Sox. He also struggled with his command, walking six (tying a season high for the rookie) and allowing four runs in a 6-1 defeat to Chicago. Smith said he wants to try and get outs without going so deep into counts -- which will help him last longer in games and won't put the A's bullpen on alert as early.
away_pitcher_note: The knuckleball specialist battled his control at times during his start against the Tigers, issuing five walks during his six-inning stint. But it was the long ball that prevented him from winning his third game of the season, as solo pokes by ex-Mariner Carlos Guillen and Miguel Cabrera left Dickey on the short end of a 2-1 game when he departed. The five free passes were a single-game season high, as were the two home runs. He had surrendered just three home runs in 31 innings entering the game at Safeco Field. This will be Dickey's first outing of the season against the Athletics. He is 0-4 with a 9.00 ERA in seven career games against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher, acquired by the A's on Tuesday in a six-player deal that sent Rich Harden to the Cubs, will be making his first start in an Oakland uniform -- and as an American League pitcher. In his last starting assignment, with Chicago, Gallagher gave up three runs on four hits through five innings en route to losing to the Giants. This will be Gallagher's first career start against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was in total control of the Blue Jays on Sunday, a homer by Rod Barjaras the lone blemish in a four-hit, no-walk, complete-game gem. He needed only 98 pitches, 67 strikes, relying heavily on a sinker and changeup to keep hitters off balance. Two of his three strikeouts came in key situations, leaving a runner stranded at third. Since May 3, getting a feel for his new surroundings, Garland has yielded more than three earned runs just once in 13 starts. His ERA over that period is 2.78, reducing it from a high of 5.94 on April 28 to 3.76. Garland is 4-10, 4.70 ERA in 16 career starts against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland overcame first-inning struggles to notch a 4-3 win over Seattle in his last start. Upon giving up a three-run homer to Richie Sexson, Eveland left after 5 1/3 innings without surrendering another run despite allowing nine hits -- the most he's allowed since scattering 11 against Toronto on May 29. In his two starts against Los Angeles this year, Eveland compiled an 0-1 record with a 7.36 ERA. He surrendered nine runs on 11 hits through 11 innings in those games.
away_pitcher_note: Santana will be glad to kiss Rangers Ballpark goodbye until his next visit. Despite earning his 10th victory of the season at Rangers Ballpark his last time out, his career ERA there remained above eight (dropping from 8.10 to 8.05) after allowing six runs in seven innings. The six runs came on 10 hits, including two home runs, and two walks while striking out six. His main blemish was a five-run fifth inning, in which the Rangers hit both home runs. Fortunately for Santana, his next test comes against the Athletics, against whom he's 8-1 in his career with a 1.48 ERA. He has a 3-0 record with a 1.80 ERA in five starts at McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Just two days after being named to the American League All-Star squad, Duchscherer fittingly tossed a performance resembling the stuff deemed worthy of a Midsummer Classic trip. The righty threw his first career complete-game shutout as the A's grabbed a 2-0 victory against Seattle. Duchscherer pitched four innings of no-hit ball before giving up a double with two outs in the fifth inning. He allowed just one more hit the rest of the game while throwing 105 pitches through nine frames. In his only start against the Angels this year on May 1, Duchscherer surrendered six runs (one earned) on six hits in five innings while striking out six, but still notched the win.
away_pitcher_note: Mosley was called up from Triple-A Salt Lake for a spot-start because the scheduled starter, Joe Saunders, was with his wife, who gave birth to a daughter Saturday night. In seven appearances with the Angels this season, Moseley has a 1-3 record with a 7.85 ERA. His last start in the Majors was April 26 against the Tigers, a five-inning, three-run performance. He's pitching on three-days rest following a six-inning, three-run win against Tacoma.

home_pitcher_note: Mussina will take the mound for the Yankees first game following the All-Star break. The veteran right-hander last pitched on July 10 against the Pittsburgh Pirates in New York's final Interleague game of the season. He surrendered two earned runs on nine hits while striking out five over six strong innings of work. He is now 2-2 with a 3.09 ERA in his past three starts. The 39-year-old is 17-10 with a 3.82 ERA in his career against the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Smith will get the series-opening nod in the absence of originally slated starter Joe Blanton, who was traded to Philadelphia on Thursday for three Minor Leaguers.  Smith threw six shutout innings against the Mariners in his last start, but got zero run support -- nothing new for him -- en route to a no-decision. He left the game having received zero Oakland runs in seven of his 17 starts, and one run in another three outings. Smith scattered just four hits while walking one and striking out two. This will be his first career start against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Chamberlain will be making his first career appearance against the Athletics. The 22-year-old phenom has been extremely effective since joining the Yankees rotation on June 3rd, posting a 2.81 ERA in eight starts, but has just one win over that span because of a lack of run support. Chamberlain's last outing was on July 11th against the Blue Jays. He surrendered three runs on seven hits while striking out nine. He was forced to take the loss, though, as Jays ace Roy Halladay out dueled him en route to a shutout victory.
away_pitcher_note: In his first career start as an American League pitcher, the newly acquired Gallagher proved he can get a win just as easily as Rich Harden in the A's rotation by pitching seven dominant innings of two-hit, two-run ball. Traded by the Cubs for Harden in a six-player deal four days before he made the start, Gallagher struck out seven in the dominant win over the Angels. This will mark his first career start against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte's successful first half of the season came to a disappointing end during his last outing against the Blue Jays. New York's veteran left-hander suffered through a four-run second inning en route to his seventh loss of the season. The biggest blow came off the bat of infielder Marco Scutaro who hit a three-run home run over the wall in left to break the game wide-open. Pettitte managed to settle down after that, though, and completed six innings, allowing eight hits while striking out six. In all of Pettitte's losses this season he has surrendered at least seven hits. He is 9-5 with a 3.42 ERA in 18 career starts against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Two days before making his second career All-Star appearance, Duchscherer pitched 7 2/3 solid innings against the Angels, giving up just two runs on five hits while walking two and striking out three in a no-decision. He has yet to surrender more than three earned runs in a game, and his last start marked the 15th time in 16 starts he walked two batters or fewer. Duchscherer will look to repeat his stellar first half against a team he is 1-0 against in his only career start. He gave up one run on five hits through seven innings while striking out four while facing the Yankees earlier this year.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir took the loss in his last start, against the Indians on July 13, when he allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings. Kazmir has not picked up a win since June 27 at Pittsburgh, and he's 1-4 in his last five decisions. In addition, Kazmir has made it into the seventh inning just once in his last seven starts. The lefty is still working to gain command of his slider, which has historically been his best pitch. Without his slider, he has primarily used a fastball-changeup combination this season. He is 5-1 with a 2.96 ERA in nine career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: First-inning struggles continued for Eveland in his last start against the Angels. He pitched well in 5 2/3 innings, giving up two runs in the first inning, on five hits with five strikeouts, but he also walked five. It was the third straight outing in which Eveland had trouble in the opening frame, but after the game he said toning it down to about 80 percent may be the solution to his early-inning woes. He pitched his first career complete game in his only start against Tampa Bay earlier in the year, giving up a lone run on just three hits while walking one and fanning five in the win.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine got clipped for his fourth loss of the season on July 10 against the Indians when he allowed six runs on nine hits and three home runs. The right-hander is a master of deception employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. If the Rays followed in rotation after the All-Star Break, he would start this game, but it's likely the Rays will reset the rotation after the four-day break. Sonnanstine is 2-1 with a 6.10 ERA in five career starts against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: With Joe Blanton traded to the Phillies, Braden gets a spot in the starting rotation. He threw one inning Friday in Oakland's loss to the Yankees, allowing a solo home run to Alex Rodriguez. Before then, he had appeared in only one game -- on July 11 -- since being called up July 8. Braden has pitched in nine games this season, owning a 4.80 ERA over 15 innings with 16 hits and eight earned runs. Manager Bob Geren said Braden's added some velocity on his fastball since last year, when he started 14 games and had a 6.72 ERA combined with six relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Shields continued his home dominance on Friday night, notching his eighth win this season, six of which have been at Tropicana Field. The 26-year-old right-hander tossed seven innings of one-run baseball -- allowing only a solo homer to Toronto's Adam Lind -- in the four-strikeout performance. Shields' best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. He will be making his first start of the season against Oakland, a team he has traditionally fared well against. In four career starts, Shields is 2-1 with a 4.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Smith struggled Friday night against the Yankees and exited after just 3 2/3 innings. He allowed six earned runs on eight hits in the shortened outing. He fell into long at-bats to contribute to the high pitch count. The lefty threw 62 pitches through the first three innings. Smith walked five and struck out just one in the game. He is 0-1 with a 2.57 ERA against the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher is slated to make his 13th start of the season and his third with Oakland since being traded in a six-player deal with the Cubs on July 8. The right-hander garnered no decision in Saturday's 4-3, 12-inning loss in New York, allowing two runs in five innings off seven hits. He picked up his first win in an A's uniform on July 11, tossing seven innings of two-hit ball. This will be his first career start against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla returned from the disabled list on Sunday and pitched a gem after being shelved with neck stiffness. The veteran right-hander threw seven innings of shutout ball against the Twins, allowing only three hits. Padilla didn't allow a runner past first base. He was originally scheduled to pitch Saturday, but was switched to pitch the first game of the A's series. He was victorious against Oakland on May 2, going 5 2/3 innings, while giving up one earned run on five hits and four walks in a 4-3 Rangers victory.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer took a tough-luck loss against the Yankees on Sunday afternoon. The right-hander threw seven innings on a hot day despite feeling under the weather from a viral infection. He gave up six hits and two runs to a patient Yankees lineup, and the righty said he felt tired by the time he left the game. He has held opponents to two runs or fewer in 11 straight starts, pitching at least six innings in each outing. In his last start against Texas, on May 30, Duchscherer allowed two runs and six hits in a 3-1 Oakland loss.
away_pitcher_note: Since an impressive debut, Harrison has been hit hard in his last two starts. Against Chicago and Minnesota, the lefty allowed a total of 13 runs in 7 2/3 innings. On Saturday facing the Twins, he gave up eight earned runs in five innings en route to a 14-2 Rangers loss. Harrison will next make his fourth career Major League start, facing the A's on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: The left-handed Eveland fell to 7-7 after taking Monday night's series-opening loss against Tampa Bay. Eveland was twice victimized by the long ball, and the Rays turned two of their three stolen bases -- in three attempts -- into runs. Eveland has lost his only decision against Texas, and has a 4.50 ERA from that five-inning contest.
away_pitcher_note: If Hurley is feeling well enough to pitch, he'll start Sunday's finale against Oakland. Hurley was supposed to come off the 15-day disabled list to start for the Rangers on Monday against Chicago. He felt soreness in his throwing arm, so the Rangers decided to play it safe and have Scott Feldman start instead. Hurley said the left hamstring injury that landed him on the DL on July 8 has recovered and he will be ready for his next turn in the rotation. The rookie right-hander has not faced Oakland this season.

home_pitcher_note: Braden, who has bounced back and forth between Triple-A Sacramento and Oakland this season, will be making just his third start after having spent most of his time with the A's as a relief pitcher. He got the win in his last start against Tampa Bay, surrendering one run on four hits through five innings. Braden is 0-1 with an 8.44 ERA in his career against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke, after a superb getaway to his season, has not won in a month -- since June 24, when he beat the Rockies. Since then, he has three losses and two no-decisions in five starts and has a 6.67 ERA in that span. When the Tigers started belting his fastball early last Wednesday, he made an adjustment to more offspeed pitches, but admittedly he made it too late. Against Oakland, Greinke had a no-decision in a 6-5 loss on April 19. He's faced the A's eight times, with a 1-0 record and 2.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw retired the first nine Rays batters he faced on Wednesday afternoon, before being victim to the long ball. Smith allowed a pair of back-to-back homers to take his ninth loss this season. Despite a poor record, Smith has pitched well, and is mainly a victim of Oakland's struggling offense. His 3.07 average run support is lowest in the American League. Smith will look to change his recent fate -- and pick up his first win since the calendar flip -- against the Royals on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Meche came up with a beauty on Thursday night after an ugly beginning. He threw 31 pitches in the first inning but held the Rays scoreless, as he did for seven innings before turning the game over to the bullpen. He got his second victory since the break, allowing just one run in 13 1/3 innings to two first-place clubs, Chicago and Tampa Bay. He's been pretty good after a shaky start to his season, posting a 3.27 ERA in his last 14 games. Meche faces the A's for the first time this year; he's just 2-7 against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start with the A's, Gallagher got tagged for five runs (one earned) on nine hits -- two of them home runs -- in 5 1/3 innings against Texas. He struck out five but also walked five in the no-decision. This marks Gallagher's first career starting assignment against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister was hurt by defensive miscues in his last start on Friday night against Tampa Bay. He lasted just 5 1/3 innings, the extra outs driving his pitch count up to 100, and was charged with three runs (two earned) on seven hits. Bannister did feel he made good adjustments in his delivery on the stretch, a pregame goal. But he still hasn't won since June 23. Bannister started against Oakland on April 18 and was drilled for five runs in five innings. The loss came after he'd won his first three starts of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield suffered through his shortest outing since May 23 on Sunday, surrendering six runs and eight hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Yankees. That May 23 game was against Oakland, which will be Wakefield's next challenge when he takes the mound on Friday. Wakefield allowed eight runs and eight hits in five innings during that outing against the A's, and he'll look to rebound from both that start in Oakland as well as his last outing against New York. Prior to the Yankees game, Wakefield had a 2.96 ERA in four July starts.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer endured his worst performance of the season in his last start against Texas, giving up a career-high eight runs on nine hits while pitching into the seventh inning after entering the game not having allowed more than three earned runs all season. He said he felt fine and explained that the powerful Rangers lineup "flat out beat me." Duchscherer will look to get back on track against a team against which he earned a win earlier in the season. He didn't allow a run and scattered just one hit through eight innings in that start versus Boston.

home_pitcher_note: When Lester last took the mound on Sunday against the Yankees, New York had taken the first two games of the series and were in position to draw even with the Sox in the standings. But just as he's done all season, Lester delivered a brilliant outing that propelled Boston to a 9-2 win. He went seven strong innings and allowed just two runs -- both coming in a troublesome fifth inning. He recorded a no-decision on April 23 against the Angels, allowing four runs and two homers in a 6-4 Boston loss.
away_pitcher_note: After posting four innings of one-run ball in his last start against Texas, Eveland ran into trouble in the fifth frame and let frustration get the best of him en route to allowing five runs. The A's offense, though, had already given him six runs, so Eveland walked away with a no-decision. This will mark his first career start against Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka is coming off one of his roughest starts of the season, giving up six runs in five innings pitched against the Angels. But his July ERA was lights-out prior to the outing -- a mere 1.05 in four starts during the month. Matsuzaka walked only two batters against Los Angeles, which is always his one area of concern when he takes the ball. He's walked 62 batters this year, placing him two behind Daniel Cabrera for most in the American League as of his last start. This will be Matsuzaka's third start against the A's this season, but his first since April 1. He's 1-0 against Oakland, with Boston winning both of his starts in one-run affairs.
away_pitcher_note: In just his second start since being placed back in the rotation, Braden fared well against the Royals, but two mistakes were enough for a loss. He pitched 6 2/3 innings, surrendering six hits -- two of them two-run dingers -- en route to allowing four runs in a 4-1 loss. This will mark Braden's first career start -- and appearance -- against Boston.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Halladay lost to the Rays for the third time this season, allowing three runs on six hits in eight innings. The right-hander enters August having thrown at least one complete game in each month this season, and he will face the A's for the second time this year. On May 28, Oakland managed one run in eight innings against Halladay, who struck out nine en route to his sixth win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Royals, Gallagher surrendered three runs on five hits while walking three and striking out four in five innings en route to a no-decision. He will be making just his fifth start with Oakland this year as he faces a Toronto team he pitched against June 13. In that outing, he allowed three runs on seven hits and struck out five through five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Richmond took the loss in his first career Major League start, allowing the Rays three runs in 5 1/3 innings. The righty struck out four and walked none, throwing 54 of his 92 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Royals, Smith pitched what manager Bob Geren called "one of his sharpest outings," but two pitches that resulted in home runs doomed the A's in a 5-2 loss. Smith went seven innings, surrendering the five runs on just four hits while walking two and striking out five. He also tallied his Major League-leading 13th pickoff, which is the most by a big leaguer since Andy Pettitte picked off 14 in 1997. In his first career start against Toronto earlier this year, Smith gave up three runs (two earned) on two hits while walking five and fanning five in six innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts since coming off the disabled list, Marcum is 0-1 with a 9.82 ERA. He's yet to complete six innings in any of his starts since rejoining the rotation, as well. His last time out at Texas, Marcum departed after just 4 1/3 innings. He cruised through the first three innings, having allowed just one baserunner, but he was pummeled for six runs his next 1 1/3 and didn't figure in the decision. Marcum will next face the A's, against whom he received a no-decision earlier in the season. In that start, he allowed just one run in seven innings and struck out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired in the Nick Swisher trade with the White Sox in the offseason, the left-hander is scheduled to make his Major League debut in the third game of the four-game set against the Blue Jays. Gonzalez was 8-7 with a 4.24 ERA in Triple-A Sacramento this season, striking out 128 batters in just 123 innings. In his last start against Nashville, Gonzalez allowed just two hits over eight shutout innings, striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett set a pair of career milestones his last time out in a stadium where most milestones pitchers set aren't positive ones. Against Texas in Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, Burnett won his 13th game of the season -- his most in a single season -- and the victory gave him one against every Major League team, but it came at a cost. He allowed four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings. He'd allowed just four earned runs total in his previous four starts and hadn't allowed that many runs in a game since July 9 against Baltimore. Burnett will face Oakland next. In two starts against the Athletics this season, he's 0-1 with a 6.97 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Except for a rough outing two starts back, Duchscherer has continued to be outstanding, even though his recent record -- 0-2 in his past four starts -- doesn't reflect it. He allowed one run on five hits in six innings against the Red Sox at Fenway Park last time out, but did not receive a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers had a bizarre outing on Saturday night, in which the southpaw tied a season-low 3 1/3 innings and garnered a season-high eight strikeouts. The veteran hurler threw 109 pitches in that short span, with only 63 of those for strikes. Afterward, Rogers said he had good stuff, and was disappointed that his pitch count went awry. He had 65 tosses in the first two innings alone. Still, the 19-year veteran should have no problem bouncing back from the loss for Friday's start. In 36 starts vs. Oakland he is 21-7, with a 4.28 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Dallas Braden: While battling sickness in his previous start against the Red Sox, Braden lasted just 3 1/3 innings, surrendering four runs on six hits while striking out one. It marked his third starting assignment of the season, a time span in which he has allowed nine runs on 16 hits through 15 innings. Braden owns a 0-1 record vs. Detroit in three career starts. His 12.34 ERA against the Tigers represents his highest mark against any team.

home_pitcher_note: The questions of whether Galarraga's hot start was for real are gone now that he has carried his success into August. At this point, he's the best starter the Tigers have going, delivering consistently efficient, stingy innings and leaving with his team ahead in his past three outings. He gave up three runs in as many innings against the A's on June 3, the day of his long-lost piggyback start with Dontrelle Willis.
away_pitcher_note: With right-hander Sean Gallagher battling irritation in his throwing shoulder, the A's decided to push his start to sometime in their upcoming home series against the Rays. In place of Gallagher, Oakland will start Meyer, who was called up to the A's on Aug. 3. Facing the Blue Jays in his last appearance, Meyer provided four solid innings of relief, allowing no runs on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson ended up with no decision Tuesday at Chicago after giving up four runs on nine hits in five-plus innings, which started the White Sox on their way to overcoming a 6-1 deficit. Three of his past six starts have ended up becoming extra-inning marathons after he left, but his bigger concern lately has been lasting deeper into games. He has worked through six innings just once over his past four starts, and his ERA has risen nearly a full run over his past five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Smith pitched well against the Blue Jays in his last start. He allowed just two runs on four hits over his six innings. He walked two, struck out four and needed 87 pitches in the outing. Though he left the game in line for the win, Smith eventually received a no-decision, as A's closer Huston Street allowed the Jays to win the game in the ninth inning. Smith has not collected a victory since June 30.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez pitched well against the Blue Jays in his last start, which was also his Major League debut. He allowed four runs on four hits over six innings. The left-hander walked two and struck out four in the outing, needing 95 pitches. What was more impressive, though, was that after surrendering three runs in the first inning, he settled down considerably. During a stretch from the second to the fifth inning, he did not allow a hit, issuing one walk and retiring 15 of the 16 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive start, Kazmir struggled on the hill, as the lefty allowed a season-high nine hits and five earned runs to Cleveland. The 24-year-old Rays ace allowed three consecutive one-out hits -- including two doubles -- to the meat of the Tribe's lineup, and exited after 97 pitches and 4 1/3 innings. In his last 11 starts, Kazmir has gone seven innings just once, in a July 21 win at Oakland. Kazmir has fared well against the A's this season, going 2-0 in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer lasted a season-low five innings in his last start against Toronto, surrendering four runs on seven hits while walking two and striking out six. This will be his first career start against Tampa Bay, a team against which he owns a 1-0 record with a 1.96 ERA in 10 relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine pitched well against the Mariners Thursday when he allowed one run on five hits in 7 1/3 innings, but came away with a no-decision. After surviving minor bumps in the first and second innings in which the Mariners stranded runners at third, Sonnanstine retired the next 17 batters he faced, establishing a new club record for most consecutive hitters retired. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Sonnanstine is 1-2 with a 6.00 ERA in three career starts against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher will be making his 10th start with Oakland after missing a scheduled start last week due to right shoulder soreness that he admitted he had been experiencing for two weeks. In his last start, against Toronto, the righty was shelled for five runs in just three innings. A healthy Gallagher will look to return to solid form against a Tampa Bay team he's faced once in his career. In his first start against the Rays, earlier this year, Gallagher allowed four hits and one unearned run en route to a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Shields made his 17th quality start of the season Friday night by allowing three earned runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Mariners to pick up his 10th win of the season. The 26-year-old right-hander's best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. He is 3-1 with a 4.25 ERA in five career starts against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Braden picked up his third win of the season with the longest effort of his career on Friday against the Tigers. Using his fastball effectively on both sides of the plate to set up his changeup, Braden tossed seven innings and allowed just two runs -- both coming on a Marcus Thames home run -- while limiting the Tigers to five hits, which helped the A's snap a season-long 10-game losing streak. This will be Braden's first career start against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd didn't pitch great, but it was good enough to get his 12th win of the season. The right-hander gave up seven hits in 5 1/3 innings, surrendering five runs, though only three were earned. Floyd has allowed a Major League-leading 19 unearned runs this season. He faced Oakland once this season, shutting them out over 7 1/3 innings and picking up the win. Floyd has pitched much worse on the road this season, though, with a .272 average against and a 4.72 ERA away from U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Smith had his worst control of the year on Sunday at Detroit, but it was far from his worst outing of the year. Smith threw more balls than strikes in his 4 2/3 innings, but the only damage he was accountable for was a Curtis Granderson solo home run, which was enough to hand him the loss. Smith showed a strong ability to make the right pitch when trouble brewed, as he stranded eight runners. Smith is 1-1 in two starts against the White Sox this season, compiling a 3.75 ERA in 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Danks threw 6 1/3 innings of no-hit ball on Monday against the Red Sox, but he gave up two runs in the seventh, enough to give him the loss. It was an unfortunate finish to one of Danks' best starts of the season, which certainly says something about the young southpaw, considering he ranks sixth in the American League in ERA. It was his first loss since May 24, when he gave up, once again, two runs. The White Sox offense has scored one run or fewer in nine of his 23 starts this season. He faced Oakland on July 6 and gave up two runs in 6 1/3 innings, enough to earn him the win.

home_pitcher_note: In his second start with the A's -- his first in Oakland -- Gonzalez surrendered just one run on five hits while walking four and striking out five in five innings to earn his first Major League victory. This will be his third career start and first against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez followed the simple rule of attacking the strike zone and getting ahead of the hitters on Tuesday in picking up his first home victory since June 17 against Pittsburgh. The right-hander allowed five hits over eight scoreless innings, walking one and fanning 10. He reached double-digit strikeouts for the 37th time in his career. Vazquez threw an amazing 81 of his 109 pitches for strikes. Despite striking out 10 in his lone complete game this season, Vazquez has an 0-1 record against Oakland to go with a 3.00 ERA. He has a lifetime mark of 1-3 against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn allowed a leadoff homer to Johnny Damon in his last start against New York and never seemed in sync. The right-hander allowed four earned runs on six hits while striking out five in 4 2/3 innings, throwing 102 pitches. The Twins lost, 9-6. Blackburn's next start will kick off a three-game set against Oakland. The rookie has never faced the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer gave his club a solid pitching effort in his last start against the Rays, surrendering three runs on six hits through six-plus innings, but he walked away with his third consecutive loss in a 3-2 defeat. He struck out a career-high eight batters in the effort while throwing 107 pitches. However, he also gave up the long ball twice after having allowed just nine home runs combined through his first 20 starts. This will be Duchscherer's first career start against Minnesota, but he has an 0-2 record with a 4.73 ERA in eight relief appearances versus the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey finally gave up a first-inning run last time out. But it didn't matter much, as it was the only damage he sustained against the Yankees on Wednesday. The right-hander, who had gone a Twins-record 18 consecutive starts without giving up a run in the first, went six innings while allowing one earned run on three hits and a walk in a 4-2 Minnesota victory. Slowey hasn't faced the A's this season.
away_pitcher_note: After missing a start due to right shoulder soreness, Gallagher came back from the mini break with a shaky outing, giving up three runs on four hits while walking four and fanning five in just five innings en route to a no-decision against Tampa Bay. Gallagher said he felt fine, though, so he will look to go deeper against Minnesota. This will be his first career start against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano continued his stellar return from the Minors on Friday against Seattle. The lefty went seven innings, allowing no earned runs on two hits and two walks, while striking out five. He is 3-0 with a 1.45 ERA since being called up from Triple-A Rochester on Aug. 1. Liriano will look for continued prosperity on Wednesday at the Metrodome against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Dallas Braden tossed seven strong innings in his most recent start, allowing three runs on seven hits and a walk against the White Sox but drew a no-decision. The left-hander strained his groin slightly on a fastball to Jim Thome, but the injury has not altered his side work. Braden -- who is 2-1 on the road this season in eight appearances, three of which were starts -- will be facing the Twins for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander from Australia got off to a rocky start against the Twins, surrendering five runs in the first two innings. But he regrouped magnificently and made it through the fifth inning leading by a run. Rowland-Smith turned his start around by throwing more first-pitch strikes and getting better command of his fastball. He didn't overpower anyone, striking out one batter, but kept the on the lower edge of the strike zone more consistently. Rowland-Smith has faced the Athletics three times in his career, holding them to one earned run in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: A rookie acquired in the Dan Haren trade with Arizona over the winter, Smith has been more impressive than his win-loss record indicates. He's struggled with his command at times, costing him a game here and there, but he's also been victimized more than any pitcher on the A's staff by Oakland's anemic offense. In 24 starts, he's received two runs or fewer of support 17 times, including his last time out, when he took a 2-1 loss to the White Sox. Smith is 0-6 in his past eight starts, but he's unbeaten against the Twins, having held them to two runs on seven hits over seven innings in his only start against them this season.

home_pitcher_note: With a rocky debut start in Minnesota behind him and preferably not to be remembered any time soon, the left-hander takes on the Athletics at Safeco Field. Feierabend earned a return to the big leagues with a solid season at Triple-A Tacoma, posting a 7-1 record and 2.04 ERA. But the Twins weren't, socking it to him to the tune of five hits and five runs in the first inning. The 22-year-old was lifted after surrendering 10 hits and six runs over three innings. He is 0-0 with a 2.89 ERA in two career appearances against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez had a nightmare of an outing at home Sunday against the White Sox, the team that sent him to the A's in an offseason trade. Admittedly over-amped to face his former team, Gonzalez gave up three homers and gave up as many earned runs as he recorded outs (seven). One of Oakland's top prospects, Gonzalez was called up from Triple-A Sacramento earlier in the month and has made three starts. A rookie, he's never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander's disappointment in not being traded to the Twins last week could have been an underlining factor in one of his shortest outings of the season in his previous start against the White Sox. He did not make it through the fifth inning for only the fourth time in 24 starts, yielding eight runs in 4 1/3 innings. He absorbed the loss, the 99th of his MLB career. He has 98 wins. Washburn is 0-1 against the Athletics this season, dropping a 4-3 decision in Oakland on July 7.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland pitched well down in Triple-A Sacramento before coming back up to the big leagues thanks to some injuries in the starting rotation. In his three Minor League starts, he went 3-0 with a 2.57 ERA and 21 strikeouts in 21 innings pitched. He's already started 22 games with the big club this year, going 125 innings and striking out 85 hitters. Eveland has already faced Seattle twice this season, winning both times by giving up three earned runs over five and 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander had a rough start against the White Sox, yielding 11 hits and five runs over five innings to fall under the .500 mark this season. But the big news was the fact he did not strike out a batter for only the second time in 97 career starts. The only other time it happened was on April 8, 2007, when an injury limited him to one-third of an inning against the Twins. Also uncharacteristically, Hernandez was hurt by the long ball. He gave up two home runs for just the second time this season, and the first time since April 11 against the Angels. He is 1-1 against the Athletics this season, and 6-3 in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Meyer has gone 10-5 for Triple-A Sacramento this season and got the callup after injuries to starting pitchers Justin Duchscherer and Sean Gallagher. He's also appeared six times for the Athletics this year, including a start. He's thrown 14 2/3 innings in the Majors in 2008 and given up nine earned runs and 15 hits. He last faced Seattle on Sept. 19, 2007, when he gave up five earned runs in four and 2/3 innings to take the loss.

home_pitcher_note: More reflective of Weaver's stuff and command than the three earned runs he yielded in six innings against the Rays on Wednesday night were his nine strikeouts against one walk. After a three-run second inning that included a triple that should have been caught, Weaver pitched brilliantly to keep the Angels in a game they won late. Twice he struck out the side, getting superior movement on all of his pitches. Weaver is 2-1 with a 2.76 ERA in five career starts against the A's. He's 5-4 with a 4.03 ERA in 11 starts this year at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, who opened the year at Triple-A Sacramento and has been up with the A's four times, made his sixth start for Oakland on Wednesday at Minnesota and gave up three runs on six hits and three walks while striking out seven over 5 2/3 innings of a 3-1 loss. This will be his first start against the Angels, but he's faced the Halos four times in relief this year, allowing two runs over six innings while striking out eight without a walk.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey turned in one of his best starts of the season against the Twins on Thursday. The right-hander allowed just one run on five hits while striking out six. It was the first time he allowed one run or fewer since June 29 against the Dodgers when he threw 8 2/3 scoreless innings. Lackey has been successful against the A's in his career, going 13-3 with a 2.77 ERA against Oakland in 24 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Smith was golden last time out against the Mariners on Thursday. He allowed just four hits and delivered six shutout innings to claim the victory. A victim of poor run support for much of the season, the two runs the Athletics scored proved to be enough. Smith has been extremely hard on both lefties and righties this year, limiting them to .219 and .240 batting averages, respectively. Smith threw a masterful complete game against the Angels on June 30.

home_pitcher_note: After three scoreless innings, Saunders seemed to unravel after Delmon Young stroked a two-run homer in the fourth on Friday night to give the Twins the lead. By the time he departed with one out in the sixth, Saunders had given up nine hits and would be charged with six earned runs, ending a string of 11 consecutive starts with three or fewer earned runs allowed. He didn't register a strikeout and hit one batter without a walk, never finding his customary command. Saunders is 2-0 with a 1.26 ERA against the A's this year in two starts and is 4-1 with a 4.02 ERA in seven lifetime outings.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez improved in his last start on Friday against the Mariners. He gave up two earned runs in five innings and struck out seven as he took a no-decision. That was far better than the seven earned runs he gave up against the White Sox on August 17 in three 1/3 innings. Righties are hitting .283 against Gonzalez, but lefties are batting just .227. He has 18 strikeouts in his 19 1/3 career innings.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland made some adjustments to his windup in the Minors during his two-week August stint, and he was extremely effective in his first start back up in the big leagues against the Mariners on Saturday. He pounded the strike zone, punched out seven hitters and gave up only five hits in claiming the victory. Eveland continues to shut down lefties with a .231 batting average, and he's much better at home (3.48 ERA) than on the road (5.28).
away_pitcher_note: Unlike his two previous starts, Blackburn didn?t allow a leadoff home run when he faced the Angels on Saturday. But the right-hander couldn't continue the Twins' string of strong starts. The right-hander gave up six runs (three earned) on 10 hits over just 4 2/3 innings in the loss. A difficult night defensively didn?t help Blackburn but he was unable to make adjustments after the early trouble. Next up for Blackburn will be his second start of the season against Oakland. Blackburn earned the loss vs. Oakland on Aug. 18 when he pitched eight innings, allowing just three runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Meyer gave up four earned runs in five innings on Sunday against the Mariners. He issued a couple of walks to lead off the third inning that came back to hurt him, and he gave up a go-ahead homer in the fifth inning to Kenji Johjima. Lefties are hitting slightly better than righties against Meyer (.250 to .231), and he's been better on the road this season.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey continues to give the Twins quality starts. The right-hander allowed just two runs on eight hits over 6 1/3 innings in his last start against the Angels. He struck out five and did not issue a single walk. It's the fourth time in Slowey's last five starts that he has not walked a batter. Slowey will try to pick up his 11th win of the season when he faces the Athletics at McAfee Coliseum. In his only start against Oakland this season, Slowey earned the win by allowing just one run over seven innings and striking out a career-high 12 batters.

home_pitcher_note: Braden, who has been recalled from Triple-A Sacramento four times this season, put together his most impressive outing of the year Monday in Anaheim, holding the Angels to four hits over his final six innings of work after giving up three hits in the first -- without allowing a run. The only blemish on Braden's line was a solo home run in the sixth, and he didn't issue a walk for the second time in five starts. He didn't strike anyone out, either, but he cruised through seven innings on 82 pitches by frequently getting ahead in the count and pitching to contact.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano allowed just one run on five hits over his six innings in his last start against the Mariners. The left-hander was pleased that his velocity is starting to continually be around 92-93 mph but said that he needs to start throwing less pitches early in outings. Liriano threw a total of 95 pitches in his six innings after racking up 107 in five innings in his previous outing. He'll see if he can extend deeper in his next start against the A's. It will be Liriano's first trip to Oakland since he lasted just 2/3 of an inning and gave up six runs back on April 24, which earned him a demotion back to Triple-A Rochester.

home_pitcher_note: With the exception of an early-game stretch during which he struck out three consecutive batters, Smith was battered on Tuesday in Anaheim, where the Angels appeared to square up the ball far more often than not. Smith allowed five runs on 10 hits and two walks while striking out three over six innings and became the first Oakland rookie to lose 13 games since Matt Keough lost 15 in 1978. Smith has only won once in 10 starts since June 30, but that's in part the result of poor run support. The A's didn't score while he was on the mound on Tuesday, and he's gotten two runs of support or less 19 times in 26 starts this year. Smith leads the Majors with 15 pickoffs.
away_pitcher_note: Baker had to work in his last outing to deliver a quality start. Despite giving up 10 hits and three walks over his 6 2/3 innings, the right-hander allowed just three runs to the Mariners while picking up the loss. It ended a streak of five straight no-decisions for Baker. He'll close out the West Coast swing of the Twins 14-game road trip with his first start of the season against Oakland. In two career starts vs. the Athletics, Baker is 2-0 with a 4.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke again pitched well without getting a victory last Tuesday night against the Rangers. The only run he gave up was unearned. In fact, in his last three starts, just one of the eight runs charged against him has been earned. Greinke was limited to six innings as he ran up 101 pitches by working out of two jams. He took a lined shot off his right foot in the fifth inning but stayed in the game and expected the bruise to heal in time for this start. Greinke has faced the A's twice this year, winning his last effort on July 28, 4-2, with 7 1/3 strong innings.
away_pitcher_note: The A's staked Gonzalez to a 6-0 lead after two innings against the host Angels his last time out, but he struggled with his command and coughed up four runs in the fourth inning before being pulled with nobody out. Gonzalez, a rookie who throws his fastball in the low 90s but has only five big league starts under his belt, gave up three hits, walked five and hit a batter against the Halos, throwing only 42 of his 81 pitches for strikes. Gonzalez has never faced the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister pitched well on Wednesday night against the Rangers, giving up just three runs in 6 2/3 innings. But he lost, 3-2, when he dropped a popup and the winning run scored. His last victory came on June 23, way back in Interleague Play against Colorado, and he's 0-8 in 11 starts since. Bannister has gone back to basics, throwing his cut fastball aggressively and pounding the strike zone. It's worked well in his last two starts -- he had a career-high eight strikeouts against the Rangers -- and gives him hope for ending his drought. He's faced the A's twice this year, going 0-1 with a 6.30 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: A short stint in Triple-A during August has turned Eveland's performance around. Before being sent down, he had been 1-3 with an 8.36 ERA. In two starts since then -- thanks to a simplified motion that no longer begins with his arms above his head but instead leaves them at his waist -- Eveland has allowed just three runs and only 14 baserunners in 14 innings for an ERA of 1.93.

home_pitcher_note: Davies zipped through four scoreless innings on Friday night at Detroit, then ran into serious trouble. The Tigers scored six runs in the fifth inning, and, although four were unearned, they still clipped Davies for six hits in the inning. Davies didn't make it out of the inning and took his fourth straight loss. This is the first time he's scheduled to face the A?s this season. In his career, he's 0-1 with a 5.06 ERA in two games against them.
away_pitcher_note: Meyer, 27, made his big league debut with the Braves in 2004 and was part of the Tim Hudson trade that winter before battling through injuries for most of the 2005 and 2006 season. He's pitched in 16 games for the A's over the past two seasons while shuttling back and forth between Oakland and Triple-A Sacramento, including three callups this season since Aug. 3. Meyer, who hasn't faced the Royals this year, started against the Twins last Friday and gave up six runs (two earned) on four hits and two walks over 1 2/3 innings. He was optioned to Double-A Midland the following day and recalled when rosters expanded Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Waters has gotten a stiff test in his past three starts, going against probable postseason teams Tampa Bay, Chicago and Boston. The southpaw completed five innings in two of those three outings but has done that just three times in his first six starts. Waters has allowed fewer than three runs in just two of his first six outings.
away_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive start, Braden put together a solid outing, but this time he came out on the losing end. Braden went six innings on Saturday, allowing two runs, on seven hits while striking out two against the Minnesota Twins. Braden, who was consistently in the strike zone, pitched to contact and walked just two batters against the AL Central-leading Twins. Braden's only mistake came in the fifth inning, when he gave up a mammoth two-run homer to Denard Span, ultimately costing him the game.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera will return from his six-game suspension in time to start the first game of a doubleheader against Oakland. The right-hander has racked up an 8.02 ERA and a 1.95 WHIP in eight starts since the All-Star break, a run that caused the team to run him through a magnetic resonance imaging test after his last outing. Cabrera was given a clean bill of health and got six extra days to heal up, courtesy of his league-mandated suspension.
away_pitcher_note: Smith has lost more games than anyone since Tom Candiotti lost 16 for the A's in 1998. The won-loss record has been affected by a lack of run support. The A's have scored one run or fewer in 16 of his 27 starts. Smith allowed eight runs on seven hits in five innings in a loss to the Minnesota Twins on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Miner ended up with a no-decision in previous outing -- on Wednesday against the Angels -- giving up five runs on eight hits over six innings. It was just his third non-quality outing out of nine starts since joining the Tigers rotation a month and a half ago. Miner is trying to make his case for a full-time starting spot. Whether he does depends a lot on what happens with other Tigers starters in the offseason, but his performance down the stretch is the part of that equation he can control. Miner's only outing against the A's this season was a June relief appearance at Oakland, where he suffered a blown save while allowing a hit and two walks over 1 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, a rookie with a live fastball and good breaking stuff, has struggled with him command since being called up from Triple-A in August and hasn't won since Aug. 12. In his past two outings, including a loss to the Royals on Tuesday, Sept. 2, Gonzalez has walked eight and allowed seven earned runs over seven innings of work. He only gave up two hits over four innings in Kansas City, but both of the hits were long home runs on balls that missed their intended spots by at least two feet. Gonzalez, 22, has never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson will make a spot start on Tuesday for Kenny Rogers, who has been bothered by a sore hip, according to manager Jim Leyland. Robertson is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in two starts against the A's this year. The left-hander last started on Aug. 20, giving up six earned runs in 3 2/3 innings against Texas. He made three relief appearances after being moved to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland felt his stuff in his last start against Kansas City was as good as he's had all year. But a few bleeders and bloopers in the third inning resulted in four runs for the Royals. That was all Eveland surrendered in his six innings and he reached that juncture on 83 pitches. Eveland was able to locate all four of his pitches and pounded the strike zone. It was his third encouraging start since returning from Triple-A Sacramento on Aug. 21.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga's season-long struggles against the Twins continued on Friday, as he surrendered a Justin Morneau grand slam in a 10-2 Tigers loss. Galarraga went six innings and allowed six earned runs, walking six, his career high. He is now 0-4 against Minnesota and 12-1 against the rest of the league this season. Galarraga will next face the A's, to whom he gave up three earned runs in three innings on June 3 in a relief appearance during a 5-4 Tigers loss.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher, who was acquired in the July trade that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to the Cubs, has been on the disabled list since getting shelled by the Twins on Aug. 19, and complaining of a dead arm. His arm looked awfully lively on Sept. 4, however, as he threw five shutout innings for Oakland's Triple-A affiliate in a playoff game, allowing three hits while striking out four and walking two. Gallagher, who throws a mid-90s fastball when he's 100 percent, won his Oakland debut on July 11 but went winless in six starts before going to the DL. He's never faced the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Despite not feeling 100 percent in his last start, Braden turned in a performance that was good enough to result in his fifth win of the season. Braden was buoyed by 11 runs of support -- five of which came on bases-loaded walks surrendered by Orioles pitchers -- but he was able to get through five innings, allowing just one earned run on four hits and one walk. Braden tallied three strikeouts and said after the game that he felt good enough physically that he could have potentially gone deeper into the game. Braden is 1-0 this season against the Tigers. In his start against Detroit on Aug. 8, Braden held the Tigers to two runs on five hits and one walk over seven innings en route to a 4-2 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert earned a spot in the Rangers' rotation for the month of September by pitching seven scoreless innings in a 1-0 victory over the Mariners on Wednesday. He allowed seven hits, did not walk a batter and struck out four. He is now 1-2 with a 5.51 ERA in three starts. He has a 9.55 ERA on the road. He made one relief appearance earlier this year against the Athletics at home and pitched four scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Smith provided what manager Bob Geren called his best performance in a long time -- seven innings of three-hit, five-walk, scoreless ball against the Orioles en route to a 5-1 victory. It was the left-hander's first win since Aug. 21 but just his second since June 30. Smith still had some problems with control, walking five, but he was able to keep the Orioles away from home plate. Moving to the middle of the rubber, from the first-base side, has helped the left-hander improve his control a bit, as has the more frequent incorporation of his breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Red Sox, 15-8, on Sunday by allowing four runs in six innings, and he is now 5-1 with a 4.79 ERA in his past seven starts. He is 3-1 with a 6.65 ERA in four starts on the road. One of those victories came against the Athletics on July 26. Pitching against Justin Duchscherer, Harrison allowed three runs, one earned, in five innings, and the Rangers won, 9-4. Opponents are hitting .304 off him.

home_pitcher_note: Outman will make his first big league start. He has made two relief appearances since being called up from Triple-A Sacramento on Sept. 2.
away_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Feldman will make his first start since Aug. 30 and probably his final start of the season. He has thrown 133 2/3 innings for the Rangers this season and another 12 2/3 innings in the Minor Leagues. The Rangers would like to cut him off before he overdoes it in his first full season as a starter. He is 1-3 with a 5.63 ERA in his past seven starts. He is 4-4 with a 5.64 ERA in 11 starts on the road, and he is 1-1 with a 2.95 ERA in three starts against Oakland this year.

home_pitcher_note: In four starts since being recalled from Triple-A Sacramento, Eveland, who was sent down Aug. 3 to work on his mechanics and command, has shown dramatic improvement. His last time out, on Tuesday at Detroit, he held the powerful Tigers lineup to two runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings but didn't factor in the decision. Eveland, who needs to spot the ball to be effective despite a heavy, low- to mid-90s fastball, hasn't lost since returning to the A's, but he's 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in two career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla came off the disabled list on Tuesday and beat the Mariners, 7-3, holding them to one unearned run in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed six hits and a walk while striking out five. He is 3-2 with a 5.01 ERA in eight starts since the All-Star break while dealing with inflammation in his neck and a strained left hamstring. He is 3-4 with a 4.57 ERA in 11 starts at home. Padilla is 2-0 with a 4.63 ERA in two starts against the Athletics this season, and 5-1 with a 4.65 ERA in 11 games against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher, who had been on the disabled list since Aug. 20 with arm fatigue, was activated in Detroit on Sept. 10 and had a strange and short but effective outing, reaching 95 mph on the stadium radar gun. Acquired from the Cubs in the deal that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to Chicago, Gallagher walked three and stuck out three in the first inning against the Tigers at Comerica Park, setting the tone for a four-inning stint in which he walked six and struck out six without allowing a hit or a run. A rookie, Gallagher faced the Angels in his Oakland debut and held the Halos to two runs on two hits over seven innings on July 11.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey, the ace, got a little extra time to refresh and re-energize after the Angels clinched the AL West title on Wednesday. He'll be working on nine days rest after yielding nine earned runs in 12 innings over his past two starts, most recently surrendering five earned runs in seven innings in Chicago on Sept. 6. The big Texan always seems to get pumped for division rival Oakland. He's 2-0 with a 1.13 ERA against the A's this season and 14-3 with a 2.67 ERA in 25 lifetime starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: After throwing seven shutout innings in a Sept. 6 win at Baltimore, Smith was tagged for his 15th loss by the Texas Rangers in his last outing. Getting his pitches up in the zone, Smith gave up six runs on seven hits over 5 2-3 innings. It was the eighth loss in the last 10 decisions for Smith, who also has struggled for run support. The A's have been unable to score for him 10 times in his 29 starts.
away_pitcher_note: A forced break, caused by cuts on two fingers on his pitching hand, served Weaver well in his start against the Mariners on Thursday night. Strong after a 12-day layoff, Weaver threw six scoreless innings, surrendering three hits and three walks while striking out three. He reported no issues with the hand and said he's ready to deliver quality work down the stretch. It was his best performance since early July. Weaver is 0-1 with a 2.57 ERA in one start against the A's this season and 2-2 in six career outings with a 2.72 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Outman effectively mixed breaking balls with a 95 mph fastball in winning his first Major League start last week, holding Texas to a run in a strong five-inning outing. He stayed aggressive throughout, consistently going after the tough Rangers lineup. Outman has spent time in the bullpen, but Manager Bob Geren said he thinks Outman has the velocity and pitching array to stake his claim in the A's rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders pitched well against the Mariners on Friday but was saddled with a no-decision and still has won just one start since Aug. 1. Saunders allowed three earned runs on eight hits over seven innings while striking out five and walking one against Seattle. He's suffered from a lack of run support as the Angels have averaged just 3.9 runs per game in his last eight starts. The left-hander is 4-2 with a 5.18 ERA in eight career starts against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland labored through five innings against the Rangers on Sunday. The lefty allowed three runs on four hits while striking out six en route to a no-decision. Eveland said he felt a little out of sync, and he had to battle just to keep the team close. He gave up two RBI doubles to Nelson Cruz. Eveland, who has now thrown 30 more innings then his previous career high, said he feels like he's wearing down a bit. He is 3-0 with a 3.57 ERA in three starts against Seattle this season.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed ace makes his fourth attempt at winning his 10th game of the season as the Mariners try to keep from becoming the second team in franchise history to play an entire season without a double-digit winner. Hernandez has pitched plenty of games that were worthy of victory, but lack of run support has been an Achilles' heel for the 22-year-old. He has the second-lowest run support average in the AL this season (3.9).

home_pitcher_note: Saarloos will be making his first Major League start in more than a year, forced into emergency duty because All-Star Justin Duchscherer, who was hoping to be activated from the disabled list Saturday after spending a month on the shelf with inflammmation in his surgically repaired right hip, had to stop throwing after 10 pitches in a simulated game Thursday. Saarloos, who spent last season in the Reds organization, was promoted from Triple-A Sacramento on Aug. 18 for his second stint of the year with Oakland. A soft-tosser who doesn't get many strikeouts, Saarloos has tremendous movement on his pitches and gets a ton of ground balls with his two-seam fastball when he's on his game.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is coming off an encouraging outing at Kansas City. Although he wound up taking a loss, Silva allowed just two earned runs on eight hits through 5 1/3 innings. Silva did not allow a walk after issuing four in his previous start against Texas. He now has 58 zero-walk starts since 2004. Only Greg Maddux (67) has more over that span.

home_pitcher_note: A hard-throwing rookie who was acquired in the July trade that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to the Cubs, Gallagher put together the best start of his career on Tuesday against the visiting Angels. Coming off a strange outing in Detroit, where he threw four hitless innings but walked six and was lifted with a pitch count of 88, Gallagher didn't walk a batter over seven innings of four-hit work while striking out six to beat the Angels. Armed with a fastball that hits 95 on the radar gun and an above-average changeup and curveball, Gallagher, 22, will be making his first career start against the M's.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow will be making his fourth career start as he works through the transitional phase involved with going from reliever to starter. He took a step back last Tuesday in Kansas City, working just four innings and surrendering six earned runs. Morrow cited poor mechanics for that performance and hopes to have the flaws worked out so that he can go deeper in the game. Morrow threw two wild pitches in Kansas City, which underscored the mechanical problems. Over his previous 49 1/3 innings, Morrow had three wild pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood didn't get the victory his last time out, but he definitely pitched worthy of one for 5 1/3 innings. That was the span he went without allowing a single baserunner. Six of the 16 straight batters he retired were by way of strikeouts. However, he allowed a run in the first inning and three more in his seventh and final inning to put a damper on his outing. It's now been three starts since Millwood earned his last victory on Aug. 31. He'll try again Monday against the Athletics, whom he is 1-0 against in two starts this season with a 1.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Smith entered his most recent start with the lowest run support in the Majors at 2.82 runs per nine innings. Despite seeing that number shrink, Smith was in line to beat the 2008 American League West champions until Mark Teixeira's two-run homer in the ninth inning gave the Angels a 2-1 lead that they lost in the bottom half of the frame. Less than a month after being tagged for 10 hits by the Angels in Anaheim, Smith held the Halos to four hits and a walk over six efficient innings Wednesday in Oakland. Smith, a rookie who leads the Majors with 15 pickoffs this season, is 0-2 with a 7.15 ERA in four starts against Texas this season.

home_pitcher_note: After a perfect first inning, Nippert quickly fell apart in his last outing. He let the first two hitters reach base in the second inning to put him in the stretch. He said he felt a little uncomfortable in the stretch and once he began to struggle, he started thinking about his mechanics too much and his start continued on a downward path. His discomfort showed, lasting only 4 1/3 innings and allowing five runs on six hits and four walks. Against Oakland this season, he's 1-0 with a 1.00 ERA and 10 strikeouts to six walks.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired in the July trade that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies, Outman had a sloppy outing on Thursday at home against the Angels, allowing three runs on six hits and three walks while throwing 93 pitches in 4 1/3 innings. A rookie who throws up to 95 mph, Outman was making his second big league start against the Angels, who took a patient approach that paid off. In his first career start, Outman, who opened the year with Philadelphia's Double-A affiliate, beat the Rangers at home, allowing one run on four hits in five innings.

away_pitcher_note: Eveland, who was in the Minors less than a month ago to work on his command, had the best of his six starts since returning with an altered windup, scattering seven hits without a walk while striking out seven in a crisp 83-pitch outing on Sept. 19 against the visiting Mariners. away_pitcher_note: Gallagher followed up his last outing, in which he allowed just one run over seven innings on Tuesday against the Angels, with another solid performance against the Mariners on Sunday. home_pitcher_note:

His two-seam fastball, curveball and changeup are his primary assets, but he can also bring the four-seamer up in the zone when the occasion calls for it. Catcher Mike Napoli refers to Saunders' "power changeup" as an out pitch, one the lefty can go to when he needs a strikeout as well as the four-seamer.

A bout with a kidney stone and several rocky outings in August cost him a shot at 20 wins. He was 5-2 after the break with a 3.94 ERA after taking a 12-5 record and 3.07 ERA to the All-Star Game.

Saunders had a brilliant April in 2008, going 5-0 in six starts with a 2.08 ERA. He was 3-1 against the Athletics with a 3.18 ERA in four outings. He is 5-2 with a 4.44 career ERA against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, 25, has bounced back and forth between Oakland and Triple-A Sacramento over the past two seasons, getting called up to the A's nine different times. Poised to make his first Opening Day start, Braden has a 2.25 career ERA against the Angels and went 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA in five appearances against them last season.

home_pitcher_note: Finally healthy and confident, Moseley feels he is fully recovered from elbow surgery following the 2007 season and ready to deliver on his promise as a 2000 first-round Draft pick by the Reds. He made 10 starts for the Angels last year and has 20 career starts. The big right-hander has developed a two-seam fastball with late movement to go with his offspeed stuff. He was 3-0 with a 3.15 ERA in five Cactus League starts, with 15 strikeouts against only five walks in 20 innings. Moseley was 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three games against the Athletics last year and is 1-1 with a 7.57 ERA against the A's in seven career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, was Oakland's second-round pick in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft and in 2008 was named the A's Organizational Pitcher of the Year for the second consecutive season after leading the club's farm system with a 2.61 ERA while splitting the regular season between Single-A Stockton and Double-A Midland. Ranked by Baseball America as Oakland's No. 2 prospect and No. 11 in all of baseball, Cahill earned a spot in the starting rotation in his first trip to big league Spring Training. Having pitched in the 2008 All-Star Futures Game and in the Beijing Olympics as a member of Team USA, Cahill is no stranger to pitching under pressure, but he'll have to guard against overthrowing -- specifically, throwing so hard that the sink on his two-seam fastball disappears -- against the Halos. A Southern California native, Cahill will have several friends and family members in the stands for his coming-out party.

home_pitcher_note: Adenhart has been a different pitcher and person this spring, having matured at 22 with a more confident, assured presence on the mound. He had a rough Major League debut last year, pressing and fighting his command against the Athletics, and carried his frustration back to Triple-A after three starts with the Angels. He had a superb spring and could be hard to ship down, if he maintains his stuff and confidence, when John Lackey, Kelvim Escobar and Ervin Santana return to claim their spots. He has all the tools: mid-90s fastball, 12-to-6 curve and a changeup that might be his best pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland, 25, is the most experienced starter in the Oakland rotation. Eveland, who went 0-2 with a 6.06 ERA in three games against the Halos last season, doesn't throw particularly hard but had above-average command upon returning from a 2 1/2-week stint in the Minors late last season; he been sent to Triple-A Sacramento to sort out some mechanical issues. Eveland made his big league debut in 2005 with the Brewers, who made him their 16th-round pick in the 2002 First-Year Player Draft.

A second-round pick of the Diamondbacks in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, Anderson was acquired by Oakland in the December 2007 trade that sent Dan Haren to Arizona.
