away_pitcher_note: The reliever-turned-starter begins the '09 season exactly where he ended the '08 season -- as a member of the five-man rotation. The 26-year-old from Australia hopes to pick up where he left off. He was the Mariners' most effective starter the final six weeks of last season, reeling off eight consecutive quality starts during August and September. Rowland-Smith must keep the ball down and change speeds to be effective. He had a 1-1 record and 3.94 ERA in four appearances against the Athletics last season.

home_pitcher_note: Outman, 24, was acquired by Oakland last July in the trade that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies. He made his big league debut with the A's in early September after compiling a 35-18 record with a 2.99 ERA over 107 Minor League appearances, including 67 starts, and four of his six appearances with Oakland came as a starter. Considered a longshot to win a spot in the starting rotation this spring, Outman secured the No. 5 job with a strong final outing against the Royals in the team's second-to-last day in the desert, earning the nod for Oakland's home opener. A 10th-round pick of the Phillies in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft, Outman made one start against the Mariners in 2008, allowing three earned runs over six innings of a loss.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed Hernandez twisted his ankle in the first inning of his first start and it bothered him off and on over eight innings, but he still held the Twins to one run in the regular season opener. Hernandez escaped a first-and-second, none-out jam in the first inning without allowing a run and dodged a bigger predicament in the fifth, when the Twins loaded the bases with none out. He surrendered just one run.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, wasn't particularly sharp in his big league debut Tuesday against the host Angels, but he did a nice job of limiting the damage done by the five hits and five walks (one intentional) he allowed over five innings. Making his big league debut and his first regular-season start above Double-A ball, Cahill might have earned the victory were it not for a dropped fly ball that led to the Angels' game-tying run in the bottom of the fifth. A sinkerball pitcher with above-average command, Cahill should be considerably more comfortable pitching in front of his home fans, and because he threw more than 100 pitches against the Angels, he'll be allowed to go six or seven innings if his pitch count allows it.
away_pitcher_note: The left-handed Bedard had his strikeout artistry working during his first start of the season, fanning eight Twins in a five-inning, 85-pitch outing at the Metrodome. He struck out at least one in each of the innings he pitched, but what could have been a called third strike on Michael Cuddyer in the fifth inning wasn't and the Twins' designated hitter delivered a two-run single to cut a four-run Seattle lead to a one-run nail-biter. Bedard hit a batter, but didn't walk anyone.

home_pitcher_note: In the first Opening Day assignment of his career, Braden -- at 25 the oldest member of Oakland's starting rotation -- held the host Angels to three runs over six innings but was outpitched by Halos lefty Joe Saunders, who blanked the A's on three hits over 6 2/3 innings. Braden gave up nine hits, none bigger than Howard Kendrick's opposite-field homer in the fifth inning. A soft-tossing lefty who relies heavily on command, Braden walked one and struck out three on 97 pitches. He faced the Mariners twice last season, both times in relief, and allowed two earned runs in two innings. He's 0-1 with an 8.71 ERA over 10 1/3 innings against Seattle for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Lester tries to bounce back from a shaky first outing, in which he gave up eight hits and five runs over five innings to the Tampa Bay Rays. Lester came out strong in that one, striking out five over the first two innings. This is his third career start at the Colisuem, where he is 1-1 with a 2.31 ERA. Lifetime against the A's, Lester is 2-2 with a 3.94 ERA. He hopes to perform better on the road than he did last year, when he went 5-5 with a 4.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland, the most experienced member of Oakland's rotation with all of 36 career starts, gave up three runs on eight hits and two walks over six innings in is 2009 debut Wednesday at Angel Stadium. Eveland, whose fastball rarely tops 90 mph, needs to have impeccable command to beat the stronger lineups in the American League, and he hit most of his spots against the Halos, who scored all of their runs in the same inning and got some help in the form of a dropped fly ball that was ruled a double. The Red Sox will present even more of a challenge; Eveland has faced them once and it wasn't pretty -- a two-inning outing last year, in which he allowed nine runs.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander looks to rebound after struggling with his command in the first start of the 2009 season. Matsuzaka fell behind often to Tampa Bay batters and they took advantage by pounding three homers. He allowed four runs on nine hits while walking three and fanning five. He is 2-1 career against Oakland in four career starts with a 2.55 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 21-year-old ranked earlier this year by Baseball America as the No. 7 prospect in the game, was doomed by one bad inning in his big league debut Friday against the visiting Mariners. Anderson scattered seven hits over six innings, but five of the hits and all five of the runs he allowed came in a rocky second inning. Two of the hits in the inning were of the broken-bat variety, though, and he bounced back nicely, holding the M's to two hits and a walk over the next four frames. Anderson threw 84 pitches, 50 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer labored with his control in his first start of the season, walking five over six innings. However, Wakefield minimized the damage, allowing three runs while taking the loss. Wakefield is 9-6 with a 4.17 ERA in 37 career appearances against the Athletics. At Oakland, he is 5-4 with a 6.00 ERA.

Purcey threw 113 pitches (66 strikes) and was charged with five runs, including four earned, on four hits 
in a loss. Purcey said he had trouble gripping the ball at times because of the dry conditions at Progressive Field. Purcey has never faced Oakland in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Outman gave up three runs, all earned, and six hits over 4 1/3 innings in his season debut Saturday against Seattle, getting no decision. Outman, 24, has never faced the Blue Jays. Outman came to the A's last July as part of the trade that sent starter Joe Blanton to Philadelphia. He went 1-2 with a 4.56 ERA with the A's in 2008, starting four games and making six appearances. Throughout a Minor League career spanning 107 appearances from 2005-2008, Outman struck out 429 batters and walked 211.

Toronto recalled left-hander Bill Murphy to add another arm to its taxed bullpen, and moved Tallet into the rotation. Tallet will have a pitch count of around 70 for his first start since the 2006 season.
away_pitcher_note: One of two 21-year-olds in Oakland's starting rotation, Cahill was as good as he's been as a professional in his second big league start, taking a no-hitter into the seventh inning Sunday against the Mariners. Adrian Beltre's one-out single in the seventh ended Cahill's bid for history, former Oakland designated hitter Mike Sweeney's two-out double ended the shutout, and Cahill got stuck with a 1-0 loss. Armed with an outstanding sinker, Cahill walked three, hit a batter and struck out three over seven innings against Seattle; only three of the 18 outs he recorded before the seventh were hit in the air.

home_pitcher_note: Romero wasn't afforded the luxury of run support in his last outing and he walked away with a no-decision after a strong outing on the road against the Twins. The left-hander retired the first nine hitters of the game in order and escaped a bases-loaded, no-outs jam in the sixth inning. Over 14 innings in his first two Major League starts, Romero has given up four runs on 15 hits with seven strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Unsatisfied with his quality start (six innings, three runs) on Opening Night, Braden was quite a bit better in his second assignment of the season, working into the seventh inning and holding the Red Sox to two runs on six hits and a walk while striking out three. Braden, 25, has made one appearance against the Jays since breaking into the big leagues in 2007, allowing three earned runs over 2 2/3 innings. Not a particularly hard thrower, Braden excels when he's commanding the ball to both sides of the plate and isn't afraid to throw his "plus" changeup or tight slider when behind in the count.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte continued to hold up his end of the starting rotation with a solid outing against the Rays Wednesday at Tropicana Field. In 14 1/3 innings, he has walked two batters while striking out 10. Pettitte was 2-0 with a 1.13 ERA in two starts last season against Oakland. In his career against the Athletics, Pettitte is 10-5 with a 3.27 ERA in 19 starts.

Eveland was pulled with two out in the fifth inning, charged with five runs on eight hits and three walks. He made one start against New York last season and lost despite allowing two runs over six innings.

Hell look to be more efficient against the Athletics, a team he beat just once in three starts last season, posting a 6.62 ERA against them while with the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, who worked Oakland's home opener and gave up five runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings in his big league debut, was much sharper his second time out, holding the Red Sox to two runs on five hits and two walks (one unintentional) over seven innings on Wednesday. home_pitcher_note: Cahill delivered a decent performance against the Jays in his last outing. He walked five batters and hit one, though, leading to a total of 11 base runners. The one problem that has plagued the 21-year-old this year has been location, as he has now issued 13 walks over 17 1/3 innings this year.
away_pitcher_note: Things went from bad to worse for Kazmir against the White Sox in his third start of the season. After walking the first three batters of the night, the lefty was driven from the game by a Paul Konerko home run with no outs in the fifth. His ERA ballooned by nearly two runs after he gave up six earned runs in four innings. Kazmir is 6-2 with a 2.70 ERA in 11 career starts against the Athletics. In seven career starts at The Coliseum, he is 3-2 with a 3.40 ERA. In three starts last season against Oakland, he was 2-1 with a 1.42 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old left-hander pitched extremely well for the A's in his last start. Braden neutralized Toronto's hot-hitting lineup, allowing just one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings. He walked three, struck out four and tossed 97 pitches in the affair. Braden was a hard-luck loser, though, as the A's could not provide any support at all in the shutout loss.
away_pitcher_note: Garza allowed seven runs in his most recent start against the White Sox, the most runs he's given up in a Rays uniform and one short of his career high of eight with Minnesota on Aug. 31, 2007. He'll try to rebound in his second career start against Oakland, his first since losing to the Athletics at the Metrodome on Sept. 13, 2006. It's also his first career start at Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland endured the shortest of his three starts this season when the Yankees tagged him for four runs on nine hits and nine walks over four innings Tuesday in New York. Eveland, who doesn't throw particularly hard and needs to command the ball to both sides of the plate to be successful, had control problems throughout and frequently fell into hitters' counts. Eveland made two starts against the Rays last season and went 1-1 with a 3.21 ERA, allowing five earned runs over 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine allowed three earned runs in taking his second loss of the season Tuesday night against the Mariners. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Among those other pitches, Sonnanstine has added a changeup to his repertoire this spring, which he is fast gaining confidence in the more he masters it. The right-hander's mantra is to dispatch of hitters one way or the other in three pitches, which allows him to get deeper into the games and save the bullpen. Sonnanstine is 2-2 with a 5.25 ERA in four career starts against the A's; he is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in two career starts at McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood endured what can be considered his worst start of the season against the Jays in his last outing. However, that is just because Millwood has been so dominant. Toronto launched three home runs off of him, and the four runs allowed in the start were the most he had surrendered all year. Overall, Millwood gave up just five hits over seven innings in the start. Texas has not provided its ace with support, as the club is just 1-3 in his starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 21-year-old rookie who hadn't pitched above Double-A ball before this season, struggled through the shortest of his three starts this year on the way to a no-decision against the Yankees in New York last Wednesday. Anderson allowed five runs on nine hits and a walk over 5 1/3 innings, and his fastball velocity, which typically sits between 90-93 mph, routinely was clocked at 87-88. Anderson threw 97 pitches, down 12 from his previous outing, and allowed three home runs to the Yankees.

He scuffled at times, but worked the five innings needed to qualify for a win, ending a 14-start winless streak. Silva threw 82 pitches and 48 of them were for strikes, but he kept the Angels from erasing all of the three-run lead he got in the top of the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland, 25, picked up his first win of the season Sunday against the visiting Rays with his most encouraging outing of the year. Born in Olympia, Wash., Eveland won all four of his starts against Seattle last season, posting a 2.55 ERA over 24 2/3 innings.

Both of the walks he issued came around to score, one of them on Carlos Pena's monster home run during Tampa Bay's five-run third inning. Cahill, who threw 76 pitches, also gave up a home run to Gabe Gross and surrendered four doubles.

home_pitcher_note: Jakubauskas showed the composure the organization was looking for, bouncing back from a rough second career big league start to throw a complete game in his third. Where the 29-year-old rookie got ahead of himself against Tampa Bay, he was able to focus on strike one in Chicago. Jakubauskas retired the first 10 batters in a row on Tuesday as well as the final 13 batters he faced. The White Sox managed two hits that led to two runs, but Jakubauskas was otherwise flawless in a 2-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: A 21-year-old rookie, Anderson hasn't yet lived up to the hype that followed him out of Spring Training, during which he secured a spot in Oakland's rotation by leading the team's starters in ERA in his first trip to big league camp. He was solid his last time out, though, holding the host Rangers to three hits over five innings before being removed from the game with a blister on his left index finger. Anderson said he dealt with a blister in the same area last season in the Minors and didn't miss a start, but the A's are playing it safe and giving him an extra day between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is one guy who's probably sorry to see the calendar turn from April to May. Lifetime in April, the lefty is 10-1. He'll be the first to point out that's a small sampling over a brief Major League career, but if getting off to good start counts for anything, Saunders' impressive Aprils have become a welcome sight around Anaheim. His last outing, Tuesday at Baltimore, wasn't by any means dominating. Saunders allowed 10 hits and four runs, though only two of the tallies were charged as earned runs. And when the Orioles had runners on base and Saunders had trouble locating his pitches, he simply decided to let Baltimore put the ball in play and let his fielders do the work.

home_pitcher_note: Braden won his second straight start on Thursday, pitching five shutout innings against the Rangers' lethal offense. It was a taxing outing, as Braden threw 111 pitches in five innings, averaging right around 22 pitches per inning. In fact, he threw 22 pitches in a pivotal fifth inning, when the Rangers had the bases loaded with one out in a 0-0 game. Braden has allowed two runs or fewer in each of his last four starts. The left-hander has started two games this season when the A's were shutout and left Thursday's game in a 0-0 game.
away_pitcher_note: When Loux's sinker is working and he doesn't have to rely on that pitch to succeed, he can be effective. That was the case in his last start Wednesday in a 3-2 win over the Orioles at Camden Yards. Loux went six innings and gave up only five hits and a run -- though he had to work out of trouble early and overhaul his strategy when the sinker wasn't effective. The win over Baltimore was his first since September 2006, when Loux won for Detroit at Kansas City. A win at Oakland would give Loux his first-ever winning streak in the Major Leagues.

home_pitcher_note: Giese will make a spot start in place of Dana Eveland, who was optioned to Triple-A Sacramento on Tuesday. Giese was assigned to Sacramento after being claimed off waivers and made one appearance for the River Cats, picking up a win by allowing a run on three hits over four innings. In his 10 Minor League starts last season, all with Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, he was 4-2 with a 2.01 ERA and did not allow more than two runs in nine of the assignments.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman had it going early on against the Chicago White Sox, retiring the first 11 batters he faced, eight of them on ground balls. He wound up giving up three two-out hits in the game, and three runs. It earned Feldman another turn in the rotation with Kris Benson, the starter he replaced, out on a rehab assignment. Feldman seems to pitch better as a starter. He has allowed nine runs in 6 2/3 innings (three games) as a reliever. He has allowed four earned runs in 10 2/3 innings for two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Skipping a start and working on mechanics paid off for Cahill, who bounced back from his worst start of the season with six excellent innings against first-place Seattle. Cahill gave up one run on seven hits and settled into a groove in his later innings. After a leadoff home run by Russell Branyan and two more hits in the second, Cahill pitched shutout ball the rest of the way and retired the last seven hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy was strong in his start Saturday against the team that traded him, the Chicago White Sox, allowing three hits in five innings. He had three strikeouts and didn't walk a batter. He retired the last 12 batters he faced. McCarhty did a great job of attacking the strike zone, throwing 45 of 68 pitches for strikes. He has started a season 3-0 for the first time in his career, winning three consecutive decisions for the second time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Outman turned in the best start of his young career, tossing six strong innings against the first-place Mariners. For the first time in his three 2009 starts, Outman only walked one batter, and his five strikeouts matched his total from his April 17 start in Toronto. Outman got through the six innings in 87 pitches, and 55 of those were thrown for strikes. The lefty's only hiccup came in the fourth inning, when Jose Lopez led off with a single and Mike Sweeney followed with a two-run home run to left field. Otherwise, Outman induced six ground-ball outs and three popups in his second Major League victory.
away_pitcher_note:
Richmond allowed three runs (two earned) on five 
hits and two walks against Baltimore at Rogers Centre on Sunday. He pitched seven innings, which 
matched a career high, throwing 99 pitches, 68 of which were for strikes. He has made one career start 
against Oakland (Aug. 5, 2008), earning a win while giving up three runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gallagher is making a spot start in place of rookie lefty Brett Anderson, who is being skipped after having to leave his past two starts with a bothersome blister on his left index finger. Upon taking over for Anderson on Monday, Gallagher, 23, worked 3 2/3 scoreless innings, giving up three hits without a walk while striking out three. Gallagher, who throws a mid-90s fastball, did not win a spot on the starting staff at Spring Training despite entering camp as a near lock and opened the year in the A's bullpen; he made three appearances before being optioned to Triple-A Sacramento to join the River Cats' rotation. He made two starts in the Minors and didn't allow a hit or a run over five innings while walking three and striking out seven. Obtained in the trade that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to the Cubs last summer, Gallagher made two starts against Toronto last season and lost both, allowing seven earned runs in a total of eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Tallet took a no-hitter into the seventh inning against the Indians on Monday before giving up a single to Ryan Garko with one out. He earned a no-decision in a game the Jays lost, 9-7, in 12 innings. He gave up three runs on four hits and three walks with five strikeouts in seven innings -- the longest outing of his career. Tallet threw a season-high 94 pitches in his fourth start since being moved from the bullpen to the rotation due to injuries to Toronto's starters.

home_pitcher_note: Braden, Oakland's Opening Night starter, has been the most consistent member of the rotation by a mile. He's worked at least six innings in four of his six starts and has three of the rotation's four wins. He wasn't at his best against the Angels on Tuesday, allowing three earned runs on eight hits and a walk over six innings, and given the run support he's gotten this year, he needs to be at his best to win. The A's have been shut out twice in his starts, and on Tuesday they scored once while he was in the game. One of those shutouts came on April 19, when Braden took the loss despite allowing one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note:
Cecil, one of the Jays' top pitching prospects, made his 
Major League debut against Cleveland on Tuesday, going six strong innings and giving up two runs on six hits. Only one of the runs was earned, as Cleveland's Matt LaPorta scored on a fielding error by left fielder Travis Snider. Cecil hit three batters, but did not allow any walks and recorded six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill captured the first victory of his Major League career his last time out, holding the Rangers to five hits (four doubles and one homer) and one run over seven innings. The rookie held Texas scoreless through four innings before giving up a solo home run in the fifth. He struck out four and walked none. Itg was Cahill's second straight quality start since skipping a turn and working on his mechanics. He held Seattle to one run on seven hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Recalled from Triple-A Omaha on Sunday when closer Joakim Soria was placed on the 15-day DL with right shoulder soreness, Hochevar will join the Royals' starting rotation and push Sidney Ponson to the bullpen. In six starts with Omaha, Hochevar was 5-0 with a 0.90 ERA. His most recent start was perhaps his best -- an eight-inning gem against Memphis in which the former No. 1 overall Draft pick allowed five hits and struck out nine, allowing no runs.

home_pitcher_note: Outman was unable to get out of the fifth inning in his last start against the Blue Jays on Friday. The left-hander was hit hard in the second inning, allowing three runs, including a two-run homer to Rod Barajas. Outman said his fastball was not where it needed to be for him to be effective, but his changeup and curveball were sharp. Outman allowed three runs on six hits while striking out five in the no-decision. Outman, who is still looking to capture his first win of the young season, has faced the Royals once in his career, allowing two hits and striking two in two innings of relief work.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister has made four starts since being recalled from Triple-A Omaha and has won three of them with a wafer-thin ERA. Three of six runs scored against him in his one no-decision were unearned. In his last outing on Thursday against the Mariners, he got through six shutout innings and rang up seven strikeouts. He walked just one, but all the whiffs got his pitch count up to 105. Bannister says he's feeding off staff leaders Gil Meche and Zack Greinke with good results. Against the A's, Bannister is 1-1 in five career games with a tidy 3.38 ERA. Four of those games have been at Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: While Justin Verlander is the headline performer in the Tigers rotation, Jackson is quietly blossoming into a front-line starter by keeping his team in low-scoring duels. He has entered the seventh inning with fewer than two runs allowed in four of his last five outings, though Detroit's offense has helped him to wins in just two of them. That includes last Saturday's win at Cleveland, in which he tossed seven scoreless innings. His ability to pound the strike zone is a big step forward from his days with the Rays, and it's allowing him to eat innings in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Braden turned in another solid outing -- this time against the hot-hitting Blue Jays -- but he suffered another loss and was hit in his pitching hand by a first-inning line drive off the bat of Vernon Wells. Braden stayed in the game, allowing three runs and nine hits over six innings. X-rays of Braden's left hand were negative. He has a deep bone bruise but vowed to make his next start, when the A's open a road trip on Friday in Detroit, but manager Bob Geren left open the possibility of pushing Braden back. The A's have been shut out in three of Braden's seven starts. He has received run support of one run or fewer in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: What looked like the struggles you'd expect from a 20-year-old rookie has turned into two pretty effective starts. After Porcello turned a solid sinker into seven scoreless innings against the Twins on May 5, he overcame control woes with the same pitch to get hitters out with his secondary stuff over five innings of one-run ball last Sunday against Cleveland. He didn't give up a home run in either of those outings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Braden turned in another solid outing -- this time against the hot-hitting Blue Jays -- but he suffered another loss and was hit in his pitching hand by a first-inning line drive off the bat of Vernon Wells. Braden stayed in the game, allowing three runs and nine hits over six innings. X-rays of Braden's left hand were negative. He has a deep bone bruise but vowed to make his next start before manager Bob Geren pushed him back. The A's have been shut out in three of Braden's seven starts. He has received run support of one run or fewer in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: After leading Detroit in wins last season and earning Tigers Pitcher of the Month honors in April, Galarraga is encountering the first struggles of his Detroit tenure. He has lost his past three starts with an 8.64 ERA, allowing 16 runs on 20 hits with nine walks over 16 2/3 innings. From a pitch standpoint, his last outing Tuesday at Minnesota was an improvement, with a sharper slider. Two pitches, however, cost him the game, as they were both hit for two-run homers. While he's held right-handed hitters to a .218 average, left-handed batters have hit .286 off him. He'll have a chance to break his struggles against an Oakland lineup that has yet to find its stride.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, a 21-year-old rookie, went 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in four April starts, getting through the sixth inning once. In May he's gotten through the sixth in all three starts. In his most recent outing, Tuesday against the visiting Royals, he scattered seven hits and two walks while striking out two and allowing two runs over six innings to improve to 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA for the month. Armed with a heavy sinker with late movement, Cahill left the bases loaded in the first inning and stranded three more runners in the next two innings before working a perfect fourth. Coco Crisp broke up the shutout with a homer to open the fifth, and Mike Jacobs homered for Kansas City in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann followed two poor performances with a much-improved performance Wednesday night when he held the Orioles to two runs on eight hits to pick up his third win of the season. The 6-foot-9, 280 pound right-hander struggles at times with his mechanics, due in no small part to his height. But his height also allows him to throw at a downward angle unfamiliar to most hitters. Niemann will be making his first career appearance against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher's last outing marked his first start this season after the team optioned Dana Eveland to the Minors. Gallagher took the loss in a 6-4 defeat at Toronto, allowing three earned runs on 10 hits in five innings. The Blue Jays scored single runs in each of the first three innings, including a Lyle Overbay solo home run -- Gallagher's first homer surrendered in five appearances this season. He has two career starts against Tampa Bay, both no-decisions. He lasted just four innings in his last start against the Rays in August, yielding three runs on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Shields seemed to have everything working for him in his last start Thursday night against the Indians before an error in the fifth inning led to his undoing as three unearned runs scored. The right-hander has earned his reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth innings, which is evidenced by two consecutive seasons with 215 innings pitched. Shields is 3-1 with a 4.61 ERA in six career starts against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Outman had his best outing this season last time out, allowing three hits and one run in six innings to help the A's complete a two-game sweep against the Royals. He retired the side in order four times. The southpaw said afterward throwing strikes and attacking hitters helped him pitch into the sixth inning for just the second time in five starts. He also picked up his first win this season. Outman will make his first career start against the Rays and at Tropicana Field. His only other career start indoors came this season, when he allowed five runs in four innings at Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: The two-time All-Star continued to struggle Friday, when he faced the Indians, allowing seven earned runs on 10 hits and four walks over 3 1/3 innings in a no-decision. It was his shortest outing of the season and left him with a 12.91 ERA in his past four starts. Gone is his mid-90s four-seam fastball, replaced by fastballs in the high 80s and, occasionally, the low 90s. This wouldn't necessarily be a problem if he could consistently command his pitches, but command was absent in his most recent outing. He has had success against the Athletics (7-2, 2.48 ERA in 12 career starts) and pitched six shutout innings in Oakland on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: After leaving two consecutive starts with a blister, Anderson lasted just 3 1/3 innings in his first career start against the Tigers. The defense behind him committed a season-high four errors in the first three innings, allowing the Tigers to take a commanding lead. He exited after allowing nine runs -- three earned -- on six hits, including a grand slam and two doubles. Anderson hasn't completed more than six innings since his second start this season. He has never faced the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: Garza continued to be the brightest part of Tampa Bay's rotation in his last outing, limiting the Indians to two runs in six innings. He ran into trouble in a 40-pitch sixth, during which Cleveland scored its two runs, but he lasted long enough to win for the third time in four starts. He's one of the few Rays starters this season who has given the bullpen a bit of a break, having pitched at least six innings in six of his eight starts and lasting 5 2/3 in his other two. In two lifetime appearances against the Athletics, Garza is 0-2 with a 3.97 ERA. He allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings at Oakland on April 25, which was his most recent loss.
away_pitcher_note: Braden started last Saturday six days after taking a line drive off his throwing hand. He allowed a season-high six runs on nine hits, which tied a career high, in five innings. Braden surrendered one run through four innings, but the Tigers tagged him for five runs in the fifth, including a Ryan Raburn three-run homer. Braden entered the game ranked fifth in the American League in ERA. He'll make his second start this season against the Rays. On April 25, he allowed one run on four hits in 5 2/3 innnings.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old Cahill had a two-game winning streak snapped last time out with the shortest outing of his brief Major League career. He lasted just 2 1/3 innings, allowing a season-high seven runs on seven hits. It was only the second time in his first big league season he allowed more than two earned runs. His next start against Arizona will mark his first against a National League opponent. He'll attempt to lower his home ERA, which is almost double that of his ERA in road games.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs reached down for Minor League right-hander Billy Buckner to fill this slot. Buckner allowed three runs in 16 2/3 innings for Triple-A Reno in his recent efforts to get the attention of Arizona manager A.J. Hinch. Overall with Reno, Buckner's 2-2 with a 3.81 ERA in 28 1/3 innings and has allowed just one home run. Buckner will be making his first start as a D-back and his first in the Majors since a Sept. 27, 2007, encounter for Kansas City against the White Sox, which he lost. Buckner began the season on the D-backs' 25-man roster. He pitched four innings over three games, surrendering seven runs. He allowed seven hits and walked four, striking out three.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who signed a Minor League deal with the A's in February and did not earn a spot on the team as a non-roster invitee to Spring Training, was recalled from Triple-A Sacramento on Tuesday and will make his first start for Oakland against the only team for whom he's played in the big leagues. Gonzalez was 3-2 with a 5.22 ERA in seven starts at Sacramento, his last appearance being among his best -- he gave up a run on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings. Gonzalez, 26, started last season in Arizona's starting rotation but was moved to the bullpen after six starts. He's 14-21 with a 5.97 ERA in 80 Major League games, including 35 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Haren lost a start on Monday at Land Shark Stadium, as the 29-year-old pitched three innings of one-run ball and threw 56 pitches before rain began to fall hard in the top of the fourth. After a one-hour, 36-minute rain delay, the D-backs had their second straight road game postponed. In his last official start, on May 12, Haren gave up three runs on six hits while striking out five and not walking a batter in seven innings against the Reds. He has now turned in a quality start all eight times he's taken the mound this season. In his only career start against the Athletics, Haren gave up one run in seven innings, earning the win.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in the trade that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies last summer, Outman appears to be hitting his stride as a member of Oakland's young starting rotation. A 24-year-old rookie whose fastball sits in the low- to mid-90s, Outman, who has 96-97 in his back pocket when needed, turned in his second consecutive quality start Tuesday against the host Rays, scattering three hits and a walk while striking out a career-high six over six shutout innings on the way to a no-decision. His previous time out, Outman beat the Royals with a similar line: one run on three hits and two walks with four strikeouts over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on seven days' rest, Garland bounced back from a rocky outing in a win against the Marlins on Tuesday. The 29-year-old gave up two runs -- one earned -- on seven hits while striking out three and walking one. Garland started off the game pitching five shutout innings, allowing just five baserunners in that span, but gave up a solo home run to Hanley Ramirez with one out in the sixth. He finished throwing 80 pitches and could've kept going, but with the D-Backs trailing, 2-1, in the top of the seventh, manager A.J. Hinch opted for a pinch-hitter for Garland with two runners in scoring position. In 17 career starts against the A's, Garland is 4-11 with a 5.22 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, who has been dealing with a blister on his left index finger for the past three weeks, finally got to do all of his regular between-starts work prior to his most recent outing, and it showed. Five days after giving up nine runs -- three earned -- on six hits and two walks over 3 1/3 innings against the Tigers in Detroit, Anderson, on Wednesday, didn't allow a hit at Tampa Bay until Carlos Pena's two-run homer with two out in the fourth inning. He finished with a line of four runs -- two earned -- on four hits without a walk and five strikeouts while throwing 80 pitches over six innings. A 21-year-old rookie, Anderson made his first big league start against the Mariners on April 10 and gave up five earned runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The late-blooming right-hander pitched one of his best games of the season in his last start, holding the Angels to two hits and no runs over six stellar innings. Though he walked two and struck out one, he consistently got ahead of hitters and changed speeds to keep the Angels off-balance. The strikeout and walks came in the same inning, the fifth, when he escaped a bases-loaded jam. The second inning was the only other time Jakubauskas pitched from the stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Braden held the host Rays to three runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four over seven innings his last time out, posting his third quality start in four May assignments, but he remained winless for the month in part because he's not given much room for error. He entered the game with the second-lowest run support in the American League, at 2.42 runs per nine innings, and he was trailing 3-2 when he left the game. Braden has not faced the Mariners this season; last year he made one relief appearance against them, allowing two runs in two innings.
away_pitcher_note: After tossing four solid innings against his former team in his last start, the veteran left-hander surrendered five runs in the fifth inning, and that was the final inning he worked. It was the first time in eight starts this season that he did not get into at least the sixth inning. The six earned runs matched his season high, which previously occurred on April 26 -- against the Angels in Anaheim. This will be Washburn's second start of the season against the Athletics. He held Oakland to five hits and one run over seven innings on May 2 but settled for a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill pitched one of the best games of his young career in his last outing and still didn't win. He allowed two runs on six hits and one walk, recording a career-best five strikeouts in a season-high 7 1/3 innings against the Arizona D-backs on Friday night. Cahill did show that he could put subpar outings behind him, as he lasted just 2 1/3 innings, giving up seven runs, in his previous start. He's making his third start of the season against the Mariners, having given up two runs on nine hits over 13 innings against Seattle thus far. He lost, 1-0, on April 12 and took a no-decision in a 3-2 A's win on May 2.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't the number of hits Bedard surrendered in his last outing but how far those hits went. Juan Rivera hit a solo home run in the first inning and Gary Matthews Jr. hit a solo shot two innings later for the only hits off Bedard during a five-inning start. The veteran missed one start because of a sore right hamstring, but the layoff didn't seem to adversely affect his control, as he walked just two batters.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter is being called up to replace Matt Harrison, who is sidelined with a strained left shoulder. Hunter is 1-2 with a 4.82 ERA in four starts for Triple A Oklahoma. Hunter made three starts for the Rangers last year and was 0-2 with a 16.36 ERA. He was 13-8 with a 3.41 ERA in 25 starts in the Minors over three different levels.
away_pitcher_note: A 24-year-old rookie, Outman entered his most recent start, Sunday at home against the Diamondbacks, unbeaten with a 2.42 ERA and a .190 opponents batting average over four starts in May. He stayed hot with his most impressive outing yet, working a career-high 7 2/3 innings and rolling four double plays to offset five walks while allowing one earned run on four hits before leaving to a standing ovation with the bases empty and two out in the eighth. Acquired in the deal that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies last summer, Outman made his big league debut last September and picked up a victory over the Rangers in his first start, holding Texas to a run on four hits and two walks over five innings. He faced the Rangers again later in the month and gave up three runs over six innings on the way to a no-decision. He hasn't faced Texas this season.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman, after a 6-3 victory over the Astros on Saturday, is now 3-0 with a 2.52 ERA in six starts. Opponents are hitting .222 off him for the season. They are hitting .200 off him the first time through the lineup., .188 the second time and .375 in the third turn through the order. All his victories have come on the road. He has not won in his last 13 starts at the Rangers' Ballpark in Arlington going back to last year. His last victory at home was on May 9, 2008, against the Athletics, and he is 2-2 with a 3.86 ERA in ten games, including five starts, against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Signed to a Minor League deal and intvited to Spring Training as a non-roster candidate for the starting rotation, Gonzalez, 26, opened the year at Triple-A Sacramento and was called up last week to make his Oakland debut Saturday. He worked five solid innings against the only other team for which he's played in the Majors. Expecting his former Diamondbacks teammates to be looking for a steady diet of breaking balls, Gonzalez kept them off balance by pounding the strike zone with fastballs and gave up a run on four hits before being pulled after issuing his only two walks of the game to open the sixth inning. Gonzalez, who pitched for Arizona from 2003-08, has only faced three current members of the Rangers in his career -- Omar Vizquel, Andruw Jones and Josh Hamilton -- and has allowed four hits in 26 at-bats (.154) against the trio. Hamilton is 1-for-4 with a home run.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy pitched his first career shutout in a 5-0 victory over the Astros on Sunday, allowing nine hits and one walk while striking out six. He has pitched at least seven innings and thrown at least 105 pitches in his last three starts and is 1-1 with a 2.74 ERA. He is 2-0 with a 4.30 ERA in four starts at home this season. He lost to the Athletics, 9-4, on May 7 by allowing seven runs in four innings and is 0-3 with an 11.57 ERA in his career against them. That's his highest ERA against any team.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson may have this winning thing worked out after recording his second Major League victory in as many starts. Monday's six-inning stint was easily his best of the season. He gave up a home run to Kenji Johjima, but it was the only solid hit off him all day. He allowed one run on six hits, walked two and struck out four. He pitched in Texas on April 28, taking a no-decision after giving up three runs (one earned) over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood threw a season-low 5 2/3 innings against the Yankees on Tuesday. He allowed three earned runs, but was throwing after a rain delay that lasted more than two hours. His ERA was 2.13 in five starts in April, but Millwood has pitched to a 4.50 mark in five starts in May. He is 5-3 with a 3.71 ERA in 14 career starts against the A's. Earlier this season, Millwood allowed two earned runs over eight innings in Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, who entered his previous outing -- Tuesday at home against the Mariners -- with the lowest run support in the American League at 2.67 runs per nine innings, looked doomed to another tough loss when he walked to the dugout after the seventh inning. He was trailing 3-0 after having allowed three runs on nine hits and a walk while striking out one for his seventh quality start in 10 assignments this season. The A's offense came to life with a four-run rally to get him the win, though, ending Braden's personal three-game losing streak. A command pitcher with an excellent changeup and no fear when it comes to pitching inside, Braden beat the Rangers in his only start against them this season, scattering five hits and four walks while striking out a season-high six April 30 in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Wednesday's start at Angel Stadium did not result in a victory for Floyd but it certainly did nothing to dampen the White Sox thoughts that last year's 17-game-winner is back on the right track. Floyd threw a complete game in defeat, after shutting out Pittsburgh over eight innings in his last start, basically falling victim to one bad inning when the Angels scored three runs on four hits and a lack of offensive support against Jered Weaver. Floyd struck out eight but truly impressed manager Ozzie Guillen by asking to go back out to the mound for one more inning after Guillen talked about pulling him after seven. Floyd had a 1-0 record over two starts against Oakland last year and has that same exact record against the A's for his career. Floyd holds a 1-2 ledger with a 3.55 ERA in four starts at U.S. Cellular Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill gave up two earned runs on six hits and a walk while striking out five over six innings on May 27 against the visiting Mariners for his second consecutive quality start, but the A's offense was quiet and Cahill ended up with his third consecutive loss. A 21-year-old rookie with an excellent sinker, Cahill works quickly and gets a ton of ground balls when he's on top of his game, but he's been inconsistent all season. Cahill has faced the Rangers once this season, beating them on May 7 in Oakland by allowing one run over seven innings of six-hit work.

home_pitcher_note: The burly right-hander bounced back from a dreadful start during a 20-1 loss to Minnesota last Thursday with a stellar mound effort Tuesday night in Anaheim. Colon gave up Bobby Abreu's first home run of the season and three other hits over 6 2/3 innings, striking out three. More importantly, Colon didn't walk a hitter and let the defense behind him make one spectacular play after another, throwing 52 of his 83 pitches for strikes. Colon has a 6-4 career record against Oakland and has a 2-2 record with a 2.75 ERA over four starts at U.S. Cellular Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro, 22, will be called up from Triple-A Sacramento to make his big league debut on Tuesday, and Oakland manager Bob Geren said it's not a "one-shot deal." Mazzaro, who was a non-roster invitee to his first Major League Spring Training this year, dominated in 10 Minor League outings, posting a 2.38 ERA in 10 games with the River Cats. With the exception of back-to-back starts, on April 20 and May 6, in which he allowed a total of 11 earned runs on 20 hits over nine innings, Mazzaro has been lights-out all year. In his other eight games, he's allowed zero or one earned run seven times and two runs once. Recently named the Pacific Coast League's top pitcher for a second successive week, Mazzaro scattered four hits and one walk while striking out six over six shutout innings in his most recent outing, and over his past four assignments, he's allowed one run on nine hits and four walks while striking out 21 over 27 2/3 innings for an ERA of 0.33.

home_pitcher_note: The one-time temporary rotation replacement for Jose Contreras now has become the most consistent starter among the five. Richard gave up two runs on six hits over seven innings during the White Sox 11-2 pasting of the Royals on Friday, striking out seven and walking one. In four trips to the mound as a starter, Richard has given up 19 hits in 23 1/3 innings, striking out 20 and walking 10. He also has a 2.70 ERA during that stretch. Richard has thrown one scoreless inning in his career against Oakland and has a 2-1 record with a 4.11 ERA when pitching at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Outman had a solid outing on Friday against the Rangers, allowing three runs in 6 2/3 innings, his second longest outing of the season. He tied a career-high with nine strikeouts. His previous high this season was six on May 19 versus Tampa Bay. Outman still has a two-game winning streak and is 2-0 in May with a 2.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: One mistake to Miguel Olivo leading off the eighth prevented the White Sox ace from picking up his seventh victory. Olivo's home run on the first pitch of the bottom half of the inning erased a 3-2 White Sox lead, and Buehrle left with a no-decision one out later. Buehrle struck out six over 7 1/3 innings and extended his streak without allowing a walk to 23 straight. Buehrle was 0-2 with a 4.26 ERA last year against Oakland, and has struggled mightily against the A's overall with a 3-11 career mark. That record is far and away Buehrle's worst against any one team. Buehrle has a career 41-24 record in day games.
away_pitcher_note: Brett Anderson allowed a career-high six earned runs in four innings Saturday against the Rangers. He is now 1-2 with a 6.47 ERA (17 ER over 25 2/3 innings pitched) on the road going into Thursday's road start against the White Sox. Anderson is also battling what manager Bob Geren calls a cold. Anderson has never faced the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Braden had it going on Sunday in Texas at hitter-friendly Rangers Ballpark in Arlington before a cut on his left thumb sidetracked him a little bit. Braden had six shutout innings -- he had allowed three hits and struck out six -- before he cut his thumb on a medical kit in the top of the seventh. He came out and allowed two straight hits to start the inning and had to come out of the game. The cut is not expected to be a problem for Braden going into this start.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie allowed three earned runs in his last start and took a no-decision against Detroit, but the right-hander has lost four of his past six decisions. Guthrie, Baltimore's staff ace has allowed 13 home runs in 11 starts after allowing 24 homers in 30 starts last season. Guthrie has a 6.57 ERA on the road this year and is 1-1 with a 3.05 ERA against Oakland for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, held the White Sox to three hits while walking two and striking out three over 5 2/3 innings in Chicago on Monday. One of those hits was a game-tying solo homer by A.J. Pierzynski in the fifth inning, though, extending to four Cahill's streak of winless starts. It marked the fifth time in 11 starts that Cahill couldn't get into the sixth inning. Run support has been a problem for Cahill during his rookie season; he has been backed by more than three runs only three times, and he's gotten zero, one or two runs seven times.
away_pitcher_note: Berken has been effective in both of his big league starts and may be stating his case for a long-term slot in the rotation. The right-hander went seven innings and allowed just one earned run in his last outing, and the start before that, he threw five innings and allowed two runs. Berken and fellow rookie David Hernandez are in direct competition to stick in the rotation when Koji Uehara returns.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro, 22, was called up from Triple-A Sacramento to make his big league debut on Tuesday and wobbled through the first two innings against the host White Sox, allowing two hits and three walks while throwing 48 pitches. But he picked a runner off second base and made tough pitches when he needed them, keeping the Sox off the board and buying time before his nerves settled. And settle they did. Mazzaro settled into a groove thereafter, facing the minimum 12 batters over the next four innings on 51 pitches. Pulled after a one-out walk in the seventh, Mazzaro threw 105 pitches -- 60 for strikes despite walking four. He struck out one and gave up three hits.
away_pitcher_note: Hill was impeccable in his last start, firing seven shutout innings en route to a victory over Seattle. The southpaw stuck with his plan, firing two-seam fastballs and mixing in his changeup and hard-breaking curveball. Hill had strayed from the blueprint in his previous start and was hit hard against Toronto. Now, the left-hander wants to erase that start and build on his strong outing.

home_pitcher_note: Outman, who went 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA in six May starts, opened June with another fine outing, holding the host White Sox to two earned runs on seven hits and a walk over 6 2/3 innings. Armed with a 94-mph heater that he can pump up to 97 when it's needed, Outman is the least-hyped member of a starting rotation that features four rookies and nobody over the age of 25. But Outman, a 24-year-old rookie, has been Oakland's best pitcher by a mile over the past several weeks. He's never faced the Twins in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing just three total runs in his first two big league starts, Swarzak finally had a bad inning, giving up five runs to Cleveland in Wednesday's loss. Swarzak retired the first two batters in the third inning before giving up six straight hits, including a three-run homer by Jhonny Peralta. Swarzak left the game after just five innings, the shortest of his three outings. He struck out three and gave up nine hits.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 21-year-old rookie, allowed a career-high six earned runs in his previous outing before allowing no runs on six hits and no walks while striking out four over seven innings on June 4 against the host White Sox. Haunted by poor run support for most of the season, Anderson has experienced many of the ups and downs expected of such a young hurler, often following sub-par innings -- and outings -- with flashes of brilliance and vice-versa. His command, however, has been solid throughout the season, and when he's on top of his game, his lively four-seam fastball and fading offspeed stuff can give opponents fits. Anderson has never faced the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker rebounded from a disappointing start in Tampa to deliver a solid outing against the Indians, pitching  seven innings and allowing three runs (two earned) on six hits. He struck out a career-high 10 batters in the contest. Baker credited a mechanical adjustment in which he's standing taller in his delivery to some of the improvement he's shown in recent outings. Baker's outing against Cleveland marked only his third quality start of the season, all of which have come at the Metrodome. Baker will try to see if he can carry that success on the road when he faces the A's for the first time this season. Baker is 2-0 with a 3.27 ERA in two career starts at Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Braden proved his status as leader of the A's young pitching staff in his last start against Baltimore, limiting the Orioles to one earned run over seven innings of five-hit ball with seven strikeouts to even his record. The 25-year-old carried a shutout performance into the seventh inning before surrendering a two-out homer. In two career starts against Minnesota, Braden owns a 0-1 record with a respectable 3.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano finally found a way to get himself back on track in his last start against the Mariners. The left-hander snapped a streak of three consecutive four-inning outings by pitching six innings and allowing just one run on two hits. The lefty walked four in his outing, but unlike previous outings, he managed to escape his way out of jams by not overthrowing. Next up Liriano will face the A's. He is 0-2 with a 10.32 ERA in three career starts at Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Behind a brilliant showing of offensive support, Cahill scattered just two runs on six hits in six-plus innings, walking none and fanning five. The 21-year-old breezed through the first six innings before being forced out of the game in the seventh having thrown 91 pitches, 58 for strikes. Following his 12th career start, A's skipper Bob Geren expressed delight in his rookie's continuing improvement on keeping the ball low in the strike zone and forcing groundball outs. This will mark Cahills first career start against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed sinkerball pitcher has quietly become one of the most effective starters for the Twins this season. Blackburn delivered yet another gem for the Twins in his last outing vs. Seattle, giving up just one run on six hits over his seven innings. But yet again, Blackburn walked away with a no-decision based on a lack of run support. The starter has just five wins this season despite delivering quality starts in eight of his 12 outings, five of which he's allowed one earned run or less. He'll try to see if he can capture win No. 6 of the season when he faces the A's.  He is 0-1 with a 3.29 ERA in two career starts vs. Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has won five consecutive decisions over a span of nine starts. Though he struck out a season-low four batters in his most recent start last Sunday at Florida, he's still averaging 10.8 strikeouts per nine innings and ranks among the National League leaders in strikeouts (95), innings (79), winning percentage (.833) and ERA. In five starts this year at AT&T Park, Lincecum's 2-0 with a 3.09 ERA. He's also 4-0 with a 2.54 ERA in seven night games.
away_pitcher_note: With an impressive outing of five-hit, shutout ball in his home debut -- a 3-0 win against the Orioles -- Mazzaro extended his career-opening scoreless streak to 13 2/3 innings, which passed Aaron Harang (11 scoreless innings) for the longest such streak for a starter in A's history. The 22-year-old rookie, called up from Triple-A on June 2, walked none while striking out four in his last start. He recorded four 1-2-3 innings while easily escaping the other frames without hitting any form of damage in a 105-pitch effort. This will mark Mazzaro's first career start against the Bay-rival Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson will work on his normal four days' rest, which might be a welcome change. In his last time out, he volunteered to pitch on three days' rest to keep the rest of the starting rotation on its normal schedule. This noble act didn't exactly cost Johnson, who pitched capably at Florida. He pitched shutout ball in four of his five innings, but his lone lapse made a difference as he surrendered Brett Carroll's three-run homer in a 4-0 Giants defeat.
away_pitcher_note: Outman tossed six impressive innings against visiting Minnesota in a 4-3 A's win, marking the seventh time in nine starts he has pitched six or more innings. Besides a rocky fourth inning that resulted in three runs, the southpaw breezed through the other five, allowing four hits in all while walking two and tallying seven strikeouts -- three of which went to slugger Justin Morneau. After his shaky frame, Outman settled down to retire the next seven batters to set the team up for a win. This will mark the rookie's first career start against San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off one of his worst starts of the season, but still managed to win his career-best sixth straight decision. He allowed four earned runs and six hits, walked five and struck out six in 6 1/3 innings. He lost his only start against Oakland last season, going seven innings while allowing three earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his best start thus far in the big leagues -- a seven-inning shutout performance in Chicago -- Anderson was rocked for 10 hits and five runs courtesy an offensive explosion from a pent-up Twins lineup en route to a 10-5 A's loss on Tuesday. Following a one-run showing through five innings, Anderson found himself struggling with command in the sixth and let the ball get up in the zone one too many times. This will mark the 21-year-old rookie's first career start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw allowed three earned runs over 2 2/3 innings against the Padres on Wednesday. He walked four and allowed five hits, which forced him to throw 81 pitches in that outing. Kershaw will be making his career debut against the Athletics on Tuesday. In 11 career starts at gome, he is 3-2 with a 3.41 ERA over 60 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, 25 years old and in his first season as a full-fledged member of Oakland's starting rotation, put together his fifth consecutive quality start his last time out, giving up two runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four over seven innings against the visiting Twins. He hasn't lost since May 16, but thanks in part to poor run support, he's only 2-0 over that five-start span. He left with a 3-2 lead against Minnesota, but the bullpen gave up four runs in an eventual 6-3 loss, sticking Braden, who has gotten zero runs of backing three times this year and one run three times, with a no-decision. He has never faced the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda allowed five runs (four earned) over 5 1/3 innings pitched Friday against the Rangers. He is 6-3 with a 3.45 ERA and 1.07 WHIP in 16 career starts at home. Wednesday's start is his first against the Oakland Athletics. He is 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in two starts against the American League. Kuroda hasn't won a game in three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, hadn't allowed more than two earned runs in four consecutive starts before he gave up a three-run homer to Minnesota third baseman Joe Crede his last time out. Cahill was otherwise solid against the Twins, allowing just those three runs on seven hits and two walks over seven innings. He left the game trailing, 3-0, but Oakland rallied for three runs in the eighth to take him off the hook for a loss. Cahill, who relies heavily on a sinking two-seam fastball, hasn't issued more than three walks in a start since April 18. He's never faced the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf threw five shutout innings on 67 pitches in Saturday's start against the Rangers. He was on pace for one of his best outings of the season but was taken out after an hour-and-41-minute delay. Wolf won his only career start against the Athletics, allowing three earned runs over seven innings. In seven home starts this season, Wolf is 0-1 with a 4.53 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro's career-opening scoreless innings streak ended at 17 2/3 innings Friday when the host Giants scored three runs in the bottom of the fifth inning on the way to a 3-0 victory. Mazzaro, 22, won his first two starts after being called up from Triple-A Sacramento on June 2, and he scattered six hits and a walk while striking out four over six innings against the Giants for his third consecutive quality start. Armed with a 96-mph two-seam fastball that runs away from right-handed hitters, Mazzaro has allowed 14 hits over 19 2/3 innings as a big leaguer, walking five while striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Chris Young will miss this start with an inflamed right shoulder, an injury he attempted to pitch his way through in his last four starts. LeBlanc was to be recalled from Triple-A Portland to make the start. He was 1-3 with a 8.02 ERA in five games last September with the Padres. He was up briefly with the Padres recently but didn't pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Outman, a 24-year-old rookie, pitched far better his last time out than his line indicated. In six-plus innings against the host Giants, he gave up five hits without a walk while striking out four, but the bullpen allowed the two runners he left behind to score, so he was charged with earned four runs. That marked the end of Outman's streak of six consecutive quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: This was to be Jake Peavy's spot in the rotation, but he was placed on the disabled list on Saturday with a strained tendon in his right ankle. The Padres will go instead with Silva, who is to be recalled from Triple-A Portland. Silva started the season with the Padres and posted a 6.52 ERA in two starts before he went on the disabled list with a strained right forearm. He was later activated and optioned to Portland.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson had his second consecutive rough outing, giving up eight hits and six runs, all earned, in the A's 7-1 loss to Giants. He lasted only four innings, despite striking out six and walking just one. Anderson gave up a pair of home runs, a two-run blast to Pablo Sandoval in the first inning and a three-run, inside-the-park number to Nate Schierholtz in the third, when he got the first two outs. In his previous start, Anderson gave up 10 hits and five earned runs in a loss to the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Correia enjoyed his best outing of the season in his last start, against the Mariners on Tuesday, allowing two solo home runs in eight innings in a 2-0 loss. Correia allowed just the two hits, didn't walk a batter and struck out five in tying his career-high for most innings in a start with eight. Correia continues to enjoy success with a more streamlined delivery, where he's working faster and getting a lot of ground-ball outs. "I feel good, I've cleaned up a few things. My pitch count is improving. I've been efficient the last few games. I've felt great all year," Correia said.
away_pitcher_note: Braden had another solid outing Tuesday night against the Dodgers, mixing speeds to keep batters off-balance. Braden retired the first 14 batters he faced before allowing a two-out double to Matt Kemp in the bottom of the fifth. Then in the sixth, he gave up back-to-back run scoring doubles to Casey Blake and James Loney. In all, Braden lasted six innings, stuck out two and allowed two runs on four hits. This will be Braden's first time facing the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, the A's rookie right-hander, won Wednesday against the Los Angeles Dodgers despite not having his best stuff on the mound. Cahill walked three batters to load the bases in the first before escaping the jam. Then in the second, he saw Matt Kemp reach third with one out but Cahill again didn't yield a run. Cahill did allow a run in the fifth and sixth innings, but those two runs were unearned. In all, Cahill pitched 5 1/3 innings and allowed two runs (zero earned) on four hits. The win was Cahill's fourth of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to another uneven start, Sanchez's ERA sailed north of five for the third time this season. Tuesday against the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim, the lefty yielded seven runs (six earned) over 3 2/3 innings. Sanchez is winless in his last four starts and has a strikeout-to-walk ratio of 17-to-12 during that span. He won his lone start against the Oakland Athletics last season, allowing just one earned run in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro pitched well Thursday night at Dodger Stadium in his fourth career start. He worked quickly and did not hesitate to challenge the Dodgers hitters. Mazzaro managed to escape trouble in the bottom of the second when Orlando Cabrera stole a couple of RBIs from Russell Martin with a leaping grab at short. Mazzaro gave up a home run in the third to Orlando Hudson and allowed another run in the fifth, but he pitched well enough to win. In all, Mazzaro lasted six innings and gave up two runs on five hits. Mazzaro is 0-1 in his career against the Giants.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum was at or near his best through seven innings against the Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim on Wednesday. In the eighth, however, he yielded three runs and ended up with his first loss since April 12. The right-hander struck out nine Angels and has whiffed at least seven in 11 of his 14 starts this season. During his campaign for the National League Cy Young Award last season, he threw seven shutout innings and got the win in his only start against the Oakland Athletics.

home_pitcher_note: With Josh Outman not expected to make the start because of tightness in his left forearm, all signs point to the return of the left-handed Gonzalez, who is 4-1 with a 2.51 ERA in 12 starts at Sacramento this season. Gio Gonzalez, whose 71 strikeouts in 61 innings rank second in the Pacific Coast League, has been recalled to Oakland twice this season, and twice he was sent down the day after pitching in long relief. In those two games, he gave up seven earned runs on 11 hits and seven walks while striking out 11, but his command in Sacramento had been improving all year -- his strikeouts-to-walks ratio is now better than 2-to-1.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson's ERA crept back up to five after allowing four runs in 5 2/3 innings of work against the Texas Rangers Friday, taking a no-decision. The lefty had won three of his previous four starts. Johnson allowed two earned runs on three hits over seven innings in his last start against the Oakland Athletics on June 13. He's 14-9 all-time when facing the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Braden (5-6) threw seven innings, allowing two runs on six hits in a tough-luck loss to the Padres. He finished with one walk and six strikeouts. Braden got just one run of support from Oakland hitters, continuing a trend of poor run support for Braden this season. He has received one run or less of support in eight of his 15 starts. "I've always said my goal is: nine innings, no walks, no hits, no runs," Braden said. "We go from there. I'm not the guy to talk to about the guys who are swinging it."
away_pitcher_note: Hammel struggled when his team needed him most Saturday night in a Rockies victory over the Pirates. He gave up one run after the Rockies tied the game in the second, and three runs after his team had taken a two-run lead. But six of the eight hits off Hammel were singles. He struck out four and walked two. Hammel, who came to the Rockies from the Rays, is 2-1 with a 6.75 ERA against the Athletics. That includes one start and four relief appearances. He is 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA in three relief appearances, covering 6 2/3 innings, at McAfee Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, had one of the best outings of his rookie season on Monday against the visiting Giants, rolling through seven innings on 99 pitches while giving up one run -- a solo homer to Travis Ishikawa -- on four hits and a walk while striking out four. A sinkerball pitcher with a low-90s fastball, Cahill has been on a roll of late, allowing more than two earned runs once in seven starts since May 17. This will be his first career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa recovered from a messy start against the Rays to beat the Pirates on Sunday, but not without some trouble. He had a mechanical issue in the first inning, opening his front shoulder too quickly. Although he gave up one run, he faced seven batters and had to get the final two outs with the bases loaded. He wound up going 5 2/3 innings and giving up four runs, then turning it over to an effective bullpen. De La Rosa held the Pirates to one baserunner in the third through fifth innings. De La Rosa, who pitched for the Royals previously, is 2-1 with a 2.29 ERA in three starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: After surrendering four runs in his first two frames, Mazzaro rebounded to throw four scoreless innings before being removed in a 4-1 loss to the Giants on Tuesday. He allowed seven hits, walked two and struck out six on 105 pitches, but as he did on June 12, he had the misfortune of matching up with Tim Lincecum, who threw his second consecutive complete game against the A's. This will be Mazzaro's first career start against Colorado, and his sixth overall.
away_pitcher_note: Cook allowed one run over seven innings to earn his seventh win of the season and his 59th since joining the Rockies (a franchise record). He gave up only three hits and two walks, while recording four strikeouts. Rockies manager Jim Tracy said Cook's sinker against the Angels was "as heavy as I have seen it all season". Cook has one previous start against the Athletics, which resulted in a no-decision after he allowed one run over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was originally scheduled to pitch Friday, but was pushed back because of dead-arm issues. "His arm is fine," manager Bob Geren said. "He was a guy I felt could use some extra rest. He's not hurt." Anderson tossed five innings and allowed three runs on five hits in his last start. He struck out three, walked one and hit a batter. Overall, Anderson said he was pleased with his ability to thwart a potentially disastrous inning against the Padres, when he minimized the effects of a hit batter, two singles and a walk. Anderson allowed two runs in the inning but kept his cool to avoid further damage.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello still has a chance to become just the second pitcher 20 or younger since World War II to win 10 games by the All-Star break, or at least the fifth such pitcher to win nine in the same span. But while he's unbeaten in his last four starts, Porcello has hit a little bit of a rough patch, lasting six innings only once in his past five outings. The right-hander has done a good job of controlling damage, limiting opponents to four earned runs over his past three starts despite having allowed 21 hits over 17 2/3 innings that span, but it has cost him in his pitch counts. Porcello beat the A's with one earned run over six innings May 16 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez got off to a solid enough start against the Giants Wednesday, retiring five of the first seven batters he faced with four strikeouts. Then San Francisco shook him. Gonzalez surrendered three runs in both the second and fourth innings and was chased after just 3 2/3 innings of work. He allowed 10 hits and walked two, losing his first Major League start of the season to Randy Johnson. This will be the eighth start of his young career.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga broke a 10-game winless streak last Thursday with six innings against the Cubs, limiting them to four runs on six hits despite a three-run first. He had lost seven consecutive decisions since his previous victory, on April 26, had improved the right-hander's record to 3-0. Galarraga still has some improvement to do, but he said afterward his most recent start that he felt like he made a big step and had a better plan with which to attack hitters. Galarraga's last outing against Oakland, on May 17 at Comerica Park, saw the A's knock him out in the first inning with five earned runs on four hits and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Braden needed 100 pitches to get through 5 1/3 against the Rockies on Friday, surrendering four runs (two earned) to take the loss. It's the first time the 25-year-old has thrown at least 100 pitches without going six innings or more since May 16, where he gave up six runs in five innings -- his worst start of the year. That May 16 start could be a bad omen, as it came against these same Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander's last outing had manager Jim Leyland wondering if he might be tiring, but the Tigers' schedule doesn't allow much room for adjustment until the next time around the rotation. His last outing Friday at Houston saw him throw 76 pitches over his first three innings before he settled in to nearly last six. He ended up with three runs on seven hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings, while racking up half of his six strikeouts on called third strikes. He didn't face the A's when they visited Comerica Park in May, but his six career starts against Oakland include a 3-2 record, 2.61 ERA and 38 strikeouts over as many innings.

home_pitcher_note: Huff had shown some sort of improvement pretty much every time he took the mound in his first eight starts in the big leagues, but he took his first step back against the Reds on Sunday. In five innings of work, Huff allowed seven runs, six of which were earned, on nine hits with a walk and three strikeouts. He did not have the command that had made him so effective in some of the outings that preceded this one. This would be his first career start against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching like a 10-year veteran his last time out with seven innings of one-run ball, Cahill let his youth show last Saturday. Colorado tagged Cahill, who is 21, for four home runs. The right-hander gave up seven runs on eight hits, needing 82 pitches to get through 3 2/3 innings. It was the first time an Oakland pitcher had allowed four home runs in a game since Barry Zito was dealt the same hand in a 14-0 loss to the Rangers on Aug. 9, 2006. Cahill, who hadn't allowed more than three runs in any of his seven starts prior to facing the Rockies, will look to bounce back against a Tigers team that put seven runs on the board against him across 2 1/3 innings on May 17.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up 23 runs in 13 1/3 innings over his previous three starts, Pavano appeared to right his mechanics against the White Sox on Monday. In seven innings, he allowed just two runs on five hits with no walks and six strikeouts. He induced 11 groundball outs, which is a sure sign he was throwing downhill the way he wants to. But a lack of offensive support prevented him from getting the win. Pavano has only faced the A's one other time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro did a pretty solid job of slowing down one of baseball's hottest offenses last Sunday. It wasn't enough to get the win, though, as he surrendered two runs in a 37-pitch second before settling down to hold the Rockies to one run over his final three-plus innings in a 3-1 loss. Mazzaro allowed five hits, walked four and recorded a career-high eight strikeouts. "They were able to put some good at-bats together against him," manager Bob Geren said of the Rockies. "They fouled pitches off, got his pitch count up close to 110 pitches. ... He held a good offense down for the most part." This will be the seventh start of the 22-year-old rookie's young career.

home_pitcher_note: Lee's Major League-leading streak of 47 starts with at least five innings pitched came to a stunning halt Tuesday against the White Sox. He was roughed up for seven runs on 11 hits with a walk and three strikeouts in just three-plus innings. It was his shortest outing since May 29, 2006. Lee is 4-1 with a 2.39 ERA in nine career starts against the A's, including a 2-0 record and 0.61 ERA in two starts in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A Sacramento on June 24 to replace injured lefty Josh Outman, Gonzalez issued a four-pitch walk to open his most recent start, Tuesday against the Tigers, and gave up a two-run homer on his seventh pitch of the game. He settled down thereafter, though, and got through five innings with a respectable line of three runs on seven hits and two walks.
