It was a far cry better than the excitable Gonzalez's previous outing, in which he gave up six runs (four earned) on 10 hits and two walks against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Smoltz was well on his way to victory No. 1 as a member if the Red Sox rotation last Tuesday in Baltimore, but a rain delay shortened the right-hander's outing to four innings. After mixed results against Washington in his season debut, the 42-year-old held the Orioles to one run on three hits in an eventual 11-10 Boston loss. Making his first start of the season at Fenway Park, where he has not allowed an earned run in 20 2/3 career innings, Smoltz is 1-0 with a 2.61 ERA in three lifetime appearances (one start) against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson on Monday turned in 5 1/3 solid innings in his first start since June 20, beating virtually the same Tigers lineup that pounded him for nine runs (three earned) over 3 1/3 innings in Detroit on May 15. Given four extra days of rest after complaining of forearm tightness following his previous start, Anderson gave up one run on four hits and four walks while striking out seven to pick up his first win since June 4.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett fought through four sub-par innings to open last Wednesday's game against the Orioles before settling down and setting the stage for a dramatic Boston comeback. The Red Sox ace did not allow a baserunner after Ty Wigginton's home run to lead off the bottom of the fourth, retiring the final 12 batters he faced in a seven-inning effort. He allowed five runs on six hits while striking out five, as Boston rallied for a 6-5 win in 11 innings. Beckett is 2-3 with a 4.88 ERA in career five starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Optioned to Triple-A Sacramento on May 5 after going 1-2 with a 7.40 ERA in six games (five starts) to open the season, Eveland, 25, was recalled Monday and will working on three days of rest after throwing more than 90 pitches on Friday. Sent to the Minors to work on his command, Eveland went 7-1 with a 3.49 ERA in 12 starts at Sacramento. He has an 18.90 ERA in two career starts against the Red Sox and gave up nine runs in two innings at Fenway last season.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield's record-breaking 383rd start as a member of the Red Sox last Friday certainly wasn't his most memorable. Despite logging eight innings against the Mariners at Fenway Park, the 42-year-old knuckleballer was tagged for five runs on 10 hits. In 38 lifetime appearances against the A's, Wakefield is 10-6 with a 4.07 ERA. He pitched arguably his best game of the season April 15 in Oakland, allowing two runs on four hits in a complete-game victory.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill was roughed up for the second straight outing in a 15-3 loss to the Indians on Friday. The right-hander couldn't throw strikes and, as result, an Indians team that had lost five straight and scored just 13 runs combined in those losses, hit him hard. Cahill pitched 3 2/3 innings, giving up eight runs (five earned) and six hits with two strikeouts and four walks. Just 50 of his 95 pitches were thrown for strikes. The only positive for Cahill was that he was missing down in the zone unlike his previous start against the Rockies when he gave up four homers. Cahill wil try to regroup Wednesday against the Red Sox. It will be his first career start against Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann returns to the rotation after sitting out a turn, which enabled the Rays' No. 1 starter James Shields to make an extra start before the All-Star break. The 26-year-old rookie will be making his 16th start of the season and his first since June 29 at Toronto, when he beat Roy Halladay. During his hiatus from the starting rotation, Niemann made one appearance from the bullpen in which he allowed three runs in three innings at Texas on July 4. The Rays have won nine of Niemann's previous 10 starts. He will be making his second career start against the A's; his first one occurred on May 18, when he allowed three earned runs on eight hits in eight innings for his first win at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro pitched well against the heart of the Indians lineup, but never figured out the No. 8 and 9 hitters in Saturday's 5-2 loss to the Indians. The bottom two hitters were 6-for-6 with three RBIs against Mazzaro. He also seemed to lack a strikeout pitch in the loss. After striking out a career-high eight batters in a loss to the Rockies, Mazzaro didn't strike out a batter against the Indians. He pitched six innings, giving up a career-high five runs and 10 hits with a walk in the loss. It was his fourth loss in five games. He will try to get back to winning against the Rays on Friday. It will be his first career start against Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: After posting back-to-back wins against the Phillies and Blue Jays, Garza took a loss on Sunday night against the Rangers, allowing five runs in five innings. Garza has been working on staying aggressive and not being too cute with his pitches, and he had been making strides in that direction until Sunday night. Garza has perhaps the best stuff on the Rays' staff and seems to be maturing on the mound, where he has experienced problems controlling his emotions in the past. Garza is 0-2 with a 3.50 ERA in three career appearances against the A's; he is 11-5 with a 3.02 ERA in 24 career starts at Tropicana Field.

Shields proved once again he is Tampa Bay's true ace and stopper, throwing seven-plus sharp innings to shut down the Blue Jays Tuesday night. Unfortunately, the Rays offense didn't back him up, which has been a trend too many times this season. But his performance came at the perfect time for Tampa Bay, which needed a strong performance from its rotation to stop a four-game losing streak.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 21-year-old who has struggled with consistency for much of his rookie season, turned in the best start of his brief career Monday in Boston, firing a two-hit shutout at Fenway Park while walking two with a season-high nine strikeouts. Armed with a plus slider and a fastball that's jumped in velocity from the 88-92 range to 95-97 in his two most recent outings, Anderson was in complete control against the Red Sox, who got one runner as far as third base -- on a three-base error in the outfield. Anderson has made one start against the Rays this season, beating them with six innings of four-hit work on May 25 at Tropicana Field.

home_pitcher_note: It was a truly gutsy performance by Braden against Tampa Bay on July 11, having arrived in St. Petersburg late the night before from California as he dealt with his sick grandmother. Pitching with little rest or food over the past week, he battled for six innings and allowed just two runs on five hits to earn his seventh win of the year. And, finally, the offense gave him some support. The 3.47 runs per game in support of Braden are the lowest in the American League. The start also marked his eighth consecutive in which he allowed three earned runs or fewer -- an impressive tally to take into the second half of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Santana has struggled to recapture his form of 2008 when he was among the AL's most dominant starters, finishing second in strikeouts and fourth in innings pitched. He hasn't made it past five innings in his past three starts, giving up a total of 15 earned runs in 13 2/3 innings. He was touched for five earned runs in four innings on seven hits by the Rangers in his most recent outing on July 8. Santana has dominated the A's in his career. He's 9-1 in 14 games, 13 as a starter, with a 1.36 ERA. He's 4-0 with a 1.50 ERA in six career starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was roughed up for three straight outings heading into the All-Star break. In a 15-3 loss to Cleveland on July 3, the right-hander couldn't throw strikes and, as result, an Indians team that had lost five straight and scored just 13 runs combined in those losses, hit him hard. Cahill pitched 3 2/3 innings, giving up eight runs (five earned) and six hits with two strikeouts and four walks. Against Boston, he allowed four hits and four runs in 5 1/3, while walking three and surrendering two home runs. He has 41 walks in 98 1/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders showed signs of emerging from a recent funk against the Yankees on July 10 but still gave up five earned runs across five innings, yielding nine hits and two walks while striking out three batters. In his past 14 innings, he has been rocked for 18 earned runs and 22 hits, walking 10 while striking out seven. It has been attributed largely to command flaws, with nothing physically bothering him. He's 7-2 in 11 career starts against the A's with a 3.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro has lost five straight decisions after blanking his first two opponents. The rookie pitched decently against Tampa Bay on July 10, but the offense gave him no support and he ended up on the short end once again. He allowed two runs in five innings. A's manager Bob Geren said he liked the way the rookie battled and has seen improvement in his changeup and command. He expects better things to come for Mazzaro in the second half and believes the wins will start to fall in line.
away_pitcher_note: His teammates felt the cross-firing right-hander was worthy of an All-Star spot with his consistently superb work, leading the staff with 120 1/3 innings and 104 strikeouts along with his 10 wins. Weaver has yielded 13 earned runs in his past 18 1/3 innings, his ERA rising from 2.65 to 3.22. He's 2-2 with a 2.56 ERA in seven career outings against the A's and 1-1 in five starts with a 2.48 ERA in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson was cruising on July 12 against Tampa Bay until being lifted after four innings for precautionary reasons with lower back stiffness. A's manager Bob Geren insisted it wasn't too concerning an injury, and the All-Star break will give the 21-year-old some extra time to rest. Anderson has seemingly found his groove recently, allowing just one earned run in his last 18 1/3 innings. He followed up his masterful performance vs. Boston with four shutout innings against Tampa Bay before the back flared up. He'll be one to watch in the second half as he develops confidence and experience in his rookie season.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey headed into the All-Star break on a positive note, delivering one of his finest efforts of the first half against the Yankees on Sunday. He yielded two earned runs on six hits and three walks with six strikeouts across seven innings, outdueling CC Sabathia. Lackey has 43 strikeouts in his past 41 2/3 innings and has made it through at least seven innings in eight of his 12 starts after coming back from a forearm strain that cost him the first five weeks. Lackey is 14-4 with a 2.80 ERA in 26 career outings against the A's and 7-3 with a 3.15 ERA in 14 starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez hasn't started since July 5 after getting skipped in the rotation for the return of Dallas Braden off the bereavement list. He did pitch out of the bullpen against Tampa Bay and allowed one run in one inning. His last start against Cleveland was very solid: six innings, six hits, two runs and eight strikeouts for his first win of the season. The 23-year-old left-hander has the potential to be a very solid back-of-the-rotation starter for the A's in the second half.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn established himself as Minnesota's ace in the first half of the season, and he'll be looking to continue that success after the All-Star break. Even on a night when he didn't have his best stuff, Blackburn was efficient enough to get the win last Friday against the White Sox. He allowed four runs on nine hits through seven innings one start after throwing his third complete game of the season. Blackburn is 0-1 lifetime in three games against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Thursday wasn't Braden's night. He set or tied season worsts in hits allowed (10), earned runs (six) and innings pitched (five) as the A's fell to the Angels to open the second half. Los Angeles did the bulk of its damage with a two-out, four-run rally in the fourth. "He's usually good at closing out innings," manager Bob Geren said. "Scoring four runs with two outs is hard to do. They hit some balls hard, and others just got through." Braden had allowed three earned runs or fewer in 10 consecutive starts prior to Thursday. He'll look to bounce back against a Minnesota lineup that he limited to two runs in seven innings on June 10.
away_pitcher_note: With scheduled starter Kevin Slowey continuing to nurse a sprain in his right wrist, the rookie Swarzak will make the start in his place. In his first game since being recalled from Triple-A Rochester, Swarzak ran into a tough Yankee lineup, lasting just 4 1/3 innings after giving up four runs on eight hits. He faced Oakland once earlier this season, but didn't factor in the decision. He was hit for three runs in 3 2/3 innings in his start against the A's in June.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill's struggles continued Friday night. The 21-year-old rookie allowed three runs in just 4 2/3 innings, surrendering six hits and walking four. Things could have been worse. Brad Ziegler came in for Cahill with the bases loaded, getting a flyout to center to end the threat. Cahill has now given up 19 earned runs in 17 1/3 innings (10.00 ERA) over his past four starts. He'll look to rebound against the Twins, who he held to three runs in seven innings on June 11.
away_pitcher_note: Earning the unenviable task of starting the first game out of the All-Star break, Perkins looked a tad rusty in his last outing against the Rangers. Perkins pitched just five innings, giving up three runs on seven hits while throwing 102 pitches. It's the second successive short outing for Perkins, who had previously delivered a pair of quality starts against the Cardinals and the Royals on the road. He'll next face the A's, the only American League team he has yet to pitch against in his career.

home_pitcher_note: In his next outing, Sabathia will look for his ninth victory in 12 decisions as he draws an afternoon start against the Orioles. The lefty came away a winner on Saturday against the Tigers, hurling seven scoreless innings while scattering five hits, walking three and striking out four. He said he was too strong early in the outing but eventually settled in, outdueling Justin Verlander.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro's last start didn't exactly go according to plan, as the rookie gave up eight runs on 10 hits in three-plus innings against the Angels. Four of the runs were unearned, though, as Oakland committed four errors -- one by Mazzaro. After winning his first two starts, Mazzaro is winless in his past seven, and he has a 6.75 ERA in his past four starts. The 22-year-old will hope for better luck -- and some better defense, too -- as he faces New York for the first time in his Yankee Stadium debut.

home_pitcher_note: Chamberlain is coming off his first victory at the new Yankee Stadium, having struck out eight and pitched into the seventh inning, leading the Yankees to a series sweep of the Tigers in a 2-1 victory on July 19. Limiting the Detroit offense to only a solo home run -- Clete Thomas' fourth-inning shot -- and three hits through 6 2/3 innings, Chamberlain overcame early command issues and showed huge improvements after returning home to Nebraska to clear his mind over the All-Star break. He won for the first time since June 24 at Atlanta and had allowed seven or more hits in each of his past five starts. This will be Chamberlain's first 2009 start against the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was perfect his most recent time out -- for 6 2/3 innings, at least. The 21-year-old rookie threw eight shutout innings against the Angels on Sunday. He allowed two hits, walked none and struck out six. Anderson now has a 21-inning scoreless streak going over his past four starts, holding opponents to a .124 average over that stretch. He surrendered five runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Yankees on April 22 in his third Major League start. With the way he's been rolling lately, odds are Anderson has a different outcome in mind this time.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte hurled 7 1/3 innings of one-run ball on July 20 and happily took a no-decision in New York's 2-1 win over the Orioles. Nick Markakis took Pettitte deep for a solo homer in the first inning, but Pettitte dusted off his briefly-abandoned cutter as Baltimore managed little else against the veteran left-hander. He left to a warm ovation in the eighth after tying his longest start of the year, posting a season-high eight strikeouts and scattering six hits while walking two. Pettitte beat the A's on April 21 at Yankee Stadium, allowing two runs on nine hits over seven innings in a 5-3 New York win.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez followed up the best start of his career -- two earned runs and eight strikeouts in six innings at Cleveland -- with his worst. The 23-year-old allowed a career-high 11 earned runs in just 2 2/3 innings against Minnesota on Monday. He's the first Oakland pitcher to surrender that many runs in a game since Barry Zito gave up 11 in 3 2/3 innings at Tampa Bay on April 9, 2005. This will be his first career start against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Mitre gave the Yankees exactly what they needed out of the fifth starter spot on Tuesday. Making his first appearance in the Majors since September 2007, the right-hander allowed three earned runs in 5 2/3 innings and picked up the victory against the Orioles. Manager Joe Girardi has given Mitre a vote of confidence and said Mitre will remain in the rotation for the foreseeable future.
away_pitcher_note: Braden bounced back from a rough July 16 showing against the Halos (six earned on 10 hits in five innings) by tossing seven innings of two-run ball against Minnesota on Tuesday. He allowed five hits and walked four. Braden has never faced the Yankees. He's 2-4 with a 3.42 ERA in nine road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett was displeased with himself in his last start, giving up four runs and seven hits over eight innings. Nonetheless, it was a complete game for Beckett, giving him a career-high of three on the season. In four July starts, Beckett is 2-1 with a 3.23 ERA. Beckett has been brilliant at home, going 6-0 with a 2.44 ERA in nine starts. The right-hander beat the Athletics on July 7, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill's impressive, bounce-back showing against the Twins on Wednesday went somewhat lost in the middle of Oakland's offensive barrage in a 16-1 win. On July 17 against the Halos, Cahill allowed three earned and 10 to reach base in 4 2/3 innings before getting chased with the bases loaded. Wednesday was a much different story. Cahill gave up one run -- a solo shot by Justin Morneau in the first -- in seven innings. He allowed six hits and struck out four. Cahill surrendered four runs in 5 1/3 at Fenway on July 8. All of the runs came in the sixth as he served up a solo homer to J.D. Drew before David Ortiz delivered a three-run shot of his own.

home_pitcher_note: After performing well in his first start for the Red Sox this season, earning the win in Toronto, the wiry right-hander didn't have good feel for his pitches in his last outing -- a loss to the Rangers. Buchholz threw 90 innings over four innings, allowing six hits and three runs. This is Buchholz's first career start against Oakland. Buchholz has fared well in his eight career outings at Fenway Park, going 4-2 with a 3.02 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro's New York homecoming left a lot to be desired. The Hackensack, N.J., native allowed six runs in 4 1/3 innings on Thursday night against the Yankees and was saddled with the loss. Mazzaro had a slew of friends and family who trekked to Yankee Stadium to watch the disappointing outing. He has now lost his last six starts and seven decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Penny earned his seventh victory of the season last Friday against the Orioles, marking his highest win total since recording 16 victories with the Dodgers in 2007. The right-hander limited Baltimore to an unearned run over 6 1/3 frames at Fenway Park, improving to 5-1 with a 4.02 ERA in 10 home starts this season. He has a 1.59 ERA over his past five Fenway outings (28 1/3 innings). Penny fired seven frames of one-run ball in one career start against Oakland, striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson's streak of consecutive scoreless innings was snapped at 23 in his last start, but he continued to pitch admirably. The left-hander tossed 6 2/3 frames against the Yankees on Friday, allowing four runs and striking out seven. Though Anderson took the loss in the game, he said afterward that he believed his line was not indicative of how well he pitched. One of the runs scored two batters after left fielder Scott Hairston lost a ball in the lights, resulting in a double.

home_pitcher_note: Lester continues to dazzle during a dominant run that has seen him allow no more than three runs in each of his past 10 starts, a stretch that began on May 31. The 25-year-old workhorse is 6-2 over that span with a 1.83 ERA and 84 strikeouts. He is coming off his third dominant outing of the season against the Orioles, who mustered just two runs against the power southpaw over 7 1/3 innings last Saturday at Fenway Park. In seven career starts against Oakland, Lester is 2-3 with a 4.74 ERA and a 32:17 strikeout-to-walk ratio.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez followed a dismal outing with one of the best starts of his young career. He worked 6 2/3 innings on Sunday, allowing just one run on two hits against the Yankees in a 6-4 A's win. Afterward, Derek Jeter called Gonzalez "outstanding." In his last start, Gonzalez surrendered 11 earned runs in 2 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Twice handed leads early in last Sunday's game at Yankee Stadium, Braden twice surrendered them and was fuming afterward because it continued a trend. He'd done the same thing in his previous start, a loss to the Twins in Oakland. The trend marks a pretty dramatic reversal for Braden, who spent the first three months of the season pitching like an ace but rarely had anything to show for it because his run support was among the worst in the American League. To wit, Braden on April 19 held the host Blue Jays to one run on five hits over 7 1/3 innings but was tagged with a 1-0 loss, and on May 10 in Oakland he posted another quality start againt Toronto but took a 5-0 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Richmond will likely return from the disabled list (shoulder) to make his 14th start of the season. He hasn't pitched since June 30, when he took the loss after allowing three runs over seven innings against Tampa Bay. Richmond gives the Jays another option to balance out their trio of young pitchers, and could be a key addition to the rotation if Roy Halladay is traded before the non-waiver Trade Deadline. He's faced Oakland once this year, an eight-inning effort that resulted in a loss after he allowed five runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, who'd been outstanding in a victory over the Twins his previous time out, struggled against the host Red Sox in the opener of a four-game series on Monday, allowing six runs on 10 hits and two walks over five innings while absorbing his fourth loss in five decisions. A sinkerball specialist who need to keep his money pitch below opponents' knees to success, Cahill set the tone for his disappointing outing by surrendering a solo homer to Dustin Pedroia on a thigh-high fastball in the bottom of the first inning. Cahill has faced the Blue Jays once this year, allowing two runs on five hits and five walks over 5 1/3 innings on the way to a no-decision in Toronto on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil has been on a nice run ever since allowing seven runs in 3 2/3 innings in a start against the Yankees on July 5. In the three outings since that forgettable performance, the young lefty has gone 2-0 with a 0.45 ERA, striking out 21 and walking nine over 20 innings. On Sunday, Cecil picked up a win at home against the Rays after allowing one run on four hits with seven strikeouts and three walks over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro, a 22-year-old rookie, won the first two starts of his career but is winless in nine subsequent assignments, and it took a game-tying, three-run rally in the ninth inning Tuesday to prevent him from becoming the first A's starter to lose seven consecutive starts since Brian Kingman lost nine in a row in 1980. Mazzaro, who dominates when he keeps his fastball below the knees or above the belt, again struggled with location his last time out and gave up five runs in the third inning against the host Red Sox. In all, he was was charged with six runs on nine hits and two walks while striking out three over six innings. Mazzaro has never faced the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Romero wasn't real sharp in his last outing against the Mariners, but he managed to give a solid six innings in an 11-4 win. The lefty gave up four runs and 10 hits, but said he was happy with the way he attacked the strike zone and pitched to contact. Romero has been a reliable arm for the Jays all season, and his 11 quality starts are the second-most in the Majors for a rookie. He's never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson won for the second time in as many career starts at Fenway Park last Wednesday, firing six innings of three-run ball against the Red Sox. The hard-throwing left-hander racked up eight strikeouts, seven of which were against Boston sluggers Jason Bay and Kevin Youkilis. Anderson has a 7.00 ERA in two outings against the Rangers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert receives another emergency start, this time in place of the injured Kevin Millwood. Nippert has earned a win in his last three appearances. Over his last 13 innings, he has allowed two earned runs, which has dropped his season ERA from 7.36. Against the Athletics in his career, Nippert is 1-0 with a 2.93 ERA over 15 1/3 innings pitched. His last appearance came in relief on Millwood on July 26, when he allowed one earned run over 4 2/3 innings pitched. He picked up the win in his last start, allowing one earned run over 5 2/3 innings pitched in an emergency start against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez matched a career high by striking out eight Red Sox on Thursday at Fenway Park. The 23-year-old left-hander yielded three runs over 5 1/3 innings, earning the praise of manager Bob Geren for executing a simplified game plan centered around pounding the strike zone. He has not allowed a run in three career innings against the Rangers, all of which came last season.
away_pitcher_note: Holland allowed one earned run over 8 2/3 innings pitched against the Mariners on Thursday. He was perfect through 4 2/3 innings and retired 26 of 29 batters faced. He struck out a career-high 10, the highest by a rookie Rangers left-hander. Holland's 118 pitches were a career high and the first time he's broken 100 in his career. Against the Mariners in his career, he has a 4.50 ERA over four innings pitched in two games. On the road this season, Holland is 1-2 with a 4.25 ERA over 36 innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Dallas Braden (inflamed left ankle) scratched, Reineke has been called up from Triple-A Sacramento to start in his place. Reineke is 5-4 with a 4.37 ERA in 24 games (16 starts) with the River Cats this season. The 27-year-old pitched in four games (three starts) with the Padres last season, going 2-1 with a 5.00 ERA in 18 innings. He's never faced the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla allowed three earned runs over six innings against the Mariners on Friday. It was his ninth quality start, which ranks third on the Rangers staff. He had missed his two previous starts due to the swine flu. Padilla has a 7-3 record with a 3.69 ERA over his last 12 starts and is 4-1 with a 3.18 ERA in seven starts on the road this season. He has logged at least six innings in 11 of his last 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill's struggles continued Saturday night. He surrendered six runs on eight hits (two home runs) and four walks in 5 1/3 innings. Cahill is 1-5 with an 8.31 ERA in his past seven starts. The rookie had a 2.51 ERA over 43 1/3 innings in his seven starts prior. He's given up at least one home run in his last eight starts, pushing his season total to 23. Cahill held Texas to one run in seven innings on May 7.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter allowed five runs over five innings against the Mariners on Saturday. It was the most runs he allowed this season. He had allowed five runs in his previous five starts. Over his last five games, Hunter is 3-1. He has made one career start against the Athletics, allowing three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings (5.06 ERA) and receiving the no-decision. On the road in his career, Hunter is 0-1 with a 10.57 ERA over 7 2/3 innings in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: After four straight starts without a victory, Bannister cashed in with seven shutout innings last Sunday at Tampa Bay. He gave up just five hits with no walks and seven strikeouts, finally besting James Shields who had a no-hitter through seven. To go with his seven whiffs, Bannister got nine ground-ball outs to continue his effort to morph from being a fly-ball pitcher. He threw 117 pitches, second-most in his career, so he yielded to closer Joakim Soria for the final two innings. Bannister lost to the A's, 7-2, on May 13.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro was down 5-0 before he got the first out of the ballgame against Toronto on Sunday. The 22-year-old rookie went on to allow seven earned runs on 10 hits while walking three in five innings. Mazzaro threw 13 2/3 shutout innings over his first two starts, earning the win in both contests. He hasn't won a game since. Mazzaro has surrendered at least six runs in each of his past four starts. He's 0-3 with an 11.29 ERA in 18 1/3 innings over the stretch. This will be his first start against Kansas City.

home_pitcher_note: Experiencing one of his poorest outings in a superb season, Greinke lasted just five innings against the Rays last Monday and gave up six runs on 10 hits. The only real plus was nine strikeouts, which gave him a rousing 162 in 152 1/3 innings. He had an especially tough time in the first two innings, surrendering four runs and matching his one-game high this year with three walks. Greinke has not won in six straight starts now, dating to an Interleague victory over the Pirates on June 28. He hasn't faced the A's this year, but he's 3-0 against them in his career with a 2.72 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Mortensen, who was part of the package that the Cardinals sent to Oakland in the Matt Holliday trade, will make his A's debut and first career start on Saturday. Manager Bob Geren said Dallas Braden wouldn't be able to start on Monday, so Brett Anderson and Gio Gonzalez will get pushed back a day each to fill the void.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar's first start in August was nearly as shaky as his last start in July. After allowing seven runs in six innings against Baltimore on July 30, Hochevar gave up four runs in five innings against Seattle in his last outing. Hochevar still had quality stuff -- he struck out eight in his five innings -- but his pitch count soared to 112 by the end of the fifth. Hochevar has looked like a different pitcher in his last four outings. The young right-hander has 34 strikeouts in his last 24 1/3 innings, and that's mostly been a good thing. He finished 6-2 in June and July, and he's starting to show flashes of becoming an above-average Major League starter.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson threw 7 2/3 impressive innings against Texas on Monday, allowing two runs on six hits while striking out eight. He only got into trouble in one inning, loading the bases with nobody out in the fifth. He limited the damage to one run, though, inducing a 6-4-3 double play, then recording a strikeout to get out of the inning. The 21-year-old rookie is 3-1 with a 1.93 ERA in 46 innings over his past seven starts, holding opponents to a .182 average. This is his first start against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie pitched well in his last start, when he allowed just one run in the first seven innings. The right-hander buckled for two more in the eighth, but still got deep in the game. Guthrie has allowed more home runs (27) than any other American League starter, and he's allowed at least one long ball in six straight starts and in 17 of his last 22 games.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez matched a career-high by going 6 2/3 innings on Tuesday, allowing three hits while striking out seven to lead the A's to a 6-0 win over the Rangers. The 23-year-old rookie is 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in 18 2/3 innings over a three-start stretch against the Yankees, Red Sox and now Rangers. "Those are three high quality hitting clubs," manager Bob Geren said. "He's been simplifying his whole game plan. ...It's what he needs. He's very young. He needs that confidence."

home_pitcher_note: On Thursday in Detroit, Hernandez took the loss in his shortest start of the season, lasting only three innings in a 7-3 loss. Hernandez gave up five runs, which tied a season high, on seven hits and two walks. He struck out only one batter -- a season low. He threw only 81 pitches, 48 for strikes. Hernandez has made one appearance against the A's, pitching 2 2/3 innings of scoreless relief in Oakland, allowing four hits and no walks, striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill gave up five earned runs on eight hits in six innings against the Rangers on Thursday. After giving up solo shots to Hank Blalock and Michael Young, Cahill has now surrendered 25 home runs this season -- second most in the American League. He has a 9.37 ERA in 16 1/3 innings over his past three starts. The rookie will look to bounce back against a Baltimore lineup he held to two earned runs in six innings on June 6.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Berken won for the first time since his Major League debut in a 7-5 win over the Blue Jays at Rogers Centre. He struck out six batters -- his second-highest total of the season. Berken has made one start against the A's this season, lasting only 3 1/3 innings and giving up nine runs on seven hits and three walks en route to a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro picked up his first win since June 7 in his last start against the Royals. He'd lost eight consecutive decisions before his breakthrough in Kansas City. Manager Bob Geren said he hoped that the win would give Mazzaro a confidence boost after a rough July. Mazzaro was 0-4 with an 8.51 ERA in July, before allowing seven runs in his first start in August. Geren did compliment Mazzaro's velocity and movement.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson picked up his first win in August in his last start against the Royals, allowing three runs in six-plus innings of work. Oakland's young lefty looked untouchable for most of the day, giving up just three hits through six innings. But the 21-year-old Anderson ran out of gas late, allowing three runs in the seventh. He still managed to notch his third straight quality start. Anderson allowed two runs in 6 2/3 innings on Aug. 3 against Texas, and he drew a win over Boston on July 29 after giving up three runs over six innings. Anderson has faced the White Sox once already, throwing seven shutout innings in a win on June 4.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Ozzie Guillen says he's looking for increased confidence from the struggling Contreras. He hasn't won a game since July 8, and has allowed seven runs in his last 7 1/3 innings. Contreras couldn't make it out of the fifth inning in his last start, as he allowed four runs on six hits in 4 2/3 innings in an 8-4 loss to Cleveland. The right-hander is 3-3 with a 6.00 ERA lifetime against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie was sensational in his last start, allowing only seven hits and registering five strikeouts over six innings of shutout baseball. In his last four starts, Gonzalez is 3-0, and has allowed three runs or less in each start.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd wasn't as sharp in his last outing as he was in the one prior, allowing five runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings in a 6-4 loss to the Mariners. Things didn't start off too bad for the right-hander, as he retired the first 10 batters he faced. But two runs in the fourth inning and a run in the fifth ran his pitch count up a little bit before the big blow came in the sixth inning -- a two-out, game-tying home run on an 0-2 pitch with the Sox leading 4-3. Floyd has faced Oakland once this season, going seven innings in a 6-2 win. He allowed two runs on just four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill achieved his longest outing since going seven innings on July 22, but it wasn't enough to keep him from suffering his 12th loss of the season. The rookie allowed three earned runs on eight hits, but issued no walks in his team's 3-2 loss to the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Danks finally broke out of a recent mini-slump with one of his best outings of the season, allowing one run in eight innings against the Mariners. Danks is 4-0 lifetime against Oakland with a 1.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Tomko joins the A's after being designated for assignment on July 22 by the same Yankees team he'll face Monday. He's 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA in five career games against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of his finest outings of the season, Burnett sputtered a bit last Wednesday against the Blue Jays, serving up 10 hits, walking two batters and throwing two wild pitches -- the last of which directly led to Toronto's third run. He received his second straight no-decision. Burnett last faced the Athletics last year in Toronto, giving up four runs over six innings of a victory. He is 0-1 with a 2.13 career ERA at the Coliseum, and is 0-3 over his last five starts on the West Coast, dating back to 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro picked up his second successive win on Wednesday, tossing 5 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on eight hits. Despite the win, Wednesday marked Mazzaro's eighth straight start in which he has given up at least seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia will try for his fourth consecutive victory as the Yankees play the second game of a three-game series with the A's on Tuesday. home_pitcher_note: Anderson struggled for the first time in a long time on Friday against the White Sox. The 21-year-old rookie has given up nine earned runs over 12 innings (6.75 ERA) in two starts against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Originally scheduled to face the Mariners on Sunday, Gaudin was pushed back to Wednesday against the A's as the Yankees continue to look for a pattern that fits Chamberlain's innings limit. home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old rookie issued a season-high six walks -- three of which went on to score -- in an 8-1 A's loss to the White Sox on Saturday. Gonzalez will look to regain that form against a Tigers lineup that scored three runs on seven hits in five innings against him on June 30.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson continues to struggle with consistency on his slider and other secondary pitches -- a trend that began at the end of July -- but he's starting to find ways to get results with what manager Jim Leyland calls his "pitchability." His six innings with three runs allowed on Saturday against Kansas City earned him just his second win in his past six starts. He's 1-1 with a 3.38 ERA in two career starts against the A's, including a start on May 15 in which he threw seven innings of one-run ball for an easy win at Comerica Park, but he has never pitched in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill handled the White Sox through five innings on Sunday, holding them to just two hits. The Tigers tagged Cahill for seven earned runs in 2 1/3 innings -- a career low for the righty -- on May 17.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers hope Galarraga can get back on a routine and back up to full strength after a throat infection left him unable to eat solid food for a few days and sapped his energy last week. For someone who still looked worn down and struggled mightily with his pace in his opening inning, Galarraga had better velocity on his fastball than he had in some of his healthy starts. He's 2-1 with a 6.97 ERA in six career outings against Oakland, four of them starts.

home_pitcher_note: The A's signed Tomko to a Minor League contract on Aug. 5. On Monday, he was back in the Majors, facing the same Yankees team that released him earlier this season. away_pitcher_note: Porcello's first outing after his five-game suspension for throwing at Boston's Kevin Youkilis should provide a better idea whether he's on his way to a high-strikeout finish. The hope for the Tigers now is that they won't have to watch his innings quite so closely with the time off he got from the suspension and the second-inning ejection that led to it.

home_pitcher_note: The fourth time was the charm for the right-hander acquired from the Pirates on July 29.
