Opponents are batting .324 against him at Safeco Field. Snell has faced four current Athletics -- Adam Kennedy, Nomar Garciaparra, Eric Patterson and Scott Hairston -- and held them to a combined .216 batting average (8-for-37) with no home runs.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Mazzaro got out of a pair of bases-loaded jams to hold the Yankees to two runs (one earned) over five innings, allowing six hits and striking out two. The rookie is 2-0 with a 3.52 ERA over his past three starts after going 0-8 with a 7.22 ERA in his previous 10. This will be Snell's first start against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty from Australia had mixed results in his previous outing. He was impressive in the first three innings while retiring nine of the 10 batters he faced and not-so-good over the next 2 1/3 innings, surrendering a pair of solo home runs, four walks and a double. All three of the runners he left on base when he departed in the sixth inning scored, which hiked his ERA over the 4.00 mark. Opponents are 3-for-23 against him in the first inning. He appears to be a homebody, posting a 2.-1 record and 3.25 ERA at Safeco Field this season and 0-0 with a 6.39 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson threw seven impressive innings on Wednesday but surrendered a two-run home run to Mark Teixeira that proved to be the difference in a 3-2 loss to the Yankees. The 21-year-old rookie allowed three runs on six hits and struck out six. Anderson is 4-2 with a 3.20 ERA in 64 2/3 innings over his past 10 starts. After giving up five runs in six innings against Seattle in his Major League debut on April 10, Anderson held the Mariners to one run in six innings on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start -- against the Indians -- French's offense gave him a 7-1 lead in the fourth inning, which made the lefty's night a lot easier. French made sure he didn't let down, controlling the Indians through six innings in a 9-4 win. He allowed eight hits but stayed away from the big rally, as Cleveland scored one run in the second, fifth and sixth innings. French struck out six, tying a career high, and credited an improved slider with his swings and misses. French is 2-1 with a 4.43 ERA in four starts since being acquired from the Tigers for left-hander Jarrod Washburn on July 31.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez continued his efforts in improving his command and pounding the strike zone in his last start but took a loss against a tough Detroit lineup. The 23-year-old lasted 5 2/3 innings, giving up three runs -- two courtesy of solo home runs -- on four hits, walking four and striking out a career-high nine batters. In his first start against Seattle this season, Gonzalez walked away with a no-decision after giving up three runs on five hits in five innings. He struck out one and walked four in that outing.

home_pitcher_note: Shaking off early command issues, Santana maintained his recent roll, winning his fourth consecutive start by holding the Jays to three earned runs across six innings on Saturday in Toronto. He yielded seven hits and four walks, striking out three, but was able to get big outs when he needed them, getting assistance from a spectacular defense. Santana's ERA over his past four outings is 3.33, inspiring confidence that he's recapturing his '08 All-Star form. Santana has dominated the A's, going 10-1 in 15 career appearances with a 1.35 ERA across 100 1/3 innings, allowing only 68 hits.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the visiting Tigers, Cahill gave his team seven solid innings yet extended his winless streak to six games after picking up his eighth no-decision of the season. He surrendered two runs on five hits and three walks while fanning four in seven innings before the A's went on to win with a run in the ninth, 3-2. Cahill's effort marked just the eighth time in 26 career starts he's pitched at least seven innings. The A's rookie is 0-0 with a 4.66 ERA in two starts against the Angels this season.

home_pitcher_note: After handling himself capably in his first two starts, Bell was rocked by the Blue Jays on Sunday in Toronto, surrendering six earned runs on six hits and four walks in 1 2/3 innings, striking out two men. The three-run double lobbed over first base by Randy Ruiz that ended his day wasn't a bad pitch, down and in, but his command overall wasn't close to what it had been against the Rays and Indians. Bell, 22, has jumped from Double-A Arkansas to Triple-A Salt Lake to the big time this season, and that's a lot of ground to cover for a guy who hadn't pitched beyond Class A in his first four professional seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Tomko continued his strong stint with the A's by giving up just one run through six innings in his last start, against Detroit. He has won both of his starts since being selected by Oakland on Aug. 17 and has a 0.75 ERA in that span. Against the Tigers, he scattered just three hits while walking three and striking out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver didn't have his best stuff against the Tigers on Monday, allowing five runs on eight hits over 5 1/3 innings at Angel Stadium. Miguel Cabrera was the main culprit as he hit a run-scoring double and two-run homer against Weaver. But the bullpen was the other culprit as Weaver exited the game with two runners on in the sixth and the Angels down by three runs but by the end of the inning the Tigers led by 10. Weaver is 2-2 with a 3.28 ERA in eight career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro flirted with disaster in the early innings Monday in Seattle, stranding five runners after allowing three hits, a walk and hitting a batter in the first two frames. His command never really improved, and the Mariners went the quick-strike route -- Jose Lopez hit a solo homer in the third and Ken Griffey Jr. hit a two-run shot in the fifth -- to stick the 22-year-old rookie with his ninth loss in his past 11 decisions. Mazzaro was pulled after the fifth, having allowed three runs on five hits, four walks and two hit batters while striking out four. He's faced the Halos once this season, getting torched for eight runs (four earned) on 10 hits and two walks over three innings of a loss on July 18.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey was denied career win No. 100 when he struggled against the Tigers on Tuesday at Angel Stadium. Lackey was effective early but lost his effectiveness as the game went on, allowing two solo homers in the fifth and back-to-back triples in the seventh on his 116th and 117th pitches of the game. In all, Lackey allowed five runs on 11 hits over six-plus innings in the Angels' 5-3 loss. Lackey has dominated the A's, historically, going 15-4 with a 2.66 ERA in 27 career starts against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: A 21-year-old rookie who has been Oakland's most consistent pitcher in the second half, Anderson was brilliant during his seven-inning stint in Seattle on Tuesday, scattering six hits and a walk while striking out eight on the way to a no-decision. A late infield error cost him the victory but he lowered his ERA to 3.01 ERA over his past 11 starts. Anderson, who relied heavily on his fastball against the Mariners, has faced the Angels twice this season, both times in Oakland. On May 4 he gave up five runs on nine hits over 4 2/3 innings. On July 19 he gave up two hits over eight shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, a 23-year-old rookie, carried a 3.06 ERA over his previous six starts into his Wednesday outing in Seattle but took a small step backward by allowing four runs on seven hits and three walks over five innings while losing his third consecutive start. Equipped with a plus curveball and a low-90s fastball, Gonzalez has had a hard time getting deep into games of late, working a total of 15 2/3 innings his past three times out. He has not faced the Royals this year, and last year he gave up three earned runs in four innings against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar had a frustrating outing his last start against Cleveland. He threw the ball well, but took the loss after allowing four runs in 6 1/3 innings. The Indians capitalized on two walks, an error and a wild pitch, and Hochevar lost for a fourth straight time. Hochevar hasn't won since July 25 against Texas -- a game in which he allowed two earned runs in seven innings. You might say that Hochevar has had an eventful 2009 against the A's. After starting the season at Triple-A Omaha, Hochevar made his 2009 debut in Oakland on May 12. He lasted just two innings after giving up eight earned runs. He fared a little better on Aug. 8, surrendering four runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who was brought to Spring Training to compete for a starting job but opened the season at Triple-A Sacramento, was called up May 19 and made two starts, going 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA. His past 18 outings have come out of the bullpen, with an ERA of 5.20, but he's being moved back into a starting role because the A's will employ a six-man rotation in the season's final month in an effort to lighten the load of their four rookie starters. Gonzalez most recently faced the Royals on Aug. 8 and allowed four earned runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davies sort of wobbled at times in his last start at Seattle, but made big pitches when he had to and gave up just two runs in six innings. He gave up five hits and three walks. Davies felt he made more progress in refining his pitching motion to give him increased command, especially with his fastball. Now he's won two of his last four starts and he has 20 strikeouts in those games, a good sign. This will be his first start against Oakland this year; in his career he faced them three times with a 1-1 mark and 4.02 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill had perhaps his finest outing of the season his last time out, allowing two hits over seven shutout innings to beat the Angels in Anaheim. Cahill walked the first two batters he faced, but he didn't issue a free pass thereafter and deftly employed his sinking two-seam fastball and a changeup with good movement to produce a steady stream of groundouts. Cahill, a 21-year-old rookie, has allowed 25 home runs this year but none over his past four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Still without a victory since Aug. 2, Bannister lost last Friday night at Seattle as he gave up six runs (five earned) in 6 2/3 innings. In his past five starts, he's 0-4 with one no-decision. And in those games, he's surrendered 29 earned runs for an 8.80 ERA. That's taken his season mark up more than one run, from 3.59 to 4.60. Bannister faced Oakland once in that span and was banged for seven runs in four innings. But earlier in the season, he held the A's to two runs in 5 2/3 innings, though he lost, 2-1.

home_pitcher_note: Tomko's first start, he beat the team that had recently released him, the American League East-leading Yankees. His next time out, he beat the AL Central-leading Tigers. In his most recent outing, he held the AL West-leading Angels to four hits and a walk while striking out five over 5 2/3 innings and left the game with a 6-1 lead, but the Halos stormed back to win and stick Tomko with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Snell gave up three hits and two runs in five innings against the Royals in his last outing, but he left after five innings because of swelling in his right forearm after taking a line drive off the arm in the fifth. He finished the frame, and his day was done after just 68 pitches. X-rays were negative, and Snell should be ready to go for his next start. Despite the early exit, Snell still found his way to the win column for the third consecutive start, and he has now allowed just four earned runs in his past three outings. Snell gave up 13 runs in his first three starts with the Mariners. His only appearance against the A's this season was during the Mariners' last homestand, when he held Oakland to one run on four hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in the July trade that sent Matt Holliday to the Cardinals, Mortensen is making a spot start in place of rookie right-hander Vin Mazzaro, who has been temporarily shut down with shoulder tendinitis. Mortensen, a 24-year-old who has a 9-8 record with a 4.39 ERA in 23 starts at Triple-A this season, made his A's debut on Aug. 8 against the Royals and allowed eight runs on eight hits and three walks over four innings. He was sent back down after the outing.
away_pitcher_note: A lack of run support continues to haunt Rowland-Smith, who has experienced the feeling in his past two outings. The lefty held the Athletics to two runs over 6 1/3 innings on Aug. 25 but settled for a no-decision, and in his last start, a misplayed line drive led to three runs and a loss to the Royals and Zack Greinke, who pitched a one-hit shutout. Rowland-Smith threw 113 pitches -- 80 for strikes -- in a stellar, but losing, effort. Rowland-Smith is holding opponents to .212 (7-for-33) average in the first inning. This will be the lefty's third start against the Athletics this season, and he has yet to record a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched well early against the Angels on Sunday but had a rough fifth inning, when he allowed an RBI double to Chone Figgins and a three-run homer to Torii Hunter. In all, the rookie allowed four runs on seven hits over six innings in a loss to John Lackey. Anderson is 1-1 with a 3.32 ERA in three career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Throwing strikes was a piece of cake for the left-hander in his last start. Of the 96 pitches he threw against the Angels, 66 of them were strikes. The downside of that, however, is that too many of the strikes got too much of the strike zone and he was tagged for 10 hits and seven earned runs over five innings -- the most runs he has allowed since being acquired from the Tigers on July 31. French still needs to change speeds more, which keeps hitters guessing. The Angels were aggressive and French had no answer to get them off-balance. This will be his second start against the Athletics, having beaten them at Safeco Field on August 26.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez got off to a shaky start against the Royals on Monday, allowing three first-inning runs. He settled down some after that as he held Kansas City to two runs over his final 4 1/3 innings. He gave up six hits, walked four and struck out eight, throwing 103 pitches. The rookie is 0-3 with a 7.29 ERA in 21 innings over his past four starts. He's faced Seattle twice this year, allowing seven runs on 12 hits over 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fister gets the award for best turnaround in back-to-back starts. Five days after surrendering three home runs to the Royals, resulting in his first big league loss, the unheralded right-handed held the hot-hitting Angels to five hits and one run over 7 1/3 innings. Fister pitched ahead in the count most of the game and though he had just two strikeouts, the rookie zeroed in on the strike zone. Seventy of his season-high 107 pitches were strikes. His start against the Athletics will be like a home game for Fister. He grew up in Merced, Calif., and attended Fresno State.

home_pitcher_note: After the rookie's stellar effort against the Cubs on Thursday, Ozzie Guillen said Torres deserved another start. But the White Sox are waiting to see how they perform against the Red Sox in a four-game home set and if Detroit slips at all to decide if they want to give younger hurlers such as Torres and Dan Hudson an extended look. Torres threw seven scoreless innings against the Cubs, giving up just five hits and striking out six. Most importantly, Torres didn't issue a walk after giving up nine free passes in his previous 9 1/3 innings of big league baseball.
away_pitcher_note: After making three strong starts following his promotion from Triple-A Sacramento, Tomko struggled for the first time with Oakland his last time out, vs. Seattle on Thursday, and the long ball was his primary nemesis. He gave up a pair of two-run homers in the first inning and another two-run shot in the fourth on the way to a loss at the hands of the Mariners. Tomko, who gave up six runs on eight hits -- five for extra bases -- while walking one and striking out two. Released by the Yankees before being picked up by the A's, Tomko has not faced the White Sox this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia didn't need his best stuff in a 12-2 blowout victory on Friday night against the Red Sox, but he pitched well enough to win even if the game had been close. Staked to a 12-1 lead after four innings, Garcia lasted six frames, surrendering just one run on seven hits with five strikeouts and one walk to pick up his first victory since Sept. 17, 2008, when he was a member of the Tigers. Garcia posted his third straight quality start, but Friday was the first time he had allowed fewer than three runs in an outing this season. Lifetime against the A's, Garcia is 6-6 with a 5.08 ERA in 19 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill allowed three earned runs in five innings against Kansas City on Wednesday, surrendering all three runs in the third. He gave up six hits, walked two and struck out three to earn the win. The rookie is 2-1 with a 2.81 ERA over 32 innings in his past five starts. He'll look to keep things going against a White Sox team he's held to four runs in 11 2/3 innings (3.08 ERA) in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Blackburn pitched well for a second successive outing, but he was unable to secure a win. The right-hander breezed through the Indians lineup for most of the game, but he couldn't get out of some two-out trouble in seventh. He went 6 2/3 innings, giving up three runs on seven hits while striking out three and walking one. He has pitched much better in his past four starts and will look to keep that streak going against the A's. Blackburn is 0-1 with a 5.06 ERA in four career starts against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Mortensen, one of three prospects acquired in the July trade that sent Matt Holliday to the Cardinals, was called up from Triple-A Sacramento on Sept. 4 to fill in for fellow rookie righty Vin Mazzaro against the visiting Mariners and shook off a shaky second inning on the way to a career-high seven innings of six-hit work. Mortensen, 24, retired the first five batters he faced, but gave up four runs on four hits and two walks before getting out of the third. Sacrificing velocity for location thereafter, Mortensen held Seattle scoreless on two hits and a walk over his final five frames. Mortensen has never faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: In just his second Major League start, Manship saw his pitch count rise a little too early in his outing against the Blue Jays. He tossed 4 1/3 innings, allowing three runs on seven hits while throwing a total of 104 pitches. The right-hander said that he was trying to be a little too precise with his pitches in the outing, and without his changeup to rely on, it made it difficult for him to change speeds against a tough Blue Jays lineup. Manship will see if he can deliver a longer outing when he faces the A's for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson pitched just five innings last Saturday, but that was enough to beat the Mariners and notch his first win since Aug. 9 at Kansas City. He gave up three runs to the Mariners in the second inning, one on a bomb by Mike Sweeney, but settled down after that. Anderson struck out six, walked just two and allowed seven hits in the win. And for a change, he got plenty of run support in the 9-5 victory. In 13 of his 26 starts this season, he has received two or fewer runs of support. He's 0-1 with a 7.94 ERA against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing maneuvered through the first five innings of his last start at Toronto with relative ease, allowing just four hits and one walk. But the rookie southpaw couldn't continue the success into the sixth, when he loaded the bases with no outs. All of the runs would eventually score as Duensing was charged with three runs on six hits in his five-plus innings to pick up the no-decision. In his three previous starts, Duensing had posted an ERA of 1.42, allowing just three earned runs in 19 innings. He'll see if he can get back to that form when he faces makes his first start against the A's. In two relief appearances vs. Oakland this season, Duensing is 0-0 with a 9.00 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez was in command from the get-go in his last start. The lefty used a steady diet of fastballs and curveball to go with a new four-seam changeup to keep the Mariners at bay. Gonzalez went seven innings, allowing just two runs on six hits while striking out three. According to A's manager Bob Geren, Gonzalez's changeup could make a huge difference down the stretch. Gonzalez now has three pitches he can turn to when he's in a jam and is gaining more confidence with every start.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman takes a seven-game winning streak over eight starts into this game. He has a 2.29 ERA in those eight games and he has allowed just one run in his last four starts and 261/3 innings. He is the only Rangers right-hander to allow just one run over four starts. Feldman has started five of the Rangers 11 league-leading shutouts, including three in his last four starts. He is trying to become the first Rangers right-hander to win at least 17 games in a season since Rick Helling won 20 in 1998. He beat Oakland twice earlier this season, both times in May, by holding them to two runs in six innings in both starts. He won 3-2 on May 6 and 5-2 on May 29.
away_pitcher_note: Backed by seven runs in the game's first two innings, Tomko picked up an easy victory in an 11-3 win against the White Sox on Tuesday night. Tomko probably would have liked to go deeper into the ballgame, however. Despite a hefty cushion, he lasted only 5 1/3 innings, allowing three runs on six hits with three strikeouts and one walk. He threw 82 pitches, but A's manager Bob Geren had seen enough after Tomko surrendered a homer and walk in the sixth. Tomko has thrown six innings only once in his five starts with the A's. Lifetime against the Rangers, Tomko is 1-3 with a 7.94 ERA in 13 games (five starts).

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy is 2-0 with a 4.26 ERA in two starts since coming off the disabled list. He missed three months with a stress fracture in his right shoulder blade. In 12 2/3 innings since he returned with new mechanics, he has allowed eight hits, four walks and six strikeouts. He is 4-0 with a 3.31 ERA in seven starts at home this season and is 7-4 with a 4.00 ERA in 20 starts over the past three years at the Ballpark in Arlington. He is 1-3 with an 8.15 ERA in six career games, including four starts, against the Athletics. That's his highest ERA against any opponent.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who has pitched in long relief for most of the season, is now part of a six-man rotation designed to reduce the workload of Oakland's young staff. Formerly a swing man for the D-backs, Gonzalez has been slightly more effective as a starter with the A's, posting a 4.20 ERA in three nods, but he rarely gets deep into games, as he's worked 15 innings on those starts. Gonzalez has faced the Rangers once this season, as a starter, and allowed five runs on eight hits and three walks over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nippert was 3-2 with a 4.43 ERA in nine starts before being replaced by Brandon McCarthy in the rotation. He is 2-0 with a 0.90 ERA in relief. His last start was against the Blue Jays on Sept. 1, when he allowed two runs in six innings in a 5-2 victory. He is 4-0 with a 2.11 ERA in six games, including three starts, at Rangers Ballpark. He made one start against the Athletics this year and pitched five scoreless innings on Aug. 3 in Oakland. He left with a 1-0 lead after five innings but the Athletics rallied for three runs in the ninth for a 3-2 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, has one of his worst outings of the season last week in Chicago, allowing three runs on five hits and two walks before being pulled after the third inning with a pitch count of 74. Heavily reliant on his sinking two-seam fastball, Cahill has struggled to keep his money pitch down in the strike zone, leaving him vulnerable to the long ball. His 26 homers allowed are an Oakland rookie record. Cahill likely won't be allowed to throw more than 100 pitches because he in uncharted waters in terms of innings pitches, and the Rangers might run him out early, anyway. On Aug. 6 in Oakland, Texas tagged the rookie for two homers on the way to scoring five runs on eight hits and two walks over six innings to pin Cahill with a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Mortensen earned his first career win in just his third career start last time out against the Twins on Friday. The young right-hander's only mistake came against the first batter as leadoff man Denard Span tagged Mortensen for a solo homer. But Mortensen settled down after that, pitching six strong innings while allowing just the one run on five Twins hits. He said after Friday's win that it was the first time he was able to effectively throw all three of his pitches. He'll be facing Texas for the first time in his young career.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson is still getting the hang of this starting stuff, and a big key for him will be learning how to remain aggressive to keep his pitch count low and last deep into ballgames. He turned in a strong start against the Royals on Friday, but it wasn't quite as long a start as he'd like as he allowed just a run on four hits with four walks and four strikeouts in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: In his past two starts, Anderson has picked up back-to-back wins for the third time this season. The lefty pitched seven strong innings in a winning effort against Minnesota last Saturday, allowing just two Twins runs on five hits while collecting four strikeouts. It was the fewest hits Anderson had allowed since July 29, when he gave up just four to Boston. Anderson also did not surrender a walk on Saturday -- the first time in 10 starts he did not allow a free pass. He'll be facing Cleveland for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Huff, who joined the Indians' rotation in mid-May, became the club's first 10-game winner this season when he turned in six innings against the Royals on Sept. 12, allowing three runs on seven hits with a walk and six strikeouts. Huff has won five of his last six starts. He's shown improved command and aggressiveness of late, as his rookie season winds to a close.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Gonzalez was hit hard by the Twins. The lefty gave up seven runs on eight hits in a losing effort Sunday. Prior to that, his only other outing against Minnesota yielded an 11-run, 10-hit night, although he didn't factor into the decision. The loss Sunday for Gonzalez was his first since Aug. 26 against Seattle. He's 1-0 this season against the Indians, earning a win back in early July when he pitched six innings and struck out eight.
away_pitcher_note: Facing the Twins on Sept. 14, Sowers worked seven scoreless innings. He had tossed seven scoreless in a win over the Mariners on July 25, so his performance in this one was not without precedent this season. Still, it was another strong step forward for Sowers, who has produced quality starts in six of his last nine outings after developing a reputation as a guy who falls apart the second or third time through an opponent's lineup. He gave up just six hits with two walks and two strikeouts to the Twins, stranding a pair of runners in the first, third and seventh innings.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland has pitched in the bullpen since Sept. 1 when he was recalled from Triple-A Sacramento for his third stint with the A's this season. He's pitched three innings of relief, allowing five hits and one earned run. Eveland made the A's Opening Day roster as a starter but was sent down May 5 after going 1-2 with a 7.40 ERA. He was recalled July 6 to start against Boston but lasted just 2 2/3 innings, giving up four earned runs, and was sent down again the next day. Eveland made his only career start against Cleveland on April 5 last season and got the win, going seven innings. He struck out seven and allowed one earned run.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona got through the first inning against the Twins on Sept. 15, so that was progress over his two-thirds of an inning clunker against the Rangers in his previous start. But Carmona nevertheless turned in an outing that served as another bit of evidence that his rough 2008 and '09 seasons are more rule than exception. The exception, it seems, was that 19-win season in 2007 when Carmona and his trusty sinker dominated from coast to coast. These days, Carmona doesn't coast through much, as evidenced by the fact that he couldn't hold a lead against the Twins and gave up five runs on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings. Carmona has allowed 19 runs over his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Oakland's designated long reliever for most of the season, Gonzalez was moved into the rotation as its sixth man as the club tries to limit the workload of its young starters. Gonzalez hasn't pitched much of late, with only six outings since July 27, but he faced the Rangers in his most recent assignment and pitched well, holding Texas to a run -- David Murphy hit a solo homer -- over four-plus innings.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is making his first start since an 8-3 loss to the Mariners in which he allowed five runs in 32/3 innings. He has spent the time since then working in the bullpen with pitching coach Mike Maddux. He is 2-5 with a 6.29 ERA in 12 starts since the beginning of July. He is 3-7 with a 4.71 ERA in 14 starts on the road. Millwood is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA in two starts against Oakland this year and 5-3 with a 3.66 ERA in 15 starts against them lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill is riding a three-game winning streak, and has a six-game unbeaten stretch. He's lowered his ERA from 5.13 to its current level over the course of the past eight games. He gave up one hit over seven shutout innings and recorded a career-high seven strikeouts in his last start, a 4-0 victory over the Rangers in Texas. He'll be making his fourth start against the Rangers, against whom he is 2-1 with a 2.70 ERA and an opponents' batting average of .192.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy is coming off a 6-1 loss to the Athletics on Tuesday when he allowed four runs in three-plus innings. He is now 2-1 with a 5.17 ERA in three starts since returning at the beginning of September after missing three months with a stress fracture in his right shoulder blade. He is 3-2 with a 6.10 ERA in seven starts on the road, where opponents are hitting .302 off him as opposed to .199 on the road. He is 1-4 with an 8.27 ERA in his career against the Athletics, his highest ERA against any opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Mortensen, a rookie who came to the A's in July from St. Louis in the Matt Holliday trade, made it two straight victories Thursday night, beating Cleveland. He continued to make progress, showing better command of his pitches and more confidence on the mound. He went five innings, holding the Indians to two runs and four hits. He struck out four and walked just three. He pitched out of a two-out, bases-loaded jam in the second, striking out Trevor Crowe. In his previous start, Mortensen held the Twins to one run on five hits over six innings, earning his first Major League win in just his third try.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter is 2-2 with a 4.23 ERA in his last six starts. He is 2-1 with a 3.08 ERA in six starts on the road this season. He has held right-handed hitters to a .203 batting average while left-handers are hitting .263. Opponents are hitting .169 with runners in scoring position, including 3-for-37 when there are two outs. He is 1-0 with a 3.65 ERA in two starts against the Athletics.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 21-year-old rookie, put together one of his sharpest outings of the year his last time out, holding the Indians to four hits and a walk while striking out a career-high 10 over six shutout innings. He was taken out after 89 pitches because he's passed his career high in innings pitches. It was Anderson's third win in three starts this month, and his command has been tremendous of late; he's averaging one walk over his past six assignments. With three strikeouts against the Rangers, whom he held to two runs on six hits over 7 2/3 innings on Aug. 3, Anderson will set the Oakland rookie record for strikeouts in a season at 142.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman won his 17th game in a 3-2 victory over the Angels on Saturday and has three more starts, giving him a chance to become the fourth 20-game winner in Rangers history. His 17 wins are the second most by a Rangers pitcher this decade behind 18 won by Kenny Rogers in 2004.  Feldman, 26, is the third youngest pitcher in Rangers history to win 17 games in a season. He is 12-1 with a 2.58 ERA in 15 games, including 14 starts, on the road this season. He is 2-1 with a 4.91 ERA in three starts against the Athletics.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver gets an extra day between starts because of the day off, and if anyone has earned it, he's the guy. The only Angels starter not to miss a turn, Weaver is coming off a solid six innings in Texas, yielding three earned runs on five hits and two walks while striking out four men. He reached 200 innings for the first time in his four seasons, a testament to his increased stamina and endurance. Weaver has been stellar at home (9-2, 2.89 in 16 starts) and has a strange history with the Athletics, going 2-2 in nine outings despite an excellent ERA of 2.93.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez couldn't get out of the fourth inning for the second straight start. He's given up eight earned runs and 10 hits over his last 6 2/3 innings. He's made one start against the Angels, giving up four runs and walking five in three innings on Aug. 27, 2008, in Anaheim.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough start, yielding three first-inning runs on two walks and three singles, Lackey settled in and got through six innings at Texas on Sunday, claiming the win while giving up five runs (four earned) in six innings. Lackey had given up three earned runs combined in his previous four starts, covering 33 2/3, but he has a history of struggling in his home state. Lackey also has a history of dominating the Athletics. He turned them away on Aug. 30 with one unearned run across eight innings for his 100th career win and is 16-4 in 28 career starts against Oakland with a 2.54 ERA. He's tied with Frank Tanana for fourth in wins in franchise history with 102.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland, moved into Oakland's six-man rotation to take the place of injured Brett Tomko, picked up his first win since April when he held the Indians to a run on five hits and two walks over five innings his last time out. A member of Oakland's rotation for most of the year, Eveland lost his job after being tagged for 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings against the Mariners on May 1 and was optioned shortly thereafter to Triple-A Sacramento, where he spent most of the year. A 25-year-old whose command needs to be spot-on for him to be effective, Eveland has made four apearances this month since being recalled, the first three out of the bullpen. He's faced the Angels once this year, allowing three runs on eight hits and two walks over six innings of a start on April 8 in Anaheim. He did not get a decision in Oakland's 6-4 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders continued his recent run of success by essentially shutting down the Yankees for 8 1/3 innings on Monday at Angel Stadium. Saunders allowed just two runs on seven hits over those eight innings as the only runs came on solo homers by Alex Rodriguez and Hideki Matsui. Saunders is 5-0 with a 2.11 ERA in his last six starts since coming off the disabled list on Aug. 26 after batting through stiffness in his left shoulder. He's also 7-3 with a 3.97 ERA in 12 career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, added as the sixth man in the rotation earlier this month as the A's monitor the workloads of their prized young starters, struggled mightly his last time out, Monday against the visiting Rangers. After allowing an unearned run in the first inning, he was touched for three runs in the second, and consecutive RBI singles with one out in the fourth chased him. All told he allowed six runs (five earned) on nine hits and two walks while throwing 73 pitches. Gonzalez, who spent most of the season as a long reliever and hasn't thrown more than five innings this year, made relief appearances against the Angels on July 16 and 18 and allowed two runs on three hits and three walks over 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The staff ace continues his quest for the Cy Young Award, making his next-to-last start of his breakout season. The right-hander is coming off his 27th quality start and surpassed the 200-strikeout mark for the first time in his career with a season-high 11 strikeouts against the Blue Jays. Felix is 4-0 with one no-decision in September, surrendering five earned runs in 40 innings. This will be his second start against the Athletics this season. The other one was on April 11 at Oakland. He allowed five earned runs in five innings and received no decision in the Mariners' 8-5 win.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, a 21-year-old rookie, has had his share of ups and downs this season but is on a strong finishing kick. He's 3-0 with a 3.05 ERA in four September starts, and his past two outings have been among his best. In consecutive starts against the Rangers, Cahill allowed one run on seven hits and four walks over 12 2/3 innings, including seven shutout innings of one-hit work in Texas. Armed with three pitches -- fastball, slider, changeup -- with excellent downward movement, Cahill has faced the Mariners three times this year and is 0-2 despite a 1.90 ERA and a .227 batting average against over 19 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander makes his final start of the season hoping to use it as a springboard into the offseason and beyond. He has shown flashes of being a top-of-the-rotation kind of hurler at times since his return from the Minors, but he also loses his release point, which leads to control lapses and head-scratching in the dugout. His overall performance has improved, however, and the organization believes the former first-round Draft choice eventually will be a quality starter.
away_pitcher_note: A 24-year-old rookie acquired in the four-player trade that sent Matt Holliday to St. Louis in July, Mortensen wasn't sharp his last time out, and neither was the defense behind him. Mortensen gave up seven runs on six hits and a walk over 4 2/3 innings, but only three of the runs were earned because the A's made three errors, including two in the visiting Rangers' four-run fifth inning. Mortensen, who had won his previous two starts, will be making his seventh big league appearance and sixth start against the Mariners, who beat him with four earned runs on six hits and three walks over seven innings on Sept. 4.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie took a perfect game into the fifth inning in his last start before the Blue Jays broke through and saddled him with his third consecutive loss. Fister has shown a penchant for giving up the long ball, having surrendered six home runs in his past four starts and 11 overall in 54 innings. His strikeout-to-walk ratio (32-to-14) is good for such an inexperienced hurler. This will be Fister's second start against the Athletics. He settled for a no-decision on Sept. 6 after holding the A's to one run over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, 21, credits a consistent workout routine with keeping him from wearing down late in the season, and he's looked extremely strong in September. In his penultimate start of the season, he threw 90 pitches -- 60 for strikes -- and improved to 4-0 with a 2.92 ERA in four starts for the month by holding the visiting Rangers to one earned run on six hits without a walk over 5 2/3 innings. Along the way he broke Rick Langford's Oakland rookie record for strikeouts with his 142nd of the season. Anderson has faced the Mariners three times this season, most recenty on Sept. 5, when he beat them with five innings of seven-hit work in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez shook off his previous two shaky outings to throw 6 1/3 scoreless innings against the high-powered Angels offense on Friday at Angel Stadium to get his sixth win of the season. Gonzalez also struck out seven batters and walked just one. He'll get another crack at the Angels on Friday in Oakland's last series of the regular season. Gonzalez is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in two starts against the Angels this season.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver, enduring a hard-luck stretch, yielded only two earned runs in six innings against the Athletics on Friday night at home but dropped his third straight start for the first time in his career. A leadoff walk in the fifth cost him a run on a two-out single, and another two-out hit delivered the second A's run in the sixth. Weaver gave up six hits and three walks, striking out one man. Weaver is 0-1 with a 4.02 ERA in three starts against the A's this season and 2-3, 2.93 in 10 lifetime outings.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland struggled against the Angels on Saturday, allowing eight runs, five earned, on five hits over 3 1/3 innings. Eveland also struggled with his command as he walked four batters and struck out just one. But he still was only saddled with a no-decision as the A's erased a seven-run deficit over the next three innings. He'll face the Angels again here hoping for a better result. The left-hander is 0-3 with a 6.66 ERA lifetime against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir has a 2.01 ERA in five starts with the Angels, but they have gotten him only eight runs while he's been on the mound, accounting for his 1-2 record. He has 23 strikeouts while yielding 25 hits and nine walks in 31 1/3 innings. His fastball command has been exceptional, but he has had trouble getting good bite and location on his slider.

home_pitcher_note: Kilby, who has yet to allow an earned run since joining the A's this month, gets the start and will work two innings. Killby's bullpen-mates will take it from there.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders had a shutout going entering the seventh against the A's on Sunday when it unraveled, with four hits, a walk and a wild pitch producing three runs. He finished with the win, his sixth in seven starts, yielding three earned runs on seven hits and a walk, striking out three men. Saunders has allowed three or fewer earned runs in his past seven outings, since recovering from shoulder issues. Saunders is 7-3 with a 3.97 ERA in 12 career outings against the Athletics and 3-1, 2.73 in four outings in Oakland.

summary: 2010-03-24 - Los Angeles Dodgers @ Oakland Athletics (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will make the start and Trevor Cahill will follow for the A's as the No. 5 starter decision goes down to the wire.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez will be on the mound for the Giants against the A's, making his final start with the No. 4 slot already clinched.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets will not only make his debut in green and gold but also make his first regular-season start since 2008 after missing all of last year following elbow surgery. He compiled what he deemed his usual string of shaky spring outings, tallying an 11.20 ERA in six starts -- one that came in a Minor League game. In 13 2/3 innings, Sheets surrendered a combined 23 hits, 20 runs (17 earned), 10 walks and 10 strikeouts. The A's new ace, who signed a one-year contract worth $10 million on Jan. 26, will rely mostly on his fastball and curveball while mixing in a couple changeups. This will mark his first career start against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander established himself as one of the best starters in the Major Leagues in 2009, winning 15 of his final 17 decisions, and was runner-up in the AL Cy Young Award voting after leading the league in winning percentage (.792). King Felix ranked in the top five of each of the pitcher's Triple Crown categories -- wins, ERA and strikeouts. He tied for first in wins and was second in ERA and fourth in strikeouts. His breakout season picked up steam in mid-May. He was 1-0 against Oakland last season despite a 4.97 ERA and is 7-2 with a 2.66 ERA in the past three seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Braden served as the A's Opening Day starter last year and put together a 8-9 mark with a respectable 3.89 ERA in 22 starts before watching his season come to an end on July 31 because of an injury that left his left foot numb. He has yet to regain feeling in the foot and, according to a neurologist, probably never will. Braden hopes the numbness will continue to play a nonexistent role on the mound this year as he looks to build on an impressive spring. In just one career start against the Mariners, Braden is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander acquired from the Pirates midway through the 2009 season begins his first full season with the Mariners bolstered by a strong finish with Seattle. He posted a 5-1 record with a 3.00 ERA from August 15 to the end of the campaign, which provided a much-needed career boost. His confidence took at beating during a stretch when he lost 14 of his first 17 decisions of the season, the first 11 of those decisions coming with the Bucs. Snell was a 14-game winner for the Pirates in '06 and pitched for Puerto Rico in the '08 World Baseball Classic.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer holds a 1-1 record and 1.29 ERA in two career starts against Seattle, but he missed all of 2009 after undergoing minor elbow surgery and dealing with a bout of clinical depression. Furthermore, he made just three spring starts thanks to lower back pain that led to a nerve ablation procedure in the middle of February. Duchscherer's velocity has never been his strength, as it tops out in the high 80s on a good day, but it was even weaker than usual throughout spring. However, the righty believes he'll be able to gain full arm strength by the time he takes the mound against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Just as expected, the Mariners will start a left-hander against the Athletics in the second game of the season. But it was supposed to be Cliff Lee. An abdominal strain will keep Lee on the sidelines for a while, giving Rowland-Smith his first start of the season earlier than anticipated. The lefty from Australia also debuted against Oakland last season. He pitched well for five innings but left with an injury that cost him half the Major League season. He was 1-0 with a 2.55 ERA against the Athletics in 2009 and is 2-1 with a 3.21 ERA against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: At the tender age of 21, Anderson boasted talent beyond his years in his first season in the big leagues last year. He set an Oakland rookie record with 150 strikeouts and led the team in both strikeouts and wins (11) while finishing second in starts (30). The key for Anderson is the development of his changeup, which he worked on all spring to complement his off-speed pitches. In five starts against Seattle last year, he compiled a 2-2 record and 3.41 ERA -- which ranks as his third-best ERA against any team next to Boston and Tampa Bay.
away_pitcher_note: The right forearm injury sustained when Fister was hit by a line drive during Spring Training has completely healed and the Fresno State product begins the season close to home and apparently in a comfort zone. The control artist, who grew up in Merced, which is fewer than 60 miles from Oakland, was 1-0 in two starts against the A's last season, surrendering just two earned runs in 12 innings. His forte is using both sides of the plate and putting the ball in play. Opposing hitters batted .264 against him last season and hit 11 home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Palmer, who worked two scorless innings of relief on Tuesday night against the Twins, gets the call with Scott Kazmir on the disabled list for one turn through the rotation, if all goes as planned. Palmer, a journeyman with only three games worth of Major League experience in San Francisco, was a godsend for the Angels last season. Arriving on April 23, Palmer won his first six decisions, the first time in MLB history a rookie at least 30 years old had achieved that feat. Getting movement from his fastball that makes him especially effective against right-handed hitters, Palmer finished 11-2 with a 3.93 ERA in 40 appearances, 13 as a starter. He faced the A's five times without a start or a decision, posting a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, who battled all spring for the fifth spot in the rotation, gets his first shot at proving his roster worth Friday when he takes the mound at Angel Stadium, where he owns a 1-0 record and perfect ERA. The lefty is 1-1 with a 2.92 ERA in two career starts against the Angels and is coming off a season during which he compiled a 6-7 mark with an ERA of 5.75. Gonzalez has put much time into improving not only his changeup but his composure as well.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver had a solid season debut on Monday, showing his resolve by preserving a one-run lead by getting out of a bases-loaded jam in the sixth with a fly ball out. His six strikeouts were indicative of quality stuff, his changeup especially effective in concert with his fastball and slider. Weaver allowed five hits and two walks, with 57 of his 94 pitches in the strike zone. He's 3-3 with a splendid 2.71 in 11 career starts against the Athletics and has always been tough at Angel Stadium, where he's 28-12 with a 3.29 career ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets struggled in his first frame in green and gold, giving up two walks and a double en route to throwing 23 of his 94 pitches. His next four innings, though not stellar, went smoother for the righty and gave Sheets confidence heading into his next start. He lasted five innings and gave up three runs on four hits (two earned) while walking four and fanning three in his A's debut. He's faced the Angels just twice in his career, once in 2002 and another time in 2004 when he tossed a one-hit shutout.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders, normally close to unbeatable in April, didn't have it in his season debut against the Twins on Tuesday, yielding five runs in five innings, with three homers among the eight hits he allowed. Saunders wasn't able to put his two-seam fastball where he wanted it, and the Twins pounded him. He was 10-1 with a 2.51 career ERA in April coming in, and he expects to rebound against the Athletics with more aggression and better tempo. He's 9-3 in 14 career starts against the A's, with a 3.99 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Braden dazzled in his 2010 debut against the Mariners, surrendering one run and four hits while tallying a career-high 10 strikeouts en route to settling for a no-decision in his first start since July 31, 2009. The A's southpaw, who has been forced to pitch with a numb left foot, boasted what Oakland manager Bob Geren deemed one of his best changeups. Also working like clockwork for Braden was his ability to tab first-pitch strikes. In five career starts against the Angels, Braden is 1-3 with a 4.36 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith bobbed and weaved his way through five innings against the Athletics in his regular-season debut last Wednesday night in Oakland, but was not at his best. He needed 101 pitches to navigate the five innings. He never surrendered more than one run in an inning, yet he was unable to protect three leads and settled for a no-decision in a game the Mariners eventually lost in the bottom of the ninth inning. Rowland-Smith left too many breaking pitches up in the zone and must keep them at knee or lower level to be the most effective because he doesn't have overpowering stuff. Keeping his pitches down is a must in his rematch against the Athletics in the Mariners' home opener at Safeco Field.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since Aug. 18, 2008, Duchscherer walked away with a no-decision against Seattle after laboring through five innings. He surrendered seven hits, five runs and a walk while fanning four with 101 pitches in an outing that left him feeling "indifferent." Duchscherer said he has yet to fully regain the form that made him a two-time All-Star, but manager Bob Geren believes his righty is just inches from producing a quality performance. He'll take on the speedy Mariners, against whom his last start came against.

home_pitcher_note: Fister lost his first start of the season in Oakland, lasting only four innings while allowing two runs. He allowed six hits and three walks. The big improvement needs to come with his pitch count. He threw 99 pitches against the A's, right at an average of 25 pitches per inning. That's not going to endear Fister to pitching coach Rick Adair. Fister did make it through his first start without allowing a home run.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Anderson mowed down the Mariners' lineup with the same ease he carried through his final 17 starts last year -- during which he compiled an 8-4 mark and a 2.96 ERA after going 3-7 with a 5.74 ERA in his first 13 starts. Anderson allowed just three hits while walking one and fanning four in six shutout innings against Seattle, whom he'll face again for his second start. He owns a career 3-2 mark and 2.83 ERA in six starts vs. the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas had a rough ending to his start against Texas on Friday, allowing five runs on eight hits in 5 1/3 innings. Rangers hitters batted .348 against the left-hander and he allowed a home run to Nelson Cruz. He was sharp for the first five innings, allowing three singles aside from Cruz's home run while striking out four through five innings. He left his changeup in the zone in the sixth inning and the Rangers hit him hard in a four-run inning.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez looked strong in his 2010 debut, allowing two earned runs on six hits while walking one and striking out six over six innings en route to a win over the Angels. It marked his first start since claiming the fifth starter role. The A's lefty felt confident in his changeup and ability to constantly pound the strike zone -- two ingredients with which he struggled last season. In five career games vs. the Mariners, three of them starts, Gonzalez has compiled a 1-1 record and 3.96 ERA. He has also tallied 22 strikeouts and 13 walks through 25 frames against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets received yet another no-decision in his most recent start against the host Angels, allowing three earned runs over six innings in what was statistically deemed a quality outing. But the A's right-hander also scattered 10 hits and walked three while striking out just one in a performance that left him longing for his next start, when he hopes to boost the life on his fastball. Sheets has faced the Orioles just once in his career -- a rather forgettable loss in 2003 that had him surrendering six hits, five runs, two homers and five walks in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez, who won the Orioles' fifth rotation spot late in camp, struggled with a high pitch count early but was effective in Saturday's regular season debut nonetheless. The young right-hander came out and fired three scoreless frames  before an odd series of events led to a run in the fourth. Using a fastball that was consistently in the mid-90s, Hernandez allowed two earned runs over six innings against the Blue Jays. He was outdueled by Dana Eveland and took the loss. Hernandez has appeared in two games (one start) against Oakland and is 1-0 with a career 1.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Braden hung around just long enough in his last start against the Halos to notch his first win of the season. A laboring six innings of work gave him a line that had three runs, five hits, a walk and a pair of strikeouts attached to his name, but he didn't receive the run support necessary of a win until minutes after he exited the game. Braden admitted he struggled throughout the contest before getting into what he deemed a "proverbial groove," but he'll look to regain his normal form when facing an Orioles team against which he owns a 1.32 ERA -- his best against any opponent. Braden boasts a 4-1 career mark in five games (four starts) against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran ace of the Orioles staff, Millwood took a 2-1 lead into the eighth inning in his last start before a costly error and a pair of homers saw his chances for victory dissipate. He gave up five hits and four runs (although only one was earned) with six strikeouts over 7 2/3 walk-free frames in a loss to the Blue Jays on Sunday. Millwood has allowed two earned runs or fewer in both of his starts this season and will look to finally record a "W" on Friday. He is a career 6-3 with a 3.38 ERA in 16 starts against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: In his most recent start against the Mariners, Duchscherer looked like his old All-Star self and received his first win since July 8, 2008. He dominated Seattle for 7 1/3 innings, surrendering just two hits while fanning four in a 4-0 A's victory. Following the game, Duchscherer mentioned he kept runners off base by having full trust in his fastball, something he lacked in his first start of the season. He also kept the ball down and hit his corner spots as planned. In nine games (two starts) against Baltimore, Duchscherer owns a career 2-0 mark and 2.78 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie has twice been on the wrong side of a well pitched game, falling both times at the hands of Rays' right-hander Matt Garza. After allowing a solo homer in the third inning Monday, Guthrie hunkered down and retired the next eight straight. Working off a fastball consistently clocked in the mid-90s, Guthrie allowed three earned runs on eight hits scattered over seven innings. With a lower arm angle aiding the movement on his pitches, Guthrie appears primed and ready to put a dismal '09 season behind him. In six career starts against Oakland, Guthrie is 1-3 with a 6.23 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, who has yet to give up a run in 2010, is coming off a no-decision against the Mariners but deserved better. He allowed just six hits over six innings, striking out six and walking two. In his first start of the season, also against Seattle, he gave up only three hits over six innings. He struck out four and walked one. Anderson, who will be making his first career start against the Orioles, was 11-11 with a 4.06 ERA last season, striking out 150 and walking just 45.
away_pitcher_note: A future staff ace, Matusz was masterful in Tuesday's no-decision against Tampa Bay. Five days removed from facing predominantly the same Rays lineup, the advantage was all Matusz's. An early candidate for American League Rookie of the Year, Matusz matched a career-high eight strikeouts and took a two-hit shutout into the eighth.  The 23-year-old lefty retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced and didn't run into a jam until one out in the eighth, when he yielded a run on four straight singles and left the game with the bases loaded. He was charged with four earned runs in the no decision and will look to put one in the win column against the A's. Matusz will be making his first career start at Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez lasted only 4 2/3 innings in his last start at Seattle. He allowed six hits and two earned runs while walking four and striking out five. That was a step back from his first outing when he went six innings and earned the win against the Angels. In that game, Gonzalez struck out six, walked only one and allowed two earned runs. He is 1-0 lifetime against the Yankees, beating them last July 25 in New York. He held the Yankees to two hits and one run over 6 2/3 innings, while striking out six and walking three.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez has been the only weak link in the Yankees' rotation so far in 2010, accounting for two of the team's three losses. He did improve in his second outing after being shelled against the Rays in his return to the Yankees, allowing the Angels four runs in 5 1/3 innings last Wednesday. Vazquez is 2-3 with a 4.98 ERA lifetime against the Athletics, with a 1-2 record and 5.63 ERA in Oakland -- although he allowed one run in eight innings the last time he took the hill there, in 2008. The current Athletics roster hasn't enjoyed much success against Vazquez, who has held them to a combined .196 batting average.

home_pitcher_note: In his first two starts this season, Sheets allowed a combined 14 hits and six runs -- five of them earned. He walked seven and struck out only four, but in his most recent outing against the Orioles, Sheets proved he's making progress toward returning to his former All-Star self. He tossed six scoreless innings against Baltimore, which tagged him for just five hits while walking three times and fanning four times. Sheets mastered the Yankees in his lone career start against them, but that came five years ago when he tossed seven shutout innings while surrendering just two hits.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes had a solid season debut, even if five walks and a high pitch count limited him to just five-plus innings on the hill. He gave up two runs in that time in earning the win against the Angels. This will mark Hughes' first career start against the Athletics; he does have three relief appearances against them that add up to 4 1/3 scoreless innings -- one of which was at Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum. No Athletics hitter has more than two career at-bats against Hughes.

home_pitcher_note: Braden continued his ownership of the Orioles in his last start, allowing just two runs over seven innings while improving to 5-1 lifetime with a 1.57 ERA against Baltimore. He struck out four and walked just one, moving to 2-0 with a 2.70 ERA on the season. The key for Braden thus far has been notching strike one, something he tries to stress early and often. He'll have to stay in top form against the Yankees. In four career games (one start) against New York, Braden has allowed 14 hits and eight runs in just 9 1/3 career innings. He's 0-1 with a 7.71 ERA versus the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia was every bit as dominant in his rain-shortened outing against the Rangers as he was in his near no-hitter against the Rays. After surrendering a first-inning run, Sabathia retired 17 of the last 19 men he faced and struck out nine, including six consecutive at one point. In his career, Sabathia is 5-7 with a 5.80 ERA against his hometown team; that's his highest ERA against an American League team that he doesn't pitch for. He is 2-4 with a 6.35 ERA in nine starts at Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, but he did win in his one start there last season. The Athletics have hit a combined .213 against Sabathia.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer didn't allow an earned run for the second straight outing in his most recent start versus the Orioles, against which he allowed two unearned runs and seven hits while walking two and striking out five through 5 2/3 innings. The A's righty, whose season was in question following a spring that resulted in a nerve ablation procedure and just a handful of starts, still feels he's building up strength to go deeper in games. Still, he's given the A's back-to-back solid outings and will look to do the same against the Indians. In 11 games -- two starts -- against Cleveland, Duchscherer owns a 1-3 record with a 3.60 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It was vintage Westbrook on the mound against the White Sox on Saturday. Whereas the veteran sinkerballer looked a bit shaky and had some control woes on his first two starts after his return from 2008 Tommy John surgery, Westbrook was in fine form in his last outing. He went seven strong innings, allowing just two runs on five hits with three walks and two strikeouts. He induced 15 ground-ball outs, which is an indication that his sinker was working well. Alas, he was saddled with a no-decision because he couldn't protect a 1-0 lead. He hopes to have similar form and a better end result in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since agreeing to a four-year extension with the A's, Anderson extended his scoreless streak to 14 innings on Sunday before struggling in his first loss of the season, an 8-3 defeat to the Orioles. He gave up five earned runs in five frames in the game as a result of his bread-and-butter pitch -- his slider -- not being effective. Anderson is looking to get back on track against the Indians, against whom he won in his only career start. He tossed six shutout innings of four-hit ball versus Cleveland last year.
away_pitcher_note: Carmona has been much more consistent this season, limiting the damage when he finds trouble and pounding the strike zone more effectively. He gave the Indians six strong innings in a win over the White Sox on Sunday, allowing three runs on six hits with two walks and four strikeouts. He issued first-pitch strikes to 19 of the 25 batters he faced, and that was the real key to his success. Carmona has gone at least six innings in each of his three starts thus far.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start of the season, Gonzalez took a loss against the Yankees after allowing five earned runs on three hits and five walks while striking out five in 4 1/3 innings. An excessive number of walks led to the southpaw's struggles for the second consecutive start. Gonzalez, who tossed 97 pitches in the short outing, issued a pair of walks in the first inning, then again in the fifth -- all of which led to the runs he allowed. In two career starts against the Indians, Gonzalez is 1-0 with a 2.79 ERA and 11 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson is coming off an ugly and inefficient outing against the Twins. In just four innings, he allowed five runs (two of which were earned) on five hits with five walks and six strikeouts. An Asdrubal Cabrera fielding error hurt him, but so did a costly bases-loaded walk, a wild pitch and a fielding error of his own. Masterson threw 96 pitches in that short span, and he once again struggled to tame left-handed hitters. He hasn't done much to dispute the notion that he might be better-served in a bullpen setting, but the Indians are giving him the opportunity to prove himself as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Davis will be making his fourth start of the season after his best outing so far on Wednesday night against the White Sox on a frigid night in Chicago. The 24-year-old right-hander earned his first win of the season after holding the White Sox to no runs on two hits in six innings before leaving with a 12-0 lead. Davis walked three of the first six hitters he faced, but found a rhythm that led him to a stretch where he retired 12 straight. Davis has great command of his pitches and isn't afraid to throw a breaking ball in any situation. This will be his first career start against Oakland; he is 1-2 with a 3.23 ERA in five career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets limited the defending World Series champion Yankees to four hits and two runs in six solid innings of work in his last start, but he walked away with a loss after being overshadowed by Phil Hughes' near no-hitter. The right-hander, according to manager Bob Geren, has improved in each of his four starts thus far. Sheets currently has a 2.74 ERA to show for his efforts, but he's trying to work on pitching deeper in games and improve on his strikeout-to-walk ratio. This will mark his first career start against Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: Shields went seven innings against the White Sox on Thursday to pick up his second win of the season and first career win at U.S. Cellular field. The right-hander allowed two early runs, then buckled down, holding the White Sox scoreless over the next five innings. The 28-year-old right-hander is the old man of a young Rays staff and serves as a leader at the top of the rotation. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth innings, which is evidenced by three consecutive seasons with 215 innings pitched. He is a master at using his fastball command to set up one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 3-1 with a 3.88 ERA in eight career starts against Oakland; he is 25-14 with a 3.41 ERA in 62 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Braden improved to 3-0 after holding the Yankees to two earned runs on six hits and a walk, with two strikeouts over six innings in his last start. The A's lefty kept one of the game's most imposing lineups off balance despite battling an illness that limited his outing to 81 pitches. In six career games -- five starts -- against the Rays, Braden is 3-1 with a 3.72 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Romero has been spectacular this season, but also unlucky. In all four of his starts he has managed to go at least seven innings, not once allowing more than two earned runs. However, if it's not poor run support, it's the bullpen letting Romero down as the sophomore only has one win to show for his four quality starts. In Romero's last outing against the Rays on Saturday, he went seven strong, allowing two earned runs on six hits, before reliever Scott Downs coughed up three runs in the eighth. With luck on his side, Romero will to earn his second win of the season against the Athletics, against whom he has a 2-0 record with a sparkling 1.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer gave up five hits and four walks with two strikeouts over six shutout innings in his last start against the visiting Indians on Friday en route to upping his season mark to 2-0 while lowering his ERA to 1.32. The four free passes marked something of a rarity for the A's righty, but he eased the damage by forcing Cleveland to hit into four double-play balls. Furthermore, it marked the second time in his last three outings he's lasted into at least the sixth frame on fewer than 100 pitches. In 11 career games -- just one start -- against Toronto, Duchscherer is 1-0 with a 3.09 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Statistically Morrow has looked like a different pitcher in his past two starts, giving up only two earned runs over 13 innings, while recording 16 strikeouts over that span. That being said, Morrow still displayed some of the control issues that have plagued him in the past. Against the Rays on Sunday, Morrow walked six batters over six innings and was bailed out on several occasions by catcher Jose Molina, who threw out a career-high four baserunners. It is imperative that Morrow maintain his high strikeout rate; on several occasions against the Rays he was able to prevent a potential big inning by stranding baserunners. Morrow is 2-0 against the Athletics with a 4.13 ERA over 32 2/3 career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill will make his season debut Friday in place of lefty Brett Anderson, who suffered a strain near his flexor tendon and was placed on the 15-day disabled list this week. The 22-year-old Cahill began the season on the DL with a left scapula stress reaction before being activated April 20 and immediately sent to Triple-A Sacramento, where he was 1-0 with a 1.04 ERA in two starts. The A's righty spent the entire 2009 season in the A's starting rotation en route to posting a 10-13 record with a 4.63 ERA. He joined Anderson in making the jump from Double-A Midland to the big leagues, where he made 32 starts and compiled 178 2/3 innings. In two career starts against Toronto, Cahill is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA. He surrendered 13 hits and eight runs in a combined 10 2/3 innings vs. the Blue Jays last season.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland fell back down to earth in his last start against Boston on Monday, giving up seven earned runs in just three innings as the Blue Jays fell to the Red Sox, 13-12. Somehow, Eveland managed to escape without the loss as Red Sox ace Josh Beckett blew a five-run lead and was yanked after just three-plus innings. Going into that contest, Eveland spotted a dazzling 1.93 ERA, but left with an ERA of 4.57 -- what a difference a night can make. Eveland's next outing will come against his former club, the Oakland Athletics, whom he's never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez tossed what was arguably his finest performance of the season thus far -- a seven-inning shutout performance against the Indians, who garnered just five hits off the A's lefty. The seven innings pitched tied a career high, and Gonzalez also struck out three in the winning effort. He had walked a combined 10 batters in his previous three starts, but Gonzalez offered up just two free passes in the outing. After the game, A's manager Bob Geren mentioned Gonzalez had remarkable life on his fastball and used his always impressive breaking ball often while mixing in a few changeups to offset his other two pitches. In his lone career start against the Blue Jays in 2008, Gonzalez gave up four runs on four hits and two walks in a loss.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum can't do much more to earn a win. He's already had four quality starts in five outings and has pitched at least seven innings in all but one appearance. On Tuesday night against the Red Sox, it was a familiar scene as the Blue Jays' bullpen collapsed and walked across the winning run in a 2-1 loss. Marcum went seven innings, allowing only one run in the losing effort. While Marcum has made it clear that wins are something he can't entirely control, he has not won a game since April 11, 2008 -- prior to undergoing Tommy John surgery. Marcum is 1-1 lifetime against the Athletics, with a 4.15 ERA over 21 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets had his shortest outing of the year in his last start, against the Rays, surrendering eight earned runs on nine hits and a walk with two strikeouts. The righty served up a pair of home runs after allowing just one over his first four starts combined. Sheets made no excuses for his rather forgettable performance and will look to bounce back vs. a Blue Jays team against which he owns a 2-0 record and 1.93 ERA in two career starts. The last time Sheets faced Toronto was two years ago, when he offered up two runs, four hits and four walks in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Braden was roughed up in his first loss of the year in his last start against the Rays, getting tagged for six earned runs on eight hits and three walks while striking out just one over four innings. The hiccup came after a string of four consecutive quality outings from the left-hander, who upped his ERA from 2.77 to 4.20. Considering the loss came against the team with the best record in baseball, Braden followers shouldn't fret just yet. However, he did admit after the outing that his seemingly permanent numb left foot did affect his game. Either way, Braden will look to bounce back vs. a Rangers team against which he owns a 1-2 record and 3.86 ERA in eight career games (five starts).
away_pitcher_note: Harden earned his first victory with the Rangers in his last start against the White Sox on Wednesday, allowing three runs in six innings. The Rangers won, 6-5, while Harden allowed four hits, walked five and struck out two. He has now made five starts and walked 23 in 23 2/3 innings while striking out 22. He is 0-1 with a 5.59 ERA in two starts on the road. This will be his first start ever against the Athletics. Harden was 36-19 with a 3.42 ERA in 89 starts and eight relief appearances with the Athletics from 2003-08. He is 18-9 with a 2.98 ERA in 47 starts and two relief appearances in his career at the Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro will make his 2010 big league debut after making 17 starts for Oakland last season. Mazzaro will make the start in place of injured right-hander Justin Duchscherer. Mazzaro started with Triple-A Sacramento this season and has a 1-1 record with a 2.59 ERA in five appearances (four starts). In 24 1/3 innings this year, Mazzaro has struck out 27 while walking 12. Mazzaro went 4-9 with a 5.32 ERA for Oakland last season, going 1-4 with a 5.46 ERA at home. Mazzaro has never faced the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman allowed three runs (one earned) in six innings in his last start against the White Sox on Thursday. The Rangers ended up losing, 7-5, and Feldman is now 0-2 with a 6.75 ERA in his past three starts. This is only his second start on the road. Last year, he set a Rangers record with 12 wins on the road. Left-handed hitters are batting .333 against him. He is 3-4 with a 5.33 ERA in eight starts and five relief appearances in his career against the Athletics. He has made four starts and one relief appearances at the Coliseum and is 1-3 with a 7.48 ERA there.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill was roughed up for six earned runs on seven hits over five innings in his season debut against the host Blue Jays. The A's right-hander walked one and struck out three in a loss during which he said he couldn't find his sinker. Cahill, who surrendered an Oakland rookie-record 27 home runs last season, offered up three to Toronto. The 22-year-old righty began the season on the DL with a left scapula stress reaction and was activated April 20 only to be immediately optioned to Triple-A Sacramento, where he made two starts and went 1-0 with a 1.04 ERA. Cahill earned the starting nod in Toronto due to Brett Anderson's trip to the DL, and he'll look to bounce back vs. a Texas team against which he owns a career 3-1 mark and 2.45 ERA in four starts. The ERA marks Cahill's lowest against any American League team.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis threw nine scoreless innings against the Mariners in his last start on Friday. He allowed three hits, walked one and struck out ten in a game the Rangers won in 12 innings. He retired the last 21 batters that he faced and the nine innings marked the longest outing of his Major League career. Lewis has struck out ten batters in three of his first five starts and his 38 strikeouts were the second most ever by a Rangers pitcher in the month of April. He now has a 2.33 ERA in three starts on the road. Opponents are hitting .195 off him, including .209 by left-handed hitters and .176 by right-handed hitters. Opponents are just 3-for-26 off him with runners in scoring position.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will go for his third win in as many starts when he takes the mound against the Rays. He earned the victory in his last start on Saturday in Toronto, when he allowed two runs (both earned) on three hits, walked two and struck out eight in 6 2/3 innings. Gonzalez is 1-1 with a 3.97 ERA in two home starts this season. Righties are batting .211 against Gonzalez, while lefties are hitting .222. Opponents are hitting .195 against Gonzalez in Oakland this season. Gonzalez has made three appearances (one start) against Tampa Bay lifetime, going 1-0 with a 5.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Price will make his sixth start of the season against the A's after throwing 110 pitches in six innings in the Rays' 4-2 loss to the Royals on Saturday night in Tropicana Field. He struggled in a two-run second inning, and Kansas City made him throw 52 pitches in the first two innings, but he didn't give up a hit in his final four frames. The 24-year-old left-hander has good enough stuff to put on dominant performances like his four-hit shutout of Toronto on April 25, but Tampa Bay manager Joe Maddon said it all starts with fastball command, which Price admitted he just didn't have for the first two innings of his last outing. This will be Price's first career start against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Roughed up in his last two starts, Sheets will face the Rays seeking his second win of the season.
