On Sunday in Toronto, Sheets lasted just 3 1/3 innings, giving up nine runs (all earned) on 10 hits. Sheets has faced the Rays once before, when they tagged him for eight runs (all earned) and nine hits in four innings on April 27 in Tampa Bay. In six starts this year, Sheets has a higher walks-per-nine-innings rate (4.7) than any other year in his career. His previous high is 2.9, which he accumulated in each of his first two years in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Davis outdueled AL Cy Young Award winner Zack Greinke on Sunday to earn his third win of the season. The 24-year-old right-hander held the Royals scoreless on three hits while walking three and striking out five in seven innings of work. Davis has great command of his pitches, and he isn't afraid to throw a breaking ball in any situation. Aside from his quality stuff, Davis always seems to maintain his composure, which might be his biggest asset. Davis will be making his second career start against Oakland. He picked up the win against the Athletics on April 27, when he allowed four earned runs in five innings in a game won by the Rays, 8-6.

home_pitcher_note: The last time Braden faced the Rays, they touched him up for six runs in four innings to give him his first loss of the year. On Monday, Braden was outdueled by Texas righty Rich Harden, despite tossing his fifth quality start in six tries. Braden went seven innings but gave up three runs on a career-high 11 hits in a 4-2 Oakland loss. Braden has a 2-1 record with a 2.67 ERA in four home starts this season and sports a strikeout-to-walk ratio of 19-3 at the Oakland Coliseum. Righties are hitting .274 against Braden this year, while lefties are batting .229.
away_pitcher_note: Shields went eight-plus innings against the Mariners on Tuesday night and came away with his fourth win of the season after striking out 10 and walking none. The 28-year-old right-hander is the old man of a young Rays staff, serving as a leader at the top of the rotation. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth inning, which is evidenced by his three consecutive seasons with at least 215 innings pitched. He is a master at using his fastball command to set up one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 4-1 with a 3.59 ERA in nine career starts against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis suffered his first loss of the season on Wednesday, allowing three runs in six innings in a 4-1 loss to the Athletics. He walked three and struck out six. He is 2-0 with a 3.38 ERA in two starts at home this season. Opponents are hitting .199 off him including .207 by left-handers and .186 by right-handers. They are 3-for-32 off him with runners in scoring position. He is 2-1 with a 3.60 ERA in five career starts and two relief appearances against the Athletics in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill allowed just one unearned run over five innings during Wednesday's win over the Rangers in Oakland. With the victory, Cahill moved to 4-1 with a 2.05 ERA in five career starts against the Rangers. His 2.05 ERA against Texas since the start of 2009 is the second-lowest figure in the Majors behind Scott Kazmir's ERA of 1.96. Felix Hernandez is the only other pitcher to have recorded four wins against Texas since the start of 2009. Cahill has only pitched in the Ballpark in Arlington once. He threw seven shutout innings, allowing one hit and two walks while striking out seven on Sept. 16, 2009, to earn the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Holland will be called up before the game to replace Matt Harrison, who is going on the disabled list with tendinitis in his left biceps. Holland was 4-1 with a 0.93 ERA in six starts at Triple-A Oklahoma City.  In 38 2/3 innings, he has allowed 32 hits, walked seven and struck out 37. He last pitched on May 4. Holland was 6-12 with a 6.23 ERA in 21 starts and 2-1 with a 5.48 ERA in 12 relief outings for the Rangers last year. He was 1-6 with a 10.19 ERA in his last nine starts. He was 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA in one start and two relief appearances against the Athletics last year.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez completed seven innings of work for the second time in three games in his last start, a 4-1 loss to Tampa Bay. He allowed three earned runs on three hits, striking out seven and walking five, but was outdueled by Rays lefty David Price. Citing a new slowed-down pitching motion, Gonzalez has been able to throw deeper into games recently. In three career appearances (one start) against the Rangers, Gonzalez is 1-0 with a 0.00 ERA over 9 2/3 innings. He has yet to face Texas this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson beat the Royals, 4-1, with a complete-game performance on Friday night. He allowed five hits, all singles and it was his sixth straight "quality start." He joins Kevin Brown (1993) and Charlie Hough (1988) as the only three Rangers starting pitchers to begin a season with six such starts. Nobody has done it seven times. Wilson has allowed one or fewer runs in four of his six starts. He allowed two runs over six innings in a 4-2 victory over the White Sox on April 27 and five runs -- three earned -- in his rain-shortened, six-inning complete game against the Yankees on April 16. Since that night he is 3-0 with a 1.21 ERA in four starts and the Rangers have won all four games.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his finest performance as an Athletic on Saturday, in Oakland's 4-2 win over Tampa Bay. He went 6 1/3 innings, his longest outing in the green and gold, allowing two earned runs on four hits while striking out eight and walking three. Sheets called it the most relaxed he had felt with his new team, since he signed a one-year, $10 million deal in the offseason. Sheets' breaking ball looked like it did during his days in Milwaukee, while his command looked better than it did in his previous two starts, when he gave up a combined 17 earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders has struggled this season but looked better on Saturday against the Mariners when he allowed just one earned run on five hits over 5 2/3 innings against the Mariners. Saunders, though, was still saddled with the no-decision because two unearned runs scored after a throwing error by Kevin Frandsen at third base in the fifth inning. Saunders is 9-4 with a 4.13 ERA in 15 career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Braden will take the mound for the first time since tossing baseball's 19th perfect game on Sunday in a 4-0 A's win over Tampa Bay. In his perfect effort, Braden relied on locating his inside fastball to hitters, which in turn made his changeup more effective. He struck out six Rays and got the rest to either fly out or ground out in ordinary fashion. The last time he faced the Angels, on April 11, Braden earned the win by throwing six innings, allowing three earned runs on five hits while walking one and striking out two.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has been a bit inconsistent this season and it showed against the Mariners on Sunday. The right-hander allowed five runs on 10 hits but he did last 6 2/3 innings and struck out five batters. Santana has owned the A's over his career, going 10-2 with a 1.41 ERA against Oakland in 17 career appearances (15 starts).

Pineiro wasn't perfect against the Rays the day after they were on the wrong side of a perfect game against the A's on Sunday, but he was certainly impressive, tossing 6 1/3 scoreless innings on Monday. He allowed just five hits on the night and walked just one while tying a season-high with seven strikeouts. But he was stuck with a no-decision when the bullpen blew a four-run lead. Pineiro is 8-8 with a 4.68 ERA in 22 appearances (17 starts) against the A's in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After stumbling in his season debut on April 30, Cahill has settled down in his past two starts. He's given up a combined three runs (two earned) in those two starts, allowing nine hits and five walks in 10 2/3 innings, while striking out five. Cahill has allowed one home run in that span, after giving up three in his season debut and 27 in 32 starts last year. In three career starts against Los Angeles, Cahill is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA. He is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two career starts at Anaheim.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez lasted just four innings in his last start on Wednesday, giving up four earned runs on nine hits while striking out three. Gonzalez attributed his struggles to lack of command, saying he left too many balls up in the strike zone during the 10-1 Rangers' win. It was Gonzalez's shortest outing of the year, and followed three performances when he completed at least 6 2/3 innings. In his previous start against the Mariners on April 14, Gonzalez went 4 2/3 innings, giving up two earned runs on six hits and four walks while striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: It has been a rough go for Rowland-Smith so far this season, but the left-hander gets another chance to show what he can do as a starter. His spot in the rotation could be be slipping away, and he needs a strong effort to rebuild his confidence. Rowland-Smith has made seven starts, the most recent being a tough three-inning defeat to the Orioles in Baltimore. Afterward, Rowland-Smith said he needs to get back to pitching "with a chip on my shoulder." He is 2-2 with a 3.62 ERA in his career against the Athletics. In three starts at the Oakland Coliseum, he is 1-0 with a 3.31 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his second straight quality outing on Thursday, though it came in a 2-1 extra innings loss in Texas. He went six innings, giving up an earned run on three hits and three walks while striking out eight. It was the second straight start that Sheets had recorded eight strikeouts. Both his manager Bob Geren and catcher Josh Donaldson said Sheets has added a cutter to his repertoire, though Sheets wouldn't confirm such talk. Sheets faced the Mariners on Opening Day, giving up three runs (two earned) on four hits and four walks while striking out three.
away_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander takes his second shot at getting his record back to the break-even point. Hernandez pitched well enough in his last outing to snap his personal three-game skid, surrendering just one run over seven innings against the Orioles, but the four-run lead he gave to the bullpen went out the window in the eighth inning and he had to settle for a no-decision. Hernandez did, however, pronounce himself "back" after three subpar performances.  The righty has faced the Athletics once this season, winning on Opening Night in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start since tossing a perfect game, Braden took the loss in a 4-0 defeat against the Angels on Friday. Braden threw five scoreless innings before giving up four runs in the sixth, three of which came via a Hideki Matsui home run. Braden has struggled against the Tigers in his career, as his career ERA against Detroit is 7.34 -- his second-highest figure against any team. In six career starts (30 2/3 innings pitched) against the Tigers, Braden has gone 2-2, giving up 39 hits and nine walks while striking out 17.
away_pitcher_note: Two rainouts in the past week will provide Verlander an extra two days of rest before he faces the A's. Verlander has won each of his past three starts, holding the Angels, Indians and Yankees to four runs on 11 hits in 21 innings. He shut out New York for 6 2/3 innings in his most recent start. He is 3-3 with a 3.07 ERA in seven career starts against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Ross will make his second big league start on Thursday in place of injured right-hander Justin Duchscherer. Ross made an emergency start for Duchscherer on Saturday in Anaheim, but was tagged for the loss. Ross retired the initial 11 batters he faced before giving up three straight hits, including a three-run homer to Kendry Morales. Ross said he feels most comfortable as a starter because that's what he's been his whole life. The 6-foot-6 rookie right-hander is yet to face the Tigers in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman was expected to start on Tuesday, but his start was pushed back a day to allow Tigers ace Justin Verlander to stay on turn. In his last start, Bonderman looked strong but was unable to garner any run support, as the Tigers lost to the Yankees in the second game of a day-night doubleheader last Wednesday. He allowed only two runs in seven innings before the Yankees went off in the ninth and posted six runs. The right-hander still hasn't won a game since the Tigers' home opener, which was five starts ago. Nothing would make Bonderman happier than shutting down the Oakland A's, the team that drafted him in the first round in 2001 and traded him away the following season. He will be pitching on six days' rest for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill turned in his longest outing of the year on Sunday, but was still the losing pitcher in a 4-0 defeat at Anaheim. He gave up three earned runs on five hits while striking out two and retired 13 straight batters at one point. Cahill faced the Giants once last year, giving up an earned run on four hits and a walk over seven innings. For his career, Cahill has fared much better during his 19 home appearances (8-9, 4.12 ERA) compared his 17 road starts (3-8, 5.20 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: This game could be regarded as a test for the new, improved Zito. Since joining the Giants, he's 0-3 with a 9.22 ERA in three starts against the A's, for whom he played from 2000-06. If Zito stays true to his 2010 form, he won't get caught up in facing his former team and will treat this game as he would any other. Naturally, Zito has pitched more at the Oakland Coliseum than anywhere else, compiling a 51-31 record with a 3.73 ERA in 111 starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez threw his fifth quality start in eight tries on Monday, in an 8-4 A's win. He completed seven innings, giving up three earned runs on four hits and four walks while striking out four. Gonzalez said he's learned to control his emotions on the mound and that it's allowed him to pitch deeper in games this season. Gonzalez made one start against the Giants last year and was knocked around a bit. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings, giving up six runs (four earned) on 10 hits and two walks while striking out six.
away_pitcher_note: Cain's 2-4 lifetime record against the A's obscures the fact that he pitched his best career game against them: a one-hit shutout at Oakland on May 21, 2006. He has recorded six quality starts this season in eight outings, including last Monday, when he surrendered two runs in six innings but absorbed the decision in a 3-1 Giants loss at San Diego. Typically, all Cain needs is a little offense to succeed. He's 45-18 when he receives two or more runs of support and is 40-8 when he gets three runs or more while he's in the game.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his third straight quality outing on Tuesday in an extra-innings win over Seattle. He tossed 6 2/3 innings, his longest start of the year, giving up four earned runs on eight hits and four walks while striking out five. Sheets also set a new season high in pitches thrown (111). After Tuesday's contest, Sheets said he needs to focus on cutting down his walks, but that he's happy he was able to pitch deep into the game.
away_pitcher_note: Though Sanchez has allowed a season-high four runs in two of his last three starts, his control has improved in that span. He has walked just two batters in 21 innings in those games, including none in six innings in his most recent outing last Tuesday at San Diego. He's 8-7 with a 3.32 ERA and 161 strikeouts in 143 2/3 innings since his no-hitter last July 10 against the Padres. Sanchez already has pitched seven innings or more four times this season, matching the number he reached last year. Due to poor run support, he's only 1-2 in those games this year.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie pitched six innings while giving up just one run with three strikeouts in a 4-3 Rangers win on Wednesday. He entered the game with two straight wins and posted a 2.18 ERA over his last three starts, but did not factor into the decision in the loss. In six career starts against the Athletics, Guthrie is 1-3 with a 5.23 ERA. Guthrie's ERA is lower on the road than it is at home, where he has a 1-2 record with a 4.58 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Braden put forth a valiant effort in his previous start on Wednesday but was outdueled by Detroit ace Justin Verlander in a 5-1 loss. Braden had tossed six shutout innings before giving up two earned runs in the seventh and leaving the game due to illness. He allowed six hits and a walk while striking out two. Braden made his big league debut in Baltimore and has enjoyed success against the team ever since. For his career, Braden is 5-1 with a 1.57 against the Orioles, his best such marks against any opponent.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Rangers, Matusz lasted just 2 1/3 innings, giving up seven runs on eight hits with two strikeouts in a 13-7 loss. In his last start against the Athletics, Matusz pitched 6 1/3 innings, giving up three runs on eight hits with eight strikeouts in a 8-3 win on April 18. He is 2-2 with a 3.60 ERA in six career starts at home. He is 0-4 this month after registering two victories during the month of April.
away_pitcher_note: With an injured Justin Duchscherer unavailable, Cahill has become a steady presence in the A's rotation since being called up on April 30. On Friday against the Giants, Cahill picked up his second win of the year by allowing one earned run over 6 2/3 innings. He allowed six hits and a walk while striking out four to post his second consecutive quality start. Cahill faced the Orioles twice during his rookie season last year, going 1-1 with a 3.46 ERA. He lost in his only outing at Camden Yards, though, allowing three earned runs on eight hits over seven innings while striking out four.

home_pitcher_note: Although he had been scheduled to start Friday at Toronto, Bergesen will take the mound for Thursday's get-away game against Oakland. He will fill in for David Hernandez, who was switched to a relief role to bolster a depleted bullpen. Bergesen has been the Orioles' winningest pitcher so far in 2010, with three wins in eight starts, but he took a no-decision Saturday against Washington in the Nationals' 7-6 victory. He allowed three runs through the first five innings, but was yanked in the sixth after giving up two more runs without recording an out. Bergesen has never faced the Athletics.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez turned in the finest performance of his career during his last start, a 1-0 win over the Giants on Saturday. Gonzalez tossed a career-high eight innings, shutting out San Francisco on two hits and a walk while striking out five. Gonzalez only needed 95 pitches to get through the outing but didn't get a chance to close out the game as manager Bob Geren went with closer Andrew Bailey. Gonzalez has now turned in quality starts in five of his past six outings. He made one start against the Orioles last year, striking out five over six shutout innings while allowing seven hits and a walk.

home_pitcher_note: Willis' last start seemed like two different outings in one, which is a big reason why it's so difficult to judge where the D-Train stands with his pitching at this point in the season. He not only allowed one hit among the first 12 batters he faced, but that hit was the only ball the Dodgers put in play past the infield in that span against him. Once Matt Kemp singled, however, Willis allowed five hits and three walks among the final 13 hitters he faced, along with two wild pitches and a hit batter. One suspicion was that Willis ran into serious mechanical issues pitching out of the stretch, something they might work on between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Monday's off-day allows Sheets to pitch on normal rest while the A's decide if the injured Brett Anderson can go Saturday. The ERA may look unsightly, but Sheets has sliced more than two runs off his ERA since nine runs in 3 1/3 innings against Toronto in his first May start raised him to a season-high mark of 7.12. In four starts since then, he's failed to go fewer than six innings. His most recent outing, Sunday against San Francisco, was his best of the season -- six innings of two-hit shutout ball and eight strikeouts to match a season high. If Sheets has turned a corner, it couldn't come at a better time for the A's, who could use his veteran presence in their rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello took some damage from three hard-hit comebackers in his last start, including a bruise on his right leg, but he's expected to be fine for his next start on an extra day of rest. The 21-year-old has alternated losses and wins over his last six starts, the last being six innings of two-run ball to beat the Dodgers last Sunday. He has allowed just two extra-base hits over his last three starts, and he hasn't given up a home run in his last four starts. However, Porcello has lost both of his previous meetings with the A's in his brief career, allowing 10 runs on 17 hits over 9 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Assuming he gets through a Thursday bullpen session in  Baltimore without any soreness, Anderson will be activated off the 15-day disabled list to make Saturday's start against the Tigers at Comerica Park. Anderson has been out since April 25 with a left forearm strain and left elbow inflammation, but a three-inning rehabilitation start at Triple-A Sacramento on Monday was enough to prove to the southpaw -- and, presumably, manager Bob Geren, who watched the game on his laptop -- that he was ready to return. Anderson threw sliders without any pain in his rehab outing, a good sign, but he'll be on a short leash -- Geren said he would be limited to about 75 pitches. In the unlikely event that Anderson can't make the start, right-hander Tyson Ross would probably get the call.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers will recall Scherzer from Triple-A Toledo to return to the Tigers' rotation after a pair of dominant starts for the Mud Hens suggested he has made the adjustments in arm angle and delivery he was trying to find for the better part of a month in Detroit. He allowed a run on four hits over 15 combined innings, racking up 17 strikeouts in the process against just two walks. He was last seen on a Major League mound at Comerica Park on May 14, when he gave up three Red Sox home runs, two to David Ortiz, over five innings of six-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: Braden, who pitched a perfect game on Mother's Day, left his last start in Baltimore on Tuesday with a left ankle sprain. Four innings into the 1-1 game, pitching coach Curt Young and manager Bob Geren had seen enough of Braden favoring the injury, which resulted in uncharacteristic back-to-back walks and more pitches up in the strike zone than Braden usually throws. Since then, Braden has been receiving treatment and spent a couple of days off his feet and away from baseball activities. Assuming Braden is good to go in Motown, he will pitch. But any sign that the ankle is still tender and Braden might be in line for another early exit.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will get an extra day of rest before his Memorial Day assignment, thanks to the Tigers' off-day Thursday. But judging from his frustration level after his most recent outing last Tuesday at Seattle, he might not have minded pitching again a couple days later. He took a lead into the seventh inning and a pitching duel into the eighth, but ended up with the loss thanks to two home runs earlier and a Milton Bradley RBI single in the eighth. He did not feel comfortable with his pitches, but he also had some complaints over a wet mound at Safeco Field thanks to a rain shower that hit with the roof open.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill looked rather sharp in a win over the Orioles in his last start, permitting just two hits and one earned run while walking three and fanning three over six innings. Baltimore's lone run came on a third-inning homer to Garrett Atkins, but Cahill settled in after that, relying on his sinker to give up fewer than three earned runs for the fourth time in six outings this season. The young righty has made significant strides from his rookie campaign, in which he offered up an Oakland rookie record 27 homers while compiling a 4.63 ERA. This year, he's held the opposition to a .221 average that has helped him put together a formidable 1.10 WHIP. Cahill will have to get his sinker working early and often against a power-heavy Tigers lineup, one against which he's 0-1 with a 8.68 ERA in two career starts. In a combined 9 1/3 innings vs. Detroit last year, Cahill gave up nine runs, 12 hits and five walks.

home_pitcher_note: The big righty bounced back from a few rough outings in his last start, pitching well enough to beat the Rays at Tropicana Field. Over 6 1/3 innings, Lackey scattered eight hits and two runs, walking four and striking out one. Despite an ERA that is higher than one would expect, Lackey has six quality starts. The Red Sox are 5-5 in his starts. Lackey's walk-strikeout ratio (30 walks, 35 strikeouts) is another thing that has been below par. Opponents are hitting .287 against him, which is 23 points higher than Lackey's career number. In five Fenway starts this season, Lackey is 3-1 with a 5.52 ERA. Lackey has thrived against the A's in his career, going 16-4 with a 2.76 ERA in 29 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: After firing an eight-inning scoreless gem against the Giants on May 22, Gonzalez followed with a three-run outing over 6 1/3 innings against the Orioles in his most recent start. The A's lefty allowed six hits while walking three and striking out six in the no-decision. Gonzalez is continually working on keeping the free passes to a minimum. He walked 56 batters over 98 2/3 innings last season, but has already improved this year by walking 27 through 61 innings. In one career start against Boston, Gonzalez surrendered three runs on five hits and four walks while striking out eight in 5 1/3 innings of work that resulted in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: The Red Sox continue to be baffled by Matsuzaka's inconsistency. Consider the progression of his last four starts. On May 11 against the Blue Jays, he fired seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball, walking none and striking out nine. Then five days later against the Yankees, he gave up nine hits, seven runs and three walks. But Matsuzaka rebounded from that disaster in the Bronx by coming four outs away from a no-hitter in Philadelphia, firing eight shutout innings in that one. Then he again fell off in his subsequent outing, walking eight, striking out one and allowing three hits over 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Royals. Matsuzaka has pitched three times at Fenway this season, going 2-1 with a 4.76 ERA. Matsuzaka has made five career starts against the A's, going 2-1 with a 4.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his fifth straight quality outing in his most recent start against Detroit, allowing three runs on five hits and a walk while compiling six strikeouts through seven innings. Although Sheets was handed a no-decision in an eventual 5-4 A's victory, he was rather pleased about completing seven frames -- a feat he hadn't done since Sept. 6, 2008 against the Padres while he was still pitching for Milwaukee. Sheets was clocked at 95 and 96 mph multiple times in his outing against the Tigers, and he said after the game he feels his velocity, as well as the movement on his breaking ball and his overall strike count, have all improved. Thus, the veteran righty seems to be rounding back into form after he was nailed with a total of 17 runs in consecutive starts a couple of weeks ago. Despite being in the midst of his ninth Major League season, this will mark Sheets' first career outing against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer endured one of the worst starts of his career in his last outing, blowing early leads of 3-0 and 5-2 in a 12-5 loss to the Royals. Over 3 2/3 innings, Wakefield was pelted for 12 hits and nine runs. The big blow was a grand slam off the bat of Yuniesky Betancourt. All in all, Wakefield has done a nice job when called upon this season, turning in quality starts in four of his seven starts. Wakefield has 190 wins in his career, 176 of which have been for the Red Sox. Lifetime at Fenway, he is 91-71 with a 4.35 ERA. In his career vs. Oakland, Wakefield is 11-6 with a 4.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, who was activated from the disabled list on Saturday after missing time due to a strained left forearm and elbow tendinitis, put together 5 2/3 shutout innings against the Tigers later in the day, making his first start in more than a month. He allowed just three hits while walking none and striking out four in the 70-pitch effort. A healthy Anderson once again gives the A's a solid five-man rotation, which has officially lost righty Justin Duchscherer (hip) for the season. In three career starts against Boston, Anderson is 2-1 with a 2.05 ERA. Through 22 innings against the Red Sox last year, he tallied 22 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Braden, who left his May 25 start early due to a sprained left ankle, returned to the mound against the Tigers and surrendered five runs on 11 hits while walking one and striking out five in six innings. The ankle gave the A's lefty no trouble, but he allowed Detroit's leadoff hitter to reach base in each of his six frames. Two doubled, one homered and five scored, although manager Bob Geren insists it was simply about the Tigers finding holes. Braden will look to turn it around vs. the Twins, against whom he owns a 1-1 record with a 5.79 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Although he picked up the win in his last outing, Baker admitted it was his toughest performance of the season. The right-hander gave up three runs on eight hits to the Rangers. He also tied his season high of three walks, which was set in his April 28 outing against the Tigers. He said his difficulties came from not being able to get the ball down in the zone. In Sunday's outing against the Rangers, Baker snapped his personal two-game losing streak and improved his record to 4-1 in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill has won his past three starts, the latest coming in a 4-1 win at Detroit on Monday. He allowed an earned run on five hits and a season-high four walks over 6 1/3 innings while striking out three. The 22-year-old has finished at least six innings in each of his last four starts and hasn't allowed more than three runs in the six starts since his season debut. After starting the season with Triple-A Sacramento, Cahill's spot in the rotation has been cemented with Justin Duchscherer's season-ending hip injury. Cahill is 2-0 with a 0.77 ERA in two home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano picked up his first win since May 2 in his last outing against the Mariners. The lefty held Seattle to three runs on eight hits over six innings. Although Liriano wasn't as dominant in May as he was in April when he won the AL Pitcher of the Month Award, the lefty has delivered quality starts in three of his last four outings. His strikeout numbers have been solid and he's been giving his team plenty of opportunities to win. Now he'll try to see if he can continue that trend against the A's. Liriano is 0-2 with an 8.31 ERA in four career starts at Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez's string of three consecutive quality starts came to an end on Tuesday in a 9-4 loss at Boston. Gonzalez left the game with a 4-3 lead after the fifth inning, but the A's bullpen gave up six runs to give Gonzalez the no-decision. He struggled with his command on the evening, walking four batters and allowing seven hits over five innings while striking out five. The 24-year-old southpaw has thrown a career-high 108 pitches in each of his last two starts. Lefties are hitting just .145 against Gonzalez this year while righties are batting .250.
away_pitcher_note: May was a terrific month for Blackburn as he went 5-0 with a 2.65 ERA in five starts, but he didn't get off to a strong start in June. Blackburn lasted just 3 2/3 innings, allowing five runs on 10 hits in his shortest outing of the season. Prior to that outing, the Twins had lost only once in the past 13 starts Blackburn had made, dating to September of last season. The problem this time was that Blackburn couldn't get his sinker working and all of his pitches were coming out flat. He'll try to see if he can make the mechanical tweak to get his stuff going when he faces the A's in Oakland. Blackburn is 0-0 with a 5.79 ERA in three career starts at Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: The 31-year-old veteran was tagged for a loss in his last start, a 6-4 defeat at Boston on Wednesday. Sheets allowed four earned runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out one. The outing marked the sixth straight start that Sheets had finished at least six innings of work. Sheets faced the Angels once this season, when they touched him up for three earned runs on 10 hits and three walks on April 10. Sheets has fared much better at the Oakland Coliseum this season, as he has a 2.50 home ERA compared to a 7.79 ERA on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir is coming off his fourth victory of the season, thanks to stellar run support from the Angels. Before Kazmir took the mound last Wednesday night, he had a three-run cushion, and the Angel sailed to a 7-2 victory over the Royals. Kazmir allowed one run on five hits over 5 1/3 innings, while walking four and striking out two.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, A's manager Bob Geren announced Mazzaro will start for Brett Anderson, who landed back on the 15-day disabled list with a strained left forearm. Mazzaro relieved Anderson in the third inning of Thursday's 9-8 win in Boston. Mazzaro gave up three earned runs on nine hits and a walk over 3 1/3 innings while striking out one to earn his first victory of the year.  In two career starts against the Angels, Mazzaro is 0-1 with a 7.88 ERA. He's allowed 11 runs (seven earned) on 17 hits and three walks over eight innings of work in those two starts while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver is coming off his fifth victory of the season -- a seven-inning performance against the Royals in which he allowed only four hits and no earned runs to go along with nine strikeouts. As of his last start, Weaver had the best winning percentage for active American League pitchers with a minimum of 50 victories. He holds a .659 (56-29) winning percentage for his career. Weaver has allowed two earned runs or fewer in nine of his past 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Braden is still seeking his first win since tossing baseball's 19th perfect game on May 9. On Friday, he got a no-decision against Minnesota after allowing four earned runs on six hits and one walk while striking out two over 6 1/3 innings. Braden left the mound after allowing four straight batters to reach base in the seventh, giving the Twins a 4-1 lead before they won, 5-4, in 11 innings. In two starts against the Angels this season, Braden is 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA. He's thrown 14 innings, allowing seven earned runs on 12 hits and two walks while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: After a terrible start, losing five of his first six starts, Saunders has found his form in winning three of his past four decisions. He kept the ball down and in good spots against the Mariners on Friday night, holding them to one run across six innings with the benefit of three double-play grounders. He scattered eight hits with two walks and one strikeout. Saunders has more wins against the Athletics than any other club, going 10-4 in 16 career outings with a 3.73 ERA. He's 4-1 with a 2.87 ERA in five starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill's streak of winning starts came to a halt on Saturday, as he ended up with a no-decision in a 4-3 loss to the Twins. Cahill had won his previous three starts, but gave up three earned runs on five hits and four walks over six innings Saturday, while striking out six. Still, Cahill is yet to lose in three home starts this season and has a 2.04 ERA in Oakland. Cahill faced the Angels on May 16 in Anaheim, allowing three earned runs on five hits over seven innings, while striking out two.
away_pitcher_note: Recapturing his 2008 All-Star form with a brilliant slider to go with superb fastball command, Santana keeps racking up wins while shaving his ERA. He didn't have overpowering stuff in claiming his fifth win in as many outings at Seattle on Saturday, but an offensive eruption gave him a soft cushion for his six innings. He yielded one earned run on seven hits and three walks, striking out two hitters. Santana has ruled the Athletics in his career, going 11-2 with a 1.50 ERA in 16 starts and 18 appearances. He's 5-0 with a 1.38 ERA in nine games and seven starts in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: After going 0-2 with an 8.22 ERA in a span of three outings, Lincecum improved considerably last Sunday at Pittsburgh, where he worked seven innings and allowed three runs and six hits while walking two and striking out six. Lincecum, who allowed 10 home runs last year, already has yielded five. He didn't face Oakland in this year's previous Interleague series and is 3-0 with a 1.23 ERA in four career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez tossed a career-high 117 pitches Sunday, in a 5-4 win over the Twins in Oakland. He finished seven innings, giving up two earned runs on six hits and a walk, while striking out four. He has now thrown a quality start in seven of his past nine outings. Gonzalez turned in the finest effort of his career the last time he faced the Giants on May 22. He tossed eight shutout innings and retired the final 20 batters he faced, allowing two hits and a walk while striking out five, but didn't get a chance to close out the game, as manager Bob Geren elected to go with closer Andrew Bailey in the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Zito took a third straight no-decision, a 6-5 come-from-behind San Francisco win against Cincinnati, in which he gave up five runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings. The last time Zito took a decision was May 21 against the A's, when he allowed six runs on nine hits in a 6-1 loss. Zito has never beaten his old club, and holds a career record of 0-4 with an 8.85 ERA against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets took his second straight loss on Monday, 4-2 to the Angels. Sheets delivered his eighth quality start in 13 outings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits over six innings. He didn't walk a batter for the first time all year and struck out five. Sheets has made two career starts at AT&T Park, going 0-1 with a 4.09 ERA. Righties are batting .293 against him, while lefties are hitting .245.

home_pitcher_note: Cain has worked at least eight innings and allowed no more than one run in each of his past four starts. He has three complete games and two shutouts in that 34-inning stretch, in which he has yielded one earned run -- a 0.26 ERA. Only four Giants pitchers have sustained similar streaks since the franchise moved to San Francisco in 1958. Two are Hall of Famers: Juan Marichal (1965 and '66) and Gaylord Perry (1967 and '70). Vida Blue (1978) and Mike Krukow (1985) also accomplished the feat.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old righty picked up his second consecutive win on Wednesday, in a 10-1 win over the Angels. Mazzaro allowed an earned run on five hits over five innings, while striking out three. Manager Bob Geren gave Mazzaro the start after Brett Anderson returned to the 15-day disabled list with inflammation in his left arm. Righties are batting .405 against Mazzaro this season, while lefties are hitting .242. In two career starts against the Giants, Mazzaro is 0-2 with a 5.25 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano gave up two hits in five innings in his last start against the Brewers but he also walked five. He was pulled after throwing 88 pitches. It was his second start since returning to the rotation after 13 relief appearances. The Cubs are hoping that with more starts, he'll improve his command. He has faced the Athletics once, and that was in 2004. So far this season. Zambrano is 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA at home and 2-3 with a 6.91 ERA on the road. Those numbers include his relief appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill turned in one of the finest performances of his career in his last start, a 6-1 win over the Angels. The 22-year-old right-hander tossed a career-high eight innings, allowing an earned run on six hits and a walk while striking out four. Since taking over for an injured Justin Duchscherer in Oakland's rotation, Cahill has proved to be one of the A's most consistent pitchers. He's thrown a quality start in each of his last six outings, going 4-1 with a 2.25 ERA in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster took the loss in his last start against the Brewers, giving up three runs on five hits over 5 1/3 innings. He threw 104 pitches -- and was pulled because the Cubs wanted to shorten him up, pitch count wise. Dempster is 2-3 with a 3.71 ERA at home, and has served up 13 home runs in 13 games. Last year, he gave up 13 homers in 17 starts in the first half. That's not a good trend. He also walked five against the Brewers. That's another bad trend.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez struggled with his control in his last start, a 6-2 defeat at San Francisco on Friday. Gonzalez was visibly upset with himself on the mound after issuing walks and exited after giving up a pair of two-run homers. He finished 5 1/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on six hits and four walks while striking out four. The start marked the third time all year Gonzalez gave up more than three earned runs and it was the first since May 12, a span of five starts. Gonzalez has never faced the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Wells had troubles in the first inning again. He did retire the first two batters he faced but then served up four straight hits, including RBI singles to Andruw Jones and A.J. Pierzynski in his last start. Opposing teams now are batting .357 off the right-hander in the first. Pitching coach Larry Rothschild has identified a mechanical glitch when Wells pitches out of the stretch, so it'll be interesting to see if he makes the adjustment this time. Wells' confidence level is down; he needs to get off to a good start from the first pitch.
away_pitcher_note: Braden was originally scheduled to start on Tuesday, but had it moved back to rest his inflamed left elbow tendon. Braden said he felt tightness in the area in the week leading up to his last start on June 9, specifically citing a bullpen session that may have caused his arm to tighten up. Braden said he felt the arm cramp up a bit during the third or fourth inning of the outing, which ended after he gave up five runs (four earned) on 11 hits and a walk, while striking out four in 5 2/3 innings. Braden said he had no history of injuries with his throwing elbow prior to this incident.

home_pitcher_note: Through no fault of his own, the Cardinals have lost Carpenter's past two starts. He allowed three runs in 13 innings and struck out 13 over those two games, and didn't take the loss himself either time. But still, St. Louis must seize the opportunity whenever Carpenter pitches, since the back end of its rotation remains somewhat unsettled. Carpenter has a 2.16 ERA and has averaged more than seven innings per start at home this year.
away_pitcher_note: A's manager Bob Geren said he would like to keep Mazzaro on five days' rest as he gets acclimated to the starting rotation, moving Ben Sheets' scheduled start back to Saturday. Mazzaro made his second start since replacing the injured Brett Anderson on Sunday, in a 6-2 loss to the Giants. The 23-year-old righty tossed six innings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits and a walk while striking out one. He is now 0-4 with a 4.66 ERA in four career Interleague starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a somewhat uncharacteristic start at Dodger Stadium, Wainwright looked more like himself his last time out. Which is to say he looked like one of the National League's best pitchers. He's been absolutely brilliant at home this year, going 6-0 with a 1.96 ERA in six starts at Busch Stadium, and he's averaged 7 2/3 innings per game in those starts. Against the less-than-imposing A's offense, he should be in line for another excellent outing.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets will receive two extra days of rest this week before facing the Cardinals for the 27th time in his career. During his eight-year tenure with Milwaukee, Sheets struggled against St. Louis, the only team to hand him double-digit losing decisions. For his career, Sheets is 6-14 with a 4.05 ERA against the Cardinals. In his last start against the Giants on June 12, Sheets went six innings, allowing five runs (three earned) on eight hits and three walks while striking out two. He has now completed at least six innings in each of his last eight starts and in 11 of his 14 outings on the year.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan's second assignment as a Cardinal provides him another opportunity, as he'll again face one of the less-potent offenses in the game. He'll also again get to start at friendly Busch Stadium. If he can replicate his first start, in which he held Seattle to one run in four innings, but make it last a little bit longer, the Cardinals will be thrilled. They're not looking for him to be a world-beater, just to be a decent pitcher who eats up some innings. This start will give another indication whether he's ready to be that pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old righty won his fifth straight decision on Tuesday, coming in a 9-5 win at Wrigley Field against the Cubs. Cahill went 5 2/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on six hits and two walks while striking out five. In his past six starts, Cahill is 5-0 with a 2.56 ERA. Over 38 2/3 innings of work in that span, Cahill has struck out 25 while allowing 30 hits and 15 walks. Cahill is 3-0 with a 1.75 ERA in four home starts this season, compared to 3-2 with a 4.29 ERA in six road outings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has struggled in his last two starts, losing to the Giants and Cubs on the road. In those 10 1/3 innings, the 24-year-old southpaw has allowed 10 earned runs on 14 hits and seven walks to raise his season ERA from 3.58 to 4.21. Gonzalez has been especially tough on left-handed batters this season, limiting them to a .138 average. Righties, meanwhile, are batting .274 against Gonzalez. He has fared much better at home this season, going 4-2 with a 2.90 ERA at the Oakland Coliseum.
away_pitcher_note: It took more than two months, but Leake finally took the loss in a start last Wednesday. The rookie pitcher started 12 games before his first career loss until a five-run, six-inning performances against the Dodgers saw him drop a 6-2 game to Clayton Kershaw. Five runs are the most Leake has allowed in a start, and two of the three times he's done it are in his last two starts. In the five starts before the last two, Leake had given up a combined four earned runs. Leake didn't pitch in the Reds' series with the Indians and Royals, so Monday will be his first career appearance in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Braden is still searching for an elusive victory since tossing baseball's 19th perfect game on May 9 against the Rays. In the seven starts since, Braden is 0-4 with a 4.29 ERA. Braden has experienced tightness in his throwing arm in his past two starts, stemming from inflammation of the flexor tendon in his elbow. Pitching on seven days rest at Wrigley Field on Thursday, Braden went six innings, allowing an earned run on five hits and a walk while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo did it all last time out against the Dodgers, as he allowed just one run in seven innings to earn a win and also belted a three-run home run off John Ely in the second inning. Arroyo has lost just one start since April 23, going 6-1 in a 10-game span. He's pitched at least seven innings in his last three starts and seven times in the last 10, helping give rest to a bullpen that's been inconsistent and lacking in depth. Despite the 7-1 win on Thursday, Arroyo chalked much of his performance up to luck, as he got away with walking a season-high six batters.

home_pitcher_note: Since becoming a part of the A's rotation, Mazzaro has gone 1-1 with a 4.50 ERA in three starts. Against the Cardinals on Saturday, the 23-year-old righty finished five innings, allowing four earned runs on six hits and three walks. He tossed a season-high 92 pitches while striking out a season-high five. Righties are batting .333 off Mazzaro this season, while left-handers are hitting .283. Mazzaro has limited opponents to a .240 batting average at home this season, compared to .368 average on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto lost Friday at Seattle, and although he threw 115 pitches in 5 2/3 innings, he was also the victim of a complete game shutout by Cliff Lee in a 1-0 Reds loss. Cueto had not dropped a decision since April 24 against the Padres and was 6-0 in his previous nine starts. He'll try to get back in the win column against an Oakland team he's never faced before. Only two A's batters have ever faced Cueto. Cueto has pitched fairly well in Interleague Play, as he's 4-3 with a 3.68 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets has struggled since the calendar turned to June, losing all four of his starts in the month. In his latest outing on Saturday in St. Louis, Sheets gave up four earned runs on four walks and six hits while striking out two over seven innings. He hasn't earned a victory since defeating Tampa Bay on May 8. Like the rest of his teammates, Sheets has fared much better at home this season. He's 2-2 with a 2.79 ERA in seven home starts in 2010, compared to 0-5 with a 6.95 ERA in eight road outings. In 22 career starts against the Pirates, the 31-year-old righty is 8-8 with a 2.92 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln will get a fourth crack at his first Major League win in this start. He hasn't had a terrific outing yet, but he's had three suitable ones. Lincoln has pitched six innings in all of his starts since being called up, and he did so last time after enduring a 32-pitch first. Lincoln's fastball command was a bit shaky against the Indians on Sunday, but he is showing more aggressiveness, perhaps a sign that he's not giving hitters too much credit anymore. The key now for Lincoln is to be able to preserve leads when they're given to him. This will be Lincoln's first career appearance against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander is making his case to become an All-Star in his second big league season. Cahill has won his last five decisions and hasn't lost since May 16 against the Angels. His 3.21 ERA is the lowest among current A's starters. In his last outing on Sunday in St. Louis, Cahill went six innings, allowing two earned runs on four hits. He struck out seven batters to set a new season high and tie his career high. Sunday's start marked the second time all season that he hadn't walked a batter. Cahill is 3-0 with a 1.75 ERA in four home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: His 2010 line with the Pirates isn't pretty -- 0-2, 13.50 ERA in three starts and four appearances -- but there's a belief he's improved lately in Indianapolis. He's 4-5 with a 3.86 ERA in 10 starts at Triple-A, and even though his last start on June 21 was a loss, he still went seven innings and allowed two earned runs. McCutchen has never pitched in an interleague game. His last appearance with the Pirates was one inning of scoreless relief April 24. He was optioned to Triple-A the next day.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez threw a gem in his latest start against the Reds in Oakland on Monday, but the bullpen faltered down the stretch in a 6-4 loss. Gonzalez threw seven innings, allowing an unearned run on four hits and a walk while striking out a season-high nine. Gonzalez said they key to his success was trusting his curveball and changeup, which he threw for strikes all night. In seven home starts this season, Gonzalez is 4-2 with a 2.47 ERA. Gonzalez has been particularly tough on lefties this season, limiting them to a .145 batting average, while righties are hitting .261 off him.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf remains winless through 10 starts this season, largely hurt by one or two big innings per outing. The right-hander continues to feel uncomfortable pitching out of the stretch, which explains why he is having issues closing out innings with runners on base. Opponents are also having remarkable success against him as the game progresses. Ohlendorf has held opponents to a .203 batting average his first time through the order. The second and third times through the order, opponents are batting .341. Ohlendorf has made one previous appearance against Oakland, that coming in 2008. Ohlendorf pitched 1 2/3 innings in relief and allowed one earned run on two hits and three walks.

home_pitcher_note: Matusz's string of four solid starts ended on Wednesday when he allowed six runs in six 6 1/3 innings against the Marlins. He has lost a career-high eight straight decisions. In two career starts against Oakland he is 1-1 with a 7.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Dallas Braden was initially scheduled to start, but was scratched with left elbow stiffness. Mazzaro fills in on short notice.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the season 0-8, Millwood has won his last two starts. The O's exploded for 11 runs to back his five innings and four runs allowed on Thursday against the Marlins. In 17 career starts against Oakland, Millwood is 6-4 with a 3.44 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Vin Mazzaro was originally scheduled to start Wednesday, but A's manager Bob Geren will skip the 23-year-old right-hander because of Monday's off-day. Sheets picked up his first win in nearly seven weeks on Friday, striking out a season-high nine over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta has struggled after starting his career with wins over the Yankees and Giants. In a June 20 loss in San Diego, he blew a chance to become the first Oriole to win his first three career starts, and on Friday against the Nationals he gave up five runs in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander is looking like a solid All-Star candidate. Over his past eight starts, Cahill is 6-0 with a 2.24 ERA. On Saturday against the Pirates, he threw 7 2/3 shutout innings, allowing two hits and three walks while striking out a career-high 10.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot collected his team-leading eighth victory on Sunday in Cincinnati, limiting the Reds to one run on three hits over seven innings. He walked three and struck out five. The rookie has yielded two or fewer earned runs in five of his past seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez struggled with his control in his latest start on Sunday against the Pirates, walking four batters over six-plus innings en route to getting a no-decision. Gonzalez faced the Indians on April 25, shutting out Cleveland over seven innings in an 11-0 win.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook tossed six-plus innings of one-run ball against the Blue Jays on Monday night to collect his fifth victory. The 32-year-old right-hander scattered six hits and one walk with four strikeouts in the 105-pitch outing. He is 5-2 with a 4.18 ERA in 10 starts since May 11.
away_pitcher_note: Mortensen will make his season debut with the A's in place of the injured Dallas Braden, who is battling elbow tendinitis. In 15 starts with Triple-A Sacramento this year, the right-hander posted a 10-2 record with a 3.58 ERA and 77 strikeouts, compared to just 31 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona rebounded from his worst start of the season to toss his 12th quality start against the Jays on Tuesday. He went 6 1/3 innings, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits with three walks and two strikeouts. He's induced 15 groundball double plays this season.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro made an emergency start in place of Dallas Braden (elbow) on Tuesday, allowing an earned run on three hits and six walks over six innings for the win. He is now 2-2 with a 3.41 ERA in his last five starts since filling in for an injured Brett Anderson.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets left with a 6-3 lead in a bizzare game at Baltimore on Wednesday, but got the no-decision after giving up four runs (three earned) over six innings in a 9-6 loss. He has completed at least six innings in each of his last 11 starts, going 2-4 with a 4.04 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez is looking for his first win since June 12, coming off a 7-0 loss to the Mariners on June 30 in which he allowed three runs in six innings. Vazquez beat the A's on April 20 in Oakland for his first win.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander is 7-0 with a 2.12 ERA in his last nine starts, holding batters to a .194 average in that span. On Thursday at Baltimore, he threw 95 pitches over seven innings, allowing one run on four hits and a walk while striking out four.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia is looking for his seventh consecutive winning start, taking on the A's at a stadium where he attended games growing up. Sabathia beat the Mariners with eight innings of two-run ball on July 1. He's 6-0 with a 2.00 ERA in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Despite battling with his command on Friday, Gonzalez threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings during a 3-0 win over the Orioles, allowing five hits while striking out five. He has walked four batters in each of his last two starts and in four of his last seven outings.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett ended a string of five losing starts with a no-decision vs. Toronto on Friday, hurling 6 2/3 scoreless frames and leaving in line for the win. Burnett said he felt mentally prepared for that start after going 0-5 with an an 11.35 ERA in June.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro earned his second win in as many starts on Sunday at Cleveland. The 22-year-old righty tossed 7 1/3 innings, allowing an earned run on seven hits and a walk while striking out seven. Mazzaro threw a career-high 111 pitches, but said he wanted to continue pitching.
away_pitcher_note: With wins in his past six starts and a 2.08 ERA across 43 1/3 innings, Pineiro has emerged as the club's No. 2 starter behind ace Jered Weaver. He has issued only 12 walks in those six games, consistently keeping the ball down in the zone and getting groundouts.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets allowed three earned runs over a season-high 7 1/3 innings on Monday, but lost in a 3-1 contest to the Yankees. Sheets said he finally feels like he has his stamina back, after missing all of last year while recovering from elbow surgery.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir had another frustrating outing in Chicago on Monday, getting hurt late by the long ball after bringing his elusive slider back into his repertoire with his fastball and changeup and controlling the White Sox. To get deeper in games, he needs the slider to bite.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill won't be able to pitch in the All-Star Game on Tuesday because of this start. Against the Yankees on Tuesday, Cahill served up two homers to Alex Rodriguez -- including a grand slam -- en route to giving up six earned runs over six innings in a 6-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Wrapping up a brilliant first half, Weaver had a solid effort in Chicago on Tuesday night before a stray fastball and changeup resulted in homers by Alex Rios and Andruw Jones that were his undoing. Weaver's six strikeouts give him 130 in 115 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke was scratched from Sunday's game at Chicago because of some discomfort behind his right shoulder, not believed to be serious. So he'll have nine days of rest between starts as he goes for his fifth winning decision in a row.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old has struggled with his command lately, walking 13 batters combined over his past three starts, a span of 16 2/3 innings. Gonzalez gave up five earned runs on eight hits and five walks over four innings against the Yankees in a 6-2 loss on July 7.

home_pitcher_note: Chen was pulled in the fourth inning of his last start at Chicago because his fastball lacked life, presumably due to a pre-start bout with strep throat. That came right after a sensational start at Anaheim in which he retired the first 16 batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill couldn't pitch in Tuesday's All-Star game because he pitched on Sunday, when he allowed an unearned run on five hits and two walks over seven innings in a 5-2 win over the Angels. Cahill has become the de facto ace of the A's staff without the injured Brett Anderson.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister has such a dazzling daytime record (21-8) that he was slotted for this first afternoon start following the break. He's 4-0 with a 2.37 ERA in six daytime starts. After reeling off five straight wins through June 6, Bannister is 1-4 in his last five decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro is the lesser known commodity of Oakland's promising young staff, but has looked very efficient lately. Over his last four starts, the 23-year-old is 2-1 with a 2.30 ERA and has finished at least seven innings in three of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Though it took him three months, Sheets said he finally feels like he has his usual stamina back after missing all of last season recovering from elbow surgery. Trade rumors continue to swirl around the veteran, who is 2-1 with a 3.55 ERA over his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Japanese righty battled some familiar obstacles in the first half -- health and consistency. Matsuzaka is coming off a solid start in which he gave up six hits and two runs over six innings in a win over the Blue Jays, walking none and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Braden (elbow) will make his first start since returning from the 15-day disabled list. Braden pitched for Class A Stockton on Thursday, giving up three earned runs on seven hits over four-plus innings. He left the game after giving up back-to-back homers.
away_pitcher_note: In one of his worst starts of the year Thursday, Tim Wakefield gave up eight hits and six earned runs in two innings. All six runs came in the first inning after the Texas Rangers strung six hits together, capped off by a Bengie Molina two-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Gonzalez did exactly what he intended to do: limit walks and pound the strike zone. Gonzalez lasted seven innings, allowing only one run on seven hits with three strikeouts and only one walk en route to his eighth victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Placed on the disabled list July 5 after straining his left hamstring while running the bases in San Francisco on June 26, Buchholz will make his return to the rotation against the A's. Before his trip to the DL, Buchholz's numbers earned him an All-Star nod.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill gave up five earned runs Saturday -- all coming in the second inning -- as he lasted 6 2/3 innings with four walks and three strikeouts. To Cahill's credit, after that inning, he retired the next 16 straight batters as the A's won, 6-5.
away_pitcher_note: No team has handled the White Sox ace like Oakland, during the length of his stellar decade-long career. The A's have a 12-3 mark against Buehrle, who has worked seven innings in each of his past three starts, and are 6-0 in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Mazzaro threw a career-high 7 2/3 innings in his last start against Kansas City as he picked up his fifth win of the season in a 9-6 victory, which completed a series sweep of the Royals. He allowed only one run with a walk and five strikeouts on the day.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia should have recorded his 10th victory overall in Minnesota, if not for Bobby Jenks' blown save and the Twins' four-run rally in the ninth. Garcia has a 7-1 record after White Sox losses and has made 13 quality starts out of 17.

home_pitcher_note: Braden finished 4 2/3 innings on Tuesday against the Red Sox, allowing four runs (one earned) on 10 hits, in his first start since returning from the 15-day DL with elbow stiffness. Braden is the first pitcher to go winless in nine starts after throwing a perfect game.
away_pitcher_note: Did Hudson's stellar effort in Monday's win over the Mariners earn him a rotation spot or raise his profile as a potential part in a Ken Williams' trade package? For now, Hudson's six strikeouts and one earned run allowed over 6 2/3 innings get him this start vs. Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Lee picked up his first win as a Ranger in his last start, vs. the Angels, tossing 8 1/3 frames while yielding two runs on five hits. He's pitched into the eighth in seven straight starts, the first to do that since Toronto's Pat Hentgen in 1996.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez is 3-1 with a 3.80 ERA in his last four starts. Against the Red Sox on Wednesday, Gonzalez earned the win after allowing four runs over six innings in a 6-4 A's win. He struggled in his lone start at Texas this season, allowing four runs over four frames on May 12.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Tigers, Lewis took the loss after giving up four runs on nine hits with five strikeouts. He's made two starts against the A's this season, compiling an 0-1 record with a 4.15 ERA. He's given up six runs in 13 innings while striking out 11.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill was outdueled by Mark Buehrle in his latest start on Friday. Cahill was pinned with the loss, after giving up three runs (two earned) over seven innings in a 5-1 defeat. Cahill earned a no-decision at Texas on May 11, when he gave up two runs over 5 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson pitched arguably his best game of the season Friday, holding the Angels scoreless over eight innings while not walking a batter. In his only start against the A's this season, Wilson earned the no-decision after allowing only one run in seven innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: The young righty has proved himself to be a legit big league pitcher lately. Over his last five starts, Mazzaro is 4-0 with a 2.12 ERA and a .202 batting average against. He picked up the decision in Saturday's 10-2 win vs. the White Sox, tossing six innings of two-run ball.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell is making his Major League debut on Friday against the A's. He was thrust into the start because the White Sox traded Daniel Hudson. He figures to be up for this one start before ceding his spot to Edwin Jackson.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson threw a successful 40-pitch side session on Wednesday, enabling the A's to activate him from the disabled list on Friday. It will be Anderson's first start since June 3, when he went down for the second time with elbow tendinitis.

home_pitcher_note: Danks was masterful yet again in his last start. This time, he outdueled Mariners ace Felix Hernandez, going eight innings and giving up one run. He tried to lobby manager Ozzie Guillen to pitch the ninth, but to no avail.
away_pitcher_note: Braden finally got the monkey off his back on Sunday, as he allowed three runs over 6 1/3 innings to earn the win in a 6-4 victory over the White Sox. It was the first victory in 10 tries for Braden following his perfect game on May 9.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd pitched seven innings of shutout baseball in his last start, part of a 11-0 romp of the Mariners. He has been one of the best pitchers in baseball over his last 10 starts, giving up no more than two earned runs in any of them.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez held his own in his last start, allowing one run over six innings, but was outdueled by Cliff Lee in a 3-1 extra-innings loss to the Rangers on Tuesday. Over his last seven starts, the southpaw is 3-1 with a 2.53 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old All-Star turned in one of his best performances of the year Wednesday, shutting out the Rangers on two hits over eight innings in a 3-1 win. His .196 opponents batting average is one of the lowest figures in the Major Leagues.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister is looking to stop the bleeding as he kicks off a three-game series in Oakland. He picked up his fifth straight loss Wednesday when he allowed five earned runs on 11 hits with a walk and four strikeouts in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: After a string of strong performances, Mazzaro was tagged for seven earned runs on 12 hits and a walk over 5 1/3 innings at Texas in a 7-4 loss on Thursday. Mazzaro beat the Royals on July 18, throwing 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Davies took the no-decision for the fourth time in his last five starts. Davies lasted 5 2/3 innings, allowing three earned runs on six hits with four walks, three strikeouts and a homer as the Royals lost in extras.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson struggled in his return from the 15-day disabled list on Friday, allowing five earned runs on 10 hits over 5 1/3 innings in a 6-1 loss to the White Sox. Anderson threw 91 pitches, 55 for strikes, and didn't experience any setbacks.
